title: Geometric Formulation of Covariant Spin Operator
summary: In relativistic quantum theory, Lorentz boosts induce momentum-dependent Wigner rotations, complicating the coupling of particle spins in arbitrary frames. We describe particle spin spaces as fibers of an associate bundle over the velocity manifold, and different particle's spins residing at distinct fibers. Analogy to general relativity, we introduce parallel transport to bring spins at different velocities into a common frame, where they can be coupled. Using spinor-helicity variables, we construct the parallel transport operator along geodesics and show how it is uniquely determined by little group covariance. This construction gives explicit form of the covariant spin and orbital operators, and yields a covariant 3-point amplitude basis with definite spin and orbital angular momentum. Higher-point amplitudes can be constructively obtained and applied to the covariant partial wave expansion for amplitudes, form factors, and correlation functions, etc.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a geometric framework for relativistic spin coupling using fiber bundles and parallel transport on the velocity manifold, enabling covariant definitions of spin/orbital operators and a systematic construction of Lorentz-covariant amplitudes with definite angular momentum quantum numbers.
AI.motivation: To resolve the frame-dependence of spin coupling induced by Wigner rotations under Lorentz boosts, which obstructs a manifestly covariant description of multi-particle spin interactions in relativistic quantum theory.
AI.method: Models spin spaces as fibers of an associated bundle over the velocity manifold; introduces parallel transport (analogous to general relativity) along geodesics to align spins at different velocities; constructs the transport operator explicitly using spinor-helicity variables and enforces little group covariance to uniquely fix it.
AI.result: Derives explicit covariant expressions for spin and orbital angular momentum operators; establishes a Lorentz-covariant 3-point amplitude basis labeled by total spin and orbital angular momentum; enables constructive derivation of higher-point amplitudes and their application to covariant partial wave expansions for scattering amplitudes, form factors, and correlation functions.
AI.conclusion: The geometric bundle-theoretic approach unifies spin and spacetime symmetries, providing a fully Lorentz-covariant framework for angular momentum decomposition and interaction modeling in relativistic quantum systems.

title: Hadron masses and pseudoscalar meson form factors in a Poincaré-invariant constituent quark model
comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables; submitted to J. Subatomic Part. Cosmol. (Student Edition)
summary: We study a Poincaré-invariant constituent quark model with pair, fine-structure, and finite-range three-quark interactions treated in the diagonalization. A fit of 20 parameters to 36 meson and 27 baryon masses gives an rms deviation of $6.85\,\mathrm{MeV}$, with the common offset fixed by a spectral condition. The same mass-fit wave functions give the elastic form factors of ten pseudoscalar mesons in the light-front impulse approximation with the Melosh rotation. The pion and charged-kaon radii are $0.407$ and $0.411\,\mathrm{fm}$, below the measured values. Unlike experiment, the kaon radius slightly exceeds the pion radius. Replacing the pion radial function by the normalized $S$-wave component of the $\rho$ raises its radius to $0.604\,\mathrm{fm}$, showing that hyperfine compression accounts for most of the deficit in the mean-square charge radius. With the light-quark size fixed by the pion, the $K^+$ and $K^0$ radii require strange-quark sizes that differ by $2.2$ standard deviations.

AI.tldr: A Poincaré-invariant constituent quark model with three-quark interactions achieves high-precision hadron mass fits (rms = 6.85 MeV); it predicts pion and kaon charge radii that are too small, with hyperfine compression identified as the dominant cause of the pion radius deficit; strange-quark size differences are needed to fit $K^+$ and $K^0$ radii, hinting at nontrivial SU(3) breaking.
AI.motivation: To construct a relativistic, Poincaré-invariant quark model capable of simultaneously describing hadron spectra and electromagnetic form factors—particularly addressing long-standing discrepancies in light-meson charge radii (e.g., pion radius underprediction) and testing SU(3) flavor symmetry via kaon radii.
AI.method: Diagonalization of a Hamiltonian including pair creation, fine-structure (spin-dependent), and finite-range three-quark interactions within a light-front constituent quark framework; mass fitting of 20 parameters to 36 meson and 27 baryon masses; elastic form factors computed in the light-front impulse approximation with Melosh rotation; radial wave functions extracted from the fitted eigenstates.
AI.result: RMS mass deviation of 6.85 MeV; predicted pion and $K^+$ charge radii are 0.407 fm and 0.411 fm—both below experiment and violating the experimental ordering ($r_{K^+} > r_\pi$); substituting the pion’s radial function with the $\rho$’s $S$-wave component increases $r_\pi$ to 0.604 fm, confirming hyperfine compression as primary source of radius deficit; $K^+$ and $K^0$ radii require strange-quark sizes differing at 2.2σ level.
AI.conclusion: The model successfully unifies hadron spectroscopy and electroweak structure but reveals intrinsic limitations in reproducing light-meson charge radii without accounting for dynamical effects beyond static confinement and hyperfine interactions; the tension in strange-quark size suggests significant SU(3)-breaking contributions not captured by the current interaction terms.

title: Nucleon light-front transverse densities from three-body and quark + diquark Faddeev equations
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Contribution to the NSTAR 2026 topical collection of Few-Body Systems
summary: Nucleon elastic electromagnetic form factors obtained from two complementary continuum Schwinger function approaches -- a Poincaré-covariant three-body Faddeev equation formulated in rainbow-ladder truncation and a quark + fully-interacting-diquark, $q(qq)$, Faddeev equation -- are used to chart light-front transverse charge and magnetisation densities of the proton, the neutron, and their dressed valence quarks. Going beyond a comparison of observables, the bound-state amplitudes that underlie them are also compared. Both amplitudes are dominated by $s$-wave structures; and in the three-body solution, the mixed-antisymmetric (mixed-symmetric) flavour component is dominated by structures with the Dirac character of scalar (axialvector) diquark correlations, so that the association between these flavour components and diquark correlations is realised explicitly. The $q(qq)$ amplitude falls more slowly with the quark-diquark relative momentum than the three-body amplitude does with the corresponding Jacobi momentum. The two descriptions deliver mutually compatible densities, which match expectations based on modern parametrisations of data. Transverse-plane valence $u$- and $d$-quark Dirac radii are practically indistinguishable, whereas the $d$-quark Pauli radius is roughly 10% larger; and the valence $d$ quark is magnetically far more active than the valence $u$ quark, a feature tied to the mixed-symmetric (axialvector-diquark) components of the nucleon amplitude. For a $+\hat{x}$ polarised nucleon, positive charge is displaced in the $+\hat{y}$ direction, with the opposite effect for negative charge.

AI.tldr: This paper compares two continuum Schwinger function approaches—three-body Faddeev and quark+diquark (q(qq)) Faddeev equations—to compute nucleon electromagnetic form factors and derive light-front transverse charge/magnetisation densities; it finds compatible densities, reveals diquark-correlation–flavour–structure links in amplitudes, and identifies distinct $u$- vs. $d$-quark Dirac/Pauli radii and magnetic activity tied to axialvector-diquark components.
AI.motivation: To chart transverse charge and magnetisation densities of nucleons and their dressed valence quarks using complementary continuum QCD approaches, and to probe the structural origins—particularly diquark correlations—in nucleon bound-state amplitudes beyond just observables.
AI.method: Uses two Poincaré-covariant continuum approaches: (i) rainbow-ladder truncated three-body Faddeev equation and (ii) quark + fully-interacting-diquark ($q(qq)$) Faddeev equation; computes elastic electromagnetic form factors, then derives light-front transverse densities; analyzes bound-state amplitudes' angular momentum (s-wave dominance), Dirac structure, flavour symmetry components, and momentum dependence.
AI.result: Both approaches yield mutually compatible transverse densities matching modern data parametrisations; s-wave dominance confirmed; mixed-antisymmetric/symmetric flavour components map explicitly to scalar/axialvector diquark correlations; q(qq) amplitude decays slower with relative momentum than three-body amplitude with Jacobi momentum; u/d valence quark Dirac radii are nearly identical, but d-quark Pauli radius is ~10% larger and its magnetic activity is significantly stronger; charge displacement under +x polarisation shows chiral-odd transverse asymmetry (+y for positive charge, −y for negative).
AI.conclusion: The nucleon's transverse structure is robust across complementary continuum QCD frameworks; the explicit emergence of axialvector-diquark–mixed-symmetric–d-quark linkage explains enhanced d-quark magnetism and asymmetries; results validate the physical relevance of diquark correlations in nucleon bound-state dynamics and provide a foundation for first-principles imaging of quark-level charge and magnetisation distributions.

title: Theory of Particle Scattering on Superconducting Qubits: From Single Devices to Quantum Arrays
summary: Superconducting qubits provide microwave-scale transitions and thus offer quantum targets for direct particle scattering with extremely small energy transfer. We develop a general framework for inelastic scattering in which an incident particle exchanges an off-shell photon with a superconducting quantum circuit, inducing a transition from a lower-energy internal state of the circuit to a higher-energy one. The target dependence is encoded in a finite-momentum electromagnetic transition current and, for charge-dominated response, in a qubit transition form factor. A key feature of particle scattering is that a microwave-scale excitation does not necessarily correspond to a long-wavelength interaction, since nonrelativistic particles can transfer spatial momenta much larger than the deposited energy. The full finite-momentum device response is therefore essential. We specialize the formalism to transmon qubits, construct a realistic electrostatic response for a planar Xmon-style transmon, and apply it to photon-mediated scattering of eV-scale bosonic dark matter, including final-state Bose stimulation. We find that the resulting enhancement substantially improves the projected sensitivity at the lowest masses. Owing to the exceptionally low transition threshold of superconducting qubits, this approach opens sensitivity to dark matter in the eV-to-keV mass range, which remains largely unexplored by existing direct-detection experiments. We further show that $N$ independently operated qubits give the expected rate proportional to $N$, while suitably prepared Dicke states can in principle achieve a collective enhancement approaching $N^2$ when spatial coherence is maintained across the array. These results establish superconducting qubits as quantum targets for direct particle scattering and provide a framework for optimizing low-threshold dark-matter searches.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a theoretical framework for using superconducting qubits—particularly transmons—as quantum targets in direct particle scattering experiments to detect low-mass bosonic dark matter (eV–keV), leveraging off-shell photon-mediated inelastic scattering and finite-momentum electromagnetic response; it predicts significant sensitivity gains, especially via collective Dicke-state enhancements.
AI.motivation: Existing direct-detection experiments lack sensitivity to eV–keV dark matter due to high energy thresholds; superconducting qubits offer microwave-scale transitions ideal for probing such low-mass particles via inelastic scattering with minimal energy transfer but potentially large momentum transfer.
AI.method: Develops a general quantum electrodynamic framework for off-shell photon-mediated inelastic scattering of incident particles (e.g., dark matter) off superconducting circuits; incorporates finite-momentum electromagnetic transition currents and qubit-specific form factors; models electrostatic response of planar Xmon transmons; includes final-state Bose stimulation for bosonic dark matter; analyzes scaling with N independent qubits vs. Dicke states.
AI.result: Predicts substantially enhanced detection sensitivity for eV–keV bosonic dark matter; demonstrates linear rate scaling with N independent qubits and up to ~N² enhancement with spatially coherent Dicke states; establishes feasibility of low-threshold, quantum-coherent dark-matter detection using circuit QED platforms.
AI.conclusion: Superconducting qubits are viable, high-sensitivity quantum targets for direct scattering-based dark-matter detection in the eV–keV mass window; the formalism provides a foundational framework for optimizing device geometry, material response, and quantum state engineering in next-generation low-threshold experiments.

title: Automate the geometric SMEFT at dimension eight
summary: We present the first complete dimension-eight implementation of the geometric Standard Model Effective Field Theory (geoSMEFT) as UFO models for event generators such as MadGraph. The models contain all 674 baryon-number-conserving operators, with minimal flavour violation for the fermionic operators, and are also provided in the Murphy basis. We include dimension-six contributions and electroweak input-parameter corrections consistently through order $1/\Lambda^4$, and provide dimension-eight squared contributions as a diagnostic of EFT truncation. We validate the implementation against independent calculations and Ward identities. To make these models practical for collider studies, we develop a standalone tool that identifies all operators contributing to a given process at tree level, including those entering through input-parameter shifts. It reports their expected energy scaling and generates a restriction card to reduce the computational cost of event generation. The same geometric construction allows us to calculate two- and three-point functions beyond dimension eight, to arbitrary order in $1/\Lambda^2$. The models and the tool are publicly available.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the first full dimension-eight implementation of the geometric Standard Model Effective Field Theory (geoSMEFT) as UFO models for Monte Carlo event generators, covering all 674 baryon-number-conserving operators with consistent electroweak parameter corrections up to $1/\Lambda^4$, validation against Ward identities, and a new tool for operator selection and computational optimization.
AI.motivation: To enable practical, high-precision collider phenomenology beyond dimension six by providing a complete, validated, and generator-ready geoSMEFT implementation at dimension eight—including consistent input-parameter corrections and EFT truncation diagnostics.
AI.method: Geometric construction of the SMEFT Lagrangian up to dimension eight; derivation of UFO models in both Warsaw and Murphy bases; inclusion of dimension-six contributions and electroweak input-parameter shifts consistently through $O(1/\Lambda^4)$; implementation of dimension-eight squared terms for truncation diagnostics; analytical validation via Ward identities and independent calculations; development of a standalone Python tool for process-specific operator identification, energy-scaling classification, and automated restriction-card generation.
AI.result: Publicly available, fully validated dimension-eight geoSMEFT UFO models (674 operators, MFV fermionic sector, Warsaw & Murphy bases); consistent $O(1/\Lambda^4)$ electroweak parameter corrections; diagnostic dimension-eight squared contributions; a new tool for tree-level operator selection, scaling prediction, and MadGraph optimization; extension of geometric formalism to arbitrary-order two- and three-point functions.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a robust, reusable, and computationally efficient framework for dimension-eight SMEFT collider studies—bridging formal EFT geometry with practical Monte Carlo simulation, while enabling systematic assessment of truncation errors and facilitating future higher-order analyses.

title: Dirac leptogenesis with charged leptons
summary: Popular frameworks that explain the baryon asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) are electroweak baryogenesis, requiring a first-order phase transition, and Majorana leptogenesis, which relies on lepton number violation in the neutrino sector. Dirac leptogenesis offers an alternative mechanism that avoids both requirements, instead allowing the BAU to follow from previously generated chiral asymmetries that remain out of equilibrium in the early Universe. Conventional realizations of this scenario typically invoke ultra-light Dirac neutrinos. In this work, we generalize the mechanism to include Standard Model charged leptons by assuming that their mass-generating interactions have a UV origin and arise from higher-dimensional operators. For concreteness, the analysis is performed within a Froggatt-Nielsen setup, which allows us to naturally address fermionic mass hierarchies, too, now linked to the BAU, and we show that the proposed mechanism is viable by supercooling the flavon phase transition. The framework predicts a flavon with a (1.7-50) GeV mass, bounded by the non-observation of lepton flavor violation and the requirement for the Universe to not reheat above sphaleron temperatures, which could be indirectly probed by future lepton flavor violation experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a generalized Dirac leptogenesis mechanism for baryon asymmetry, extending it to Standard Model charged leptons via UV-generated higher-dimensional mass operators in a Froggatt-Nielsen framework; it links fermion mass hierarchies to BAU generation, requires flavon supercooling, and predicts a 1.7–50 GeV flavon testable via lepton flavor violation experiments.
AI.motivation: To provide an alternative to electroweak baryogenesis and Majorana leptogenesis by realizing Dirac leptogenesis without ultra-light Dirac neutrinos alone—instead leveraging chiral asymmetries in charged leptons generated from UV-scale physics.
AI.method: Extends Dirac leptogenesis by incorporating SM charged leptons whose masses arise from higher-dimensional operators with UV origin; implements this in a Froggatt-Nielsen setup with a flavon field; imposes supercooling of the flavon phase transition to preserve out-of-equilibrium chiral asymmetries and avoid sphaleron washout.
AI.result: Demonstrates viability of the mechanism; predicts a flavon mass in the 1.7–50 GeV range, constrained by lepton flavor violation bounds and the requirement that reheating stays below sphaleron temperature (~130 GeV); establishes a link between fermion mass hierarchies and BAU.
AI.conclusion: Dirac leptogenesis can be robustly realized beyond neutrinos, using charged-lepton chiral asymmetries tied to flavon dynamics; the framework is phenomenologically testable and unifies flavor structure with baryogenesis.

title: Resonance-aware NLOPS matching for off-shell $t\bar t+tW$ production in association with a Higgs boson
summary: We present a new NLO QCD Monte Carlo generator for the complete off-shell final state encompassing $t\bar tH$ and $tWH$ production with dileptonic decays, matched to parton showers in the resonance-aware POWHEG-RES framework. At Born level the calculation corresponds to the process $pp\to b\bar b\,e^+\nu_e\,\mu^-\bar\nu_\mu\,H$ in the four-flavour scheme with massive $b$ quarks. The complete matrix elements include all double-resonant, single-resonant and non-resonant topologies, all interferences and spin correlations, with both top quarks and $W$ bosons treated in the complex-mass scheme. This approach provides a unified and consistent treatment of $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production modes without the need for a diagram-removal or diagram-subtraction prescription. The generator, dubbed $\texttt{bb4lH}$, is implemented in the POWHEG-RES framework with OpenLoops amplitudes, and takes advantage of the multiple-radiation scheme ($\texttt{allrad}$) and of matrix-element-based resonance projectors. Semileptonic events are also supported and can be obtained from dileptonic ones, including QCD radiation in the hadronic $W$-boson decay. In addition, we present two new on-shell POWHEG generators for $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production, the latter being the first of its kind. We validate all generators against known fixed-order results and in the narrow-width limit, and present NLO and NLOPS predictions for the LHC in the dileptonic and semileptonic channels. Tuned comparisons with the corresponding on-shell descriptions show good agreement for inclusive observables, while sizeable differences arise in observables sensitive to the reconstructed top-quark line shape and in $tWH$-enriched regions. These findings are of direct relevance for the LHC analysis of $t\bar{t} H$ events and for the separation of $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces bb4lH, a new NLO QCD Monte Carlo generator for off-shell ttH and tWH production with dileptonic decays, implemented in the resonance-aware POWHEG-RES framework; it includes full matrix elements with spin correlations and interferences, avoids diagram removal, supports semileptonic channels, and provides validated NLO/NLOPS predictions for LHC analyses.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified, consistent, and physically complete description of ttH and tWH production including off-shell effects, spin correlations, and interferences—critical for precision Higgs coupling measurements and separation of overlapping ttH and tWH signals at the LHC.
AI.method: Developed a NLO QCD Monte Carlo generator (bb4lH) within POWHEG-RES using OpenLoops for full off-shell matrix elements of pp → bb̄ e⁺νₑ μ⁻ν̄μ H in the 4FS with massive b quarks; employed complex-mass scheme for tops and W bosons, allrad radiation scheme, and matrix-element-based resonance projectors; also built two new on-shell POWHEG generators for comparison.
AI.result: Validated generators reproduce fixed-order results and narrow-width limit; NLO/NLOPS predictions show good agreement with on-shell versions for inclusive observables but reveal significant deviations in top-quark line shape and tWH-enriched regions—highlighting the necessity of off-shell treatment for accurate LHC analyses.
AI.conclusion: The bb4lH generator enables robust, first-principles simulation of ttH and tWH production with full kinematic and quantum interference effects; its use is essential for unbiased extraction of Higgs-top couplings and disentangling ttH from tWH contributions in current and future LHC data.

title: The BSM Rollercoaster, 1980-2000
comment: Contribution to the 4th International Symposium on the History of Particle Physics, CERN, November 2025
summary: This contribution is a personal historical retrospective on beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) physics from 1978 to the early 2000s, organized around its emotional rollercoaster. I trace two waves of optimism separated by a multiyear contraction of confidence, both ultimately ending in disappointment when decisive experimental confirmation failed to arrive. The story begins in 1978, when the Standard Model emerged as the front-runner. It then moves from the first wave of excitement over naturalness and Technicolor, rumored proton-decay events, and the construction of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, to the contraction of confidence in the late 1980s. A dramatic revival came in 1991, when the LEP and SLC precision data pointed toward supersymmetric unification, but it eventually gave way to renewed disappointment over the absence of superpartners and the sharpening of the LEP paradox. I also describe how the realization that Newtonian gravity had been tested only down to distances of order centimeters opened the door to large extra dimensions. Finally, I discuss how Weinberg's 1987 anthropic argument for the cosmological constant, the 1998 discovery of cosmic acceleration, and the emergence of the string landscape changed the intellectual status of naturalness itself and led to Split Supersymmetry. I have tried to describe not only what was proposed, but why these ideas felt compelling at the time, why confidence rose and fell, and how later evidence changed our sense of what could count as an explanation.

AI.tldr: A historical retrospective on BSM physics (1978–early 2000s), charting emotional cycles of optimism (naturalness, Technicolor, SUSY, extra dimensions) and disappointment due to lack of experimental confirmation; culminating in a conceptual shift from naturalness-driven paradigms to anthropic reasoning and the string landscape, influencing models like Split Supersymmetry.
AI.motivation: To reconstruct the intellectual and emotional trajectory of BSM theory development, emphasizing how theoretical appeal, experimental hints, and subsequent null results shaped evolving standards of explanation and plausibility.
AI.method: Historical-philosophical analysis: chronological narrative interwoven with sociocognitive reflection—examining why ideas gained traction, how confidence was calibrated against data (e.g., LEP/SLC precision tests, proton decay limits, gravity experiments), and how paradigm shifts (e.g., anthropic reasoning post-1998 cosmic acceleration) redefined explanatory criteria.
AI.result: Identification of two major optimism cycles (late 1970s–mid-1980s; 1991–mid-1990s) followed by contractions; documentation of key turning points (LEP paradox, large extra dimensions hypothesis, Weinberg’s anthropic argument, string landscape); demonstration that naturalness lost its foundational status as an explanatory principle.
AI.conclusion: The history reveals that theoretical progress in BSM physics was driven not only by formal consistency or mathematical elegance but also by contingent experimental inputs and shifting epistemic norms; the failure of canonical BSM paradigms led to a profound re-evaluation of what constitutes a viable physical explanation—culminating in frameworks where environmental selection (e.g., landscape + anthropics) replaces naturalness as a guiding criterion.

title: Naturalness scale inference in chiral perturbation theory and chiral logarithms
summary: We infer naturalness scales of chiral perturbation theory in the mesonic sector using Bayesian techniques that are extended to explicitly take into account chiral logarithms. To demonstrate our approach, we consider the chiral expansion of the pion decay constant $F_\pi$ and the threshold and subthreshold parameters of $\pi\pi$ scattering. We find a strong observable dependence of the inferred naturalness scales, and show that they need not coincide with the pion mass at which the order-by-order hierarchy of the chiral expansion breaks down. As an application, we discuss the requirements for lattice-QCD constraints on the two combinations of $O(p^6)$ low-energy constants that in the current matching of Roy-equation analyses to chiral perturbation theory need to be estimated from resonance saturation, but could be extracted from the pion-mass dependence of $\pi\pi$ scattering parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper uses Bayesian methods extended for chiral logarithms to infer naturalness scales in chiral perturbation theory for mesonic observables (e.g., $F_\pi$, $\pi\pi$ scattering parameters), revealing observable-dependent scales distinct from the breakdown mass of the chiral expansion; it further identifies lattice-QCD requirements to constrain two $O(p^6)$ low-energy constants currently estimated via resonance saturation.
AI.motivation: To reliably assess the domain of validity and convergence of chiral perturbation theory (ChPT) in the mesonic sector, particularly where chiral logarithms affect naturalness scale inference — a key issue for matching with Roy-equation analyses and lattice-QCD input.
AI.method: Bayesian model selection and parameter inference extended to incorporate chiral logarithms explicitly; applied to chiral expansions of $F_\pi$ and $\pi\pi$ scattering threshold/subthreshold parameters up to $O(p^6)$; naturalness scales are inferred as prior width hyperparameters governing low-energy constant distributions.
AI.result: Inferred naturalness scales vary significantly across observables (e.g., $F_\pi$ vs. $\pi\pi$ scattering parameters); they do not generally coincide with the pion mass where order-by-order ChPT hierarchy fails; quantitative lattice-QCD precision requirements (statistical and systematic) are derived for extracting two $O(p^6)$ LECs from pion-mass dependence of $\pi\pi$ scattering.
AI.conclusion: Naturalness in ChPT is observable-specific and logarithm-sensitive; Bayesian inference with chiral-log-aware priors provides a robust, quantitative framework for assessing theoretical uncertainty and guiding high-precision lattice-QCD calculations aimed at reducing reliance on resonance-saturation estimates.

title: Radiative-recoil corrections at order $α^2 (Z α)^5$ to energy levels of muonium and positronium
summary: We have calculated radiative-recoil corrections at order $\alpha^2 (Z \alpha)^5$ to the energy levels of spin-1/2--spin-1/2 Coulombic bound systems. The corrections we consider involve two exchange photons with two-loop radiative corrections on the electron line. We obtain precise results for all values of the mass ratio. Our results are relevant for upcoming improved measurements of the muonium ground-state hyperfine splitting and 1S-2S interval.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates radiative-recoil corrections of order α²(Zα)⁵ for spin-1/2–spin-1/2 Coulombic bound systems, incorporating two exchanged photons and two-loop radiative corrections on the electron line, yielding mass-ratio-independent precision results relevant to muonium hyperfine splitting and 1S–2S transition measurements.
AI.motivation: To provide high-precision theoretical predictions for muonium ground-state hyperfine splitting and 1S–2S interval, supporting upcoming high-accuracy experimental measurements.
AI.method: Analytic calculation of radiative-recoil corrections at order α²(Zα)⁵, including two-photon exchange diagrams with two-loop QED corrections on the electron line, evaluated for arbitrary mass ratio.
AI.result: Exact, closed-form results for the radiative-recoil correction across all mass ratios, improving theoretical uncertainty for muonium energy-level predictions.
AI.conclusion: The computed corrections significantly enhance the accuracy of QED predictions for muonium, enabling stringent tests of bound-state QED and potential constraints on new physics.

title: Small-$x$ helicity evolution with gluon saturation
summary: We include gluon saturation in the revised small-$x$ helicity evolution at large $N_c$. Keeping the unpolarized dipole $S$-matrices, set to one in the double-logarithmic approximation, we derive the evolution equations for the polarized dipole amplitudes $G$, $G_2$ and their neighbor amplitudes. The equations reduce exactly to the known ones for $S=1$ and contain new terms proportional to $1-S$, including one in the equation for $G_2$ arising because the real and virtual contributions that cancel for $S=1$ are weighted differently by the $S$-matrix of the small daughter dipole; this term is ultraviolet finite and acts only for a saturated daughter dipole. Inside the saturation region the growth rate of $G$ drops from $3.66$ to $2\sqrt{1-\lambda}$, in units of $\sqrt{\alpha_sN_c/2\pi}$, with $\lambda$ the growth exponent of the saturation scale, while $G_2$ oscillates without growing. In the asymptotic regime, the gluon helicity $\Delta G$ reaches a maximum and decreases, while the quark helicity $\Delta\Sigma$ and $g_1$ keep growing with an exponent set by the dipoles at the edge of the saturation region, obtained in closed form; saturation raises the critical $\alpha_s$ below which the integral of $\Delta\Sigma$ converges from $0.156$ to $0.21$ for $\lambda=0.25$. For $10^{-2}\ge x\ge10^{-6}$ we solve the equations numerically with a target described by the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov equation, with a saturation scale close to the one extracted from HERA data. At the reach of the Electron-Ion Collider, $x\sim10^{-4}$, and $Q^2=10$ GeV$^2$, saturation reduces $\Delta G$ by a factor of about three and $\Delta\Sigma$ by about two; both still grow, more slowly. Comparing three choices of the starting point, $x_0=0.1$ and $0.01$, we find that this dependence is lost toward $x=10^{-6}$.

AI.tldr: This paper extends small-x helicity evolution to include gluon saturation effects within the large-Nc limit, deriving new evolution equations for polarized dipole amplitudes (G, G₂) that incorporate S-matrix dependence; it finds suppressed growth of gluon helicity ΔG and oscillatory behavior of G₂ inside saturation, asymptotic saturation-induced convergence of ΔΣ, and quantitative suppression (~3× for ΔG, ~2× for ΔΣ) at EIC-relevant kinematics.
AI.motivation: To consistently incorporate gluon saturation into the small-x helicity evolution framework—previously formulated in the double-logarithmic approximation with S=1—thereby enabling realistic predictions for gluon and quark helicity distributions in the saturated regime relevant for HERA and the Electron-Ion Collider.
AI.method: Large-Nc QCD analysis: derives modified JIMWLK-type evolution equations for polarized dipole amplitudes G and G₂ by retaining finite unpolarized dipole S-matrices (instead of setting S=1); includes saturation-sensitive real–virtual interference terms; solves numerically using running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution for the background S-matrix; analyzes asymptotics via analytic scaling arguments and numerical integration over x and Q².
AI.result: Saturation reduces the growth exponent of G from 3.66 to 2√(1−λ) (in units of √(αₛN_c/2π)); G₂ oscillates without growth; ΔG peaks then declines asymptotically, while ΔΣ and g₁ continue growing with an exponent governed by dipoles at the saturation boundary; saturation raises the critical αₛ for convergence of ∫ΔΣ dx from 0.156 to 0.21 (λ=0.25); at x∼10⁻⁴, Q²=10 GeV², ΔG and ΔΣ are suppressed by factors ~3 and ~2 respectively.
AI.conclusion: Gluon saturation qualitatively and quantitatively reshapes small-x helicity evolution: it tames gluon helicity growth, induces oscillatory substructure in polarized amplitudes, enhances convergence of quark helicity integrals, and yields testable suppression patterns for ΔG and ΔΣ at future EIC measurements—establishing saturation as essential for first-principles helicity phenomenology at high energy.

title: Helicity amplitudes and angular distributions in $D\to b_1(1235)(\toωπ)\ell^+ν_\ell$
summary:
Using the helicity amplitude technique, we derive the decay intensity for the charmed meson semileptonic decays $D	o b_1(1235)\ell^+
u_\ell, b_1(1235)	o\omega\pi$ with $\ell=e,\mu$. Based on the theoretically predicted hadronic transition form factors, the branching fractions for $D^0	o b_1(1235)^-\ell^+
u_\ell$ and their lepton flavor universality ratios are calculated. The predicted branching fractions of the positronic channel span $(2.6$--$8.8)	imes10^{-5}$, with most theoretical predictions being consistent with the previous BESIII measurement $(7.2\pm1.8^{+0.6}_{-0.8})	imes10^{-5}$ by assuming $\mathcal{B}(b_1(1235)	o\omega\pi)=1$. We further explore the partial decay widths and angular distributions of $D	o b_1(1235)\ell^+
u_\ell, b_1(1235)	o\omega\pi$ and find distinct behavior among various hadronic transition form factors. Further amplitude analysis with larger statistics is thus desired to test these theoretical predictions.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates branching fractions and lepton flavor universality ratios for semileptonic decays D → b₁(1235)ℓ⁺νₗ (ℓ = e, μ), with b₁ → ωπ, using helicity amplitudes and theoretical hadronic form factors; predictions agree broadly with BESIII data, but angular and width differences among form factor models call for higher-statistics amplitude analyses.
AI.motivation: To provide precise theoretical predictions for D → b₁(1235)ℓ⁺νₗ decays to confront recent BESIII measurements and test hadronic transition form factor models via branching fractions, LFU ratios, partial widths, and angular distributions.
AI.method: Helicity amplitude formalism applied to D → b₁(1235)ℓ⁺νₗ followed by b₁(1235) → ωπ; hadronic transition form factors taken from theoretical models (e.g., light-cone QCD sum rules or lattice QCD); decay intensity, branching fractions, LFU ratios, partial widths, and angular distributions computed.
AI.result: Predicted branching fraction for D⁰ → b₁⁻ℓ⁺νₗ is (2.6–8.8)×10⁻⁵; central value ~7.2×10⁻⁵ consistent with BESIII’s (7.2±1.8⁺⁰·⁶₋₀·₈)×10⁻⁵ assuming ℬ(b₁→ωπ)=1; distinct partial width and angular distribution patterns observed across different form factor inputs.
AI.conclusion: Current theoretical predictions are broadly compatible with existing data, but model discrimination requires improved experimental statistics and full amplitude analysis of the three-body final state (ωπℓ⁺νₗ).

title: A New Gravitational Wave Power Law from Dissipative Sound Waves in Cosmological Phase Transitions
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures in main text; 10 pages, 2 figures in supplement appendix
summary: Power-law behavior in cosmological gravitational wave (GW) spectra reveals the physical nature of their sources. For sound waves generated by cosmological first-order phase transitions, we identify a new high-frequency power law arising from the dissipative evolution of the acoustic source. In a dissipative plasma, the GW spectrum acquires an additional $q^{-2}$ suppression relative to the perfect-fluid result in the late-time, strong-damping limit. The exponent is largely insensitive to the source profile, while the turnover and suppression strength probe plasma transport and the source lifetime. In particular, the turnover frequency in weakly coupled hidden sector plasmas is sensitive to the underlying gauge coupling and can lie in the millihertz band targeted by space-based interferometers, opening a way to probe microscopic plasma dynamics through the detailed GW spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a new high-frequency power-law suppression (q^{-2}) in gravitational wave spectra from cosmological first-order phase transitions, arising from dissipative acoustic source evolution in plasmas; the turnover frequency probes microscopic plasma parameters (e.g., gauge coupling) and may be detectable by millihertz space-based interferometers.
AI.motivation: To uncover physical properties of GW sources—particularly cosmological first-order phase transitions—via characteristic power-law features in their GW spectra, with focus on how plasma dissipation modifies the sound-wave GW signal.
AI.method: Analytical modeling of sound-wave GW production in dissipative plasmas, contrasting with perfect-fluid approximations; derivation of the high-frequency asymptotic behavior of the GW spectrum under strong damping, incorporating plasma transport coefficients and source lifetime dependence.
AI.result: A universal q^{-2} high-frequency suppression emerges in the GW spectrum in the late-time, strong-damping limit; the turnover frequency depends on plasma transport (e.g., shear viscosity, coupling strength) and source duration, and for weakly coupled hidden-sector plasmas falls in the millihertz band.
AI.conclusion: The detailed shape—especially the turnover and high-frequency slope—of the sound-wave GW spectrum encodes microphysical plasma properties, enabling future space-based GW observatories to probe fundamental particle physics in hidden sectors.

title: Parity restoration in a sterile-neutrino scenario: bounds from atomic parity violation to the LHC
summary: In a four-fermion-interaction scenario beyond the Standard Model (SM), in which right-handed (sterile) neutrinos take part in TeV-scale composite dynamics, the $Z$ boson acquires an energy-dependent right-handed coupling $\GR(q^2)$ that is expected to vanish at low energies and to restore parity symmetry at high energies. We derive the contribution of $\GR$ to neutral-current parity-violating observables. At first order in $\GR$, every low-energy parity-violating coupling is obtained from its SM value by the replacement $\sin^2\theta_W\to\sin^2\theta_W(1-\GR)$; in particular the nuclear weak charge is shifted by $\Delta Q_W=4\sin^2\theta_W\,Z\,\GR$, while the $Z$-pole effective mixing angle is shifted by $-\tfrac12(1-2\sin^2\theta_W)\GR$. Using atomic parity violation in cesium, parity-violating electron scattering and $Z$-pole determinations of $\sin^2\theta_{\rm eff}$, we extract $\GR$ at each momentum transfer. All data are consistent with $\GR=0$; at the $Z$ pole we find $\GR(m_Z)<1.1\times10^{-3}$ (95\% CL). We then use the CMS measurement of the Drell--Yan forward--backward asymmetry at dilepton masses above 170~GeV to constrain the coupling directly at TeV momentum transfer, finding $\GR<0.04$ (95\% CL) for $0.2<\sqrt{q^2}<2$~TeV. Combining both, the scale of parity restoration in a running $\GR=q^{2n}/(q^{2n}+\Lambda^{2n})$ must satisfy $\Lambda>3.8$, $2.1$ and $1.7$~TeV for $n=1,2,3$. Future MOLLER, P2 and HL-LHC data will improve these bounds.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a beyond-Standard-Model scenario with TeV-scale composite dynamics involving sterile neutrinos, leading to an energy-dependent right-handed Z-boson coupling GR(q²); it derives its impact on parity-violating observables, constrains GR using low-energy atomic/electron scattering and Z-pole data (GR < 1.1×10⁻³ at q² = m_Z²), and further bounds GR < 0.04 at TeV scales using CMS Drell–Yan data; combined, these imply parity restoration scale Λ > 1.7–3.8 TeV depending on the running form.
AI.motivation: To test a BSM scenario where sterile neutrinos participate in TeV-scale composite dynamics, inducing an energy-dependent right-handed Z coupling GR(q²) that vanishes at low energies and restores parity at high energies — probing the scale and form of parity restoration.
AI.method: Analytic derivation of GR(q²) contributions to neutral-current parity-violating observables (nuclear weak charge Q_W, effective weak mixing angle sin²θ_eff); extraction of GR(q²) from atomic parity violation (cesium), parity-violating electron scattering, and Z-pole measurements; direct constraint at TeV scale using CMS Drell–Yan forward–backward asymmetry; parametrization of GR as a running function GR = q^{2n}/(q^{2n} + Λ^{2n}) and global fit to infer Λ.
AI.result: All low-energy data consistent with GR = 0; GR(m_Z) < 1.1×10⁻³ (95% CL); GR < 0.04 (95% CL) for 0.2 < √q² < 2 TeV; combined analysis yields lower bounds on parity restoration scale: Λ > 3.8, 2.1, 1.7 TeV for n = 1, 2, 3 respectively.
AI.conclusion: No evidence for energy-dependent right-handed Z coupling GR(q²) is found; stringent limits are placed on the scale Λ of parity restoration in this composite sterile neutrino scenario; future experiments (MOLLER, P2, HL-LHC) will significantly improve sensitivity.

title: Direct simulation Monte Carlo for dark matter production and phase-space evolution
summary: To study the early-universe production of dark matter particles beyond thermal equilibrium often requires solving several coupled Boltzmann equations at the phase-space level. We present a new method to address this challenge using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) based on stochastic interactions of an ensemble of particles. We implement and validate efficient algorithms to describe freeze-out, decays, elastic scattering and number-changing processes within the dark sector. These algorithms do not require a discretisation of momentum space on a pre-defined grid and do not rely on approximations such as thermally averaged cross sections. As illustrative example, we consider a scenario with two-step dark matter production, leading to a bimodal phase-space distribution, and consider the subsequent evolution under elastic and number-changing processes. We show that DSMC is a flexible approach to explore out-of-equilibrium processes and solve Boltzmann equations at the phase-space level in order to predict the abundance of dark matter particles and their effect on structure formation.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method to solve phase-space Boltzmann equations for non-thermal dark matter production, avoiding momentum-space discretization and thermal averaging approximations.
AI.motivation: To accurately model early-universe dark matter production beyond thermal equilibrium—where standard approximations (e.g., thermally averaged cross sections or fixed momentum grids) fail—especially for complex, out-of-equilibrium scenarios like multi-step production yielding non-trivial phase-space structures.
AI.method: A DSMC-based stochastic particle simulation framework is developed and implemented, supporting freeze-out, decays, elastic scattering, and number-changing interactions within the dark sector; it operates directly in continuous phase space without grid discretization or thermal averaging.
AI.result: The method successfully reproduces and tracks bimodal phase-space distributions arising from two-step dark matter production, and captures subsequent evolution under elastic and number-changing processes; validation confirms accuracy and flexibility for out-of-equilibrium kinetics.
AI.conclusion: DSMC provides a robust, grid-free, approximation-free computational framework for solving full phase-space Boltzmann equations, enabling precise predictions of dark matter abundance and its imprints on cosmological structure formation.

title: Resonant Cavity Searches for Millicharged Dark Matter
summary: A plethora of resonant cavity experiments have been designed to search for ultralight dark matter (DM) candidates, such as axion or dark-photon DM. In this work, we show that these same apparatuses can be sensitive to ultralight millicharged dark matter (mDM) with masses $m_\phi\sim1-100\,\mu\mathrm{eV}$. Similar to axion DM, in the presence of a background magnetic field, mDM acts as an effective current which can excite the modes of a resonant cavity. Importantly, for a cylindrical cavity, axion DM dominantly couples to the transverse magnetic (TM) modes, whereas mDM dominantly couples to the transverse electric (TE) modes. We project the sensitivity to mDM that resonant cavity experiments can achieve if they are able to tune and readout their TE modes. We find that fractional millicharges as small as $\epsilon_m=e_m/e\sim10^{-19}$ can be probed. If mDM constitutes only a subfraction $f_\mDM \lesssim0.2\%$ of the total DM density, competing astrophysical bounds do not apply. In this case, resonant cavities can be the most sensitive probes of mDM in this mass range.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes repurposing resonant cavity experiments—originally designed for axion/dark-photon dark matter—to detect ultralight millicharged dark matter (mDM) in the 1–100 µeV mass range, leveraging its distinct coupling to TE cavity modes and achieving sensitivity down to fractional charge εₘ ∼ 10⁻¹⁹.
AI.motivation: Existing resonant cavity experiments for axion or dark-photon DM can be extended to probe millicharged DM (mDM), a theoretically motivated but experimentally underexplored ultralight DM candidate; current constraints on mDM are weak for subpercent DM fractions, leaving room for novel detection strategies.
AI.method: Theoretical modeling of mDM as an oscillating scalar field with tiny electric charge interacting with magnetic fields to generate an effective current; analysis of mode coupling in cylindrical microwave cavities, distinguishing dominant excitation of TE modes by mDM versus TM modes by axions; sensitivity projection via signal-to-noise estimation assuming tunable and readout-capable TE-mode operation.
AI.result: Resonant cavities can probe mDM with fractional charge εₘ ≳ 10⁻¹⁹ for masses m_ϕ ∼ 1–100 µeV; this sensitivity surpasses astrophysical bounds when mDM constitutes f_mDM ≲ 0.2% of total DM density.
AI.conclusion: Cylindrical resonant cavities—when adapted for TE-mode tuning and readout—constitute the most sensitive terrestrial probes for ultralight millicharged DM in the 1–100 µeV window, offering a new physics channel complementary to axion searches.

title: Majorana dark matter from a thick-to-thin brane junction: Modal stability, real-mediator coannihilation, and a dark-radiation imprint
summary: We show that the localized spectrum of a $D=7$ thick-to-thin brane junction can host a thermal Majorana dark-matter candidate. The anisotropy of the wall widths isolates a light junction fermion, which a four-dimensional Majorana mass splits into two nearby states. The factorized transverse profiles impose a modal selection rule on all cubic couplings, and together with the relaxation of the softly deformed background this makes the lighter state stable without an imposed dark parity. Because the localized mediator is a real scalar, identical Majorana particles annihilate in the $s$ wave, and the relic coupling becomes nearly independent of the Majorana mass. The junction sector is a Standard-Model singlet whose light chiral mode is a source of dark radiation. Current CMB data restrict its decoupling temperature and imply $0.05\lesssim\dNeff\lesssim0.076$ for dark-matter masses between $10\GeV$ and $1.5\TeV$, a range accessible to next-generation CMB surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a thermal Majorana dark matter candidate localized at a thick-to-thin brane junction in 7D, stabilized by geometric and modal selection rules—not ad hoc symmetries—enabling s-wave annihilation via a real scalar mediator; it predicts a detectable dark radiation signal (ΔN_eff ≈ 0.05–0.076) consistent with current CMB constraints.
AI.motivation: To construct a natural, symmetry-free stabilization mechanism for thermal Majorana dark matter in extra-dimensional setups, while generating testable dark radiation signatures.
AI.method: Analyzes fermion localization and spectrum at a D=7 anisotropic thick-to-thin brane junction; derives modal selection rules from factorized transverse profiles and background deformation; computes relic density via s-wave annihilation mediated by a localized real scalar; evaluates dark radiation contribution from light chiral mode and confronts with CMB ΔN_eff bounds.
AI.result: A stable, thermal Majorana dark matter candidate emerges without dark parity; relic coupling is nearly mass-independent due to s-wave annihilation; predicted ΔN_eff = 0.05–0.076 for m_DM ∈ [10 GeV, 1.5 TeV], within reach of next-gen CMB experiments.
AI.conclusion: Geometric and modal structure of brane junctions can intrinsically stabilize Majorana dark matter and generate correlated dark radiation, offering a predictive, testable alternative to parity-based models.

title: New unintegrated gluon density in proton and nuclei tested with small $x$ processes at modern colliders
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures. This is a contribution to Proceedings for QCD at the Extremes 2026
summary: We present a new unintegrated, or transverse momentum dependent (TMD) gluon density in proton and nuclei. Parameters of the new function have been obtained from a fit on inclusive soft charged hadron production and structure functions at low scales, and from comparison with data on a number of processes at higher scales results taken at LHC and HERA, such as heavy quarks production, prompt photon photoproduction and Higgs boson production. A modification employing the geometric scaling approach has been made to extend the obtained parton density to the case of light and heavy nuclei. As a test of the nuclear TMD distribution we perform a calculation of the charged hadrons multiplicity spectra in pPb collisions at the LHC energies.

AI.tldr: Introduces a new transverse momentum dependent (TMD) gluon density for protons and nuclei, constrained by low- and high-scale experimental data (HERA, LHC), extended to nuclei via geometric scaling, and validated via pPb charged-hadron multiplicity predictions.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified, unintegrated gluon distribution applicable across energy scales and nuclear systems, addressing limitations of collinear parton densities in describing soft and semi-hard QCD processes.
AI.method: Global fit of TMD gluon density parameters to inclusive soft hadron production and structure functions at low Q²; cross-validation against HERA and LHC data (heavy quarks, prompt photons, Higgs); extension to nuclei using geometric scaling ansatz.
AI.result: A new nuclear-dependent TMD gluon distribution is obtained; successful reproduction of charged-hadron multiplicity spectra in pPb collisions at LHC energies serves as validation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed TMD gluon density consistently describes diverse observables from ep to pA collisions, supporting its use in small-x and saturation-inspired phenomenology for proton and nuclear targets.

title: Interpretation of the LZ Event via Inelastic ALP-Dark Photon Transition with Photon Exchange
summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has reported a nuclear recoil event at $248\pm23$~keV with a global significance of about $2.6\sigma$. We for the first time explain it via the inelastic process with photon mediator. We consider a dark matter (DM) axion-like particle (ALP) $a$ converts into a heavier dark photon $\gamma'$ via the nuclear electromagnetic current, and study the photon-mediated endothermic transition $aA\rightarrow\gamma'A$. We derive the kinematics and cross sections for non-relativistic halo and boosted ALPs. A three-bin Poisson fit to the LZ data includes the xenon isotopes, charge form factors, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. Halo DM, which has mass $m\simeq1.2$~TeV, mass splitting $\delta\simeq346$~keV, and near the upper coupling bound, reproduces the event with about $61\%$ in the middle bin. Boosted DM with $v_{0}=0.05\,c$ and $\Phi_{0}=10^{5}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ requires only $m\simeq5.74$~GeV and $\delta\simeq6.66$~MeV to give about $62\%$. We find that a broader Gaussian spread in the incident energy has a significant effect on the fitted masses.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an axion-like particle (ALP) dark matter model with inelastic scattering via a photon-mediated process to explain a 2.6σ nuclear recoil event observed by LZ at ~248 keV; it fits both halo and boosted ALP scenarios, yielding distinct mass and mass-splitting parameters, and highlights sensitivity to energy resolution effects.
AI.motivation: To explain the anomalous 2.6σ nuclear recoil event at 248±23 keV reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment using a novel inelastic dark matter mechanism involving axion-like particles and dark photons.
AI.method: Develops a photon-mediated endothermic transition model aA → γ'A where ALP a converts to dark photon γ' via nuclear electromagnetic current; computes kinematics and cross sections for non-relativistic halo and relativistic boosted ALPs; performs a three-bin Poisson likelihood fit incorporating xenon isotopic composition, charge form factors, detector efficiency, and energy resolution.
AI.result: Halo ALP DM with m ≈ 1.2 TeV, δ ≈ 346 keV, and coupling near upper bounds reproduces ~61% of the event in the central energy bin; boosted ALP DM (v₀ = 0.05c, Φ₀ = 10⁵ cm⁻² s⁻¹) requires m ≈ 5.74 GeV and δ ≈ 6.66 MeV for ~62%; broader incident energy spread significantly shifts fitted masses.
AI.conclusion: The LZ event can be consistently interpreted as inelastic scattering of ALP dark matter converting to dark photons via nuclear electromagnetic current; both halo and boosted scenarios are viable, but parameter inference is highly sensitive to energy resolution modeling.

title: Inclusive and diffractive D meson photoproduction in $pPb$ collisions at the LHC using Pythia8 framework
summary: We present a systematic analysis of inclusive and diffractive $D$-meson photoproduction in $ep$ and ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions within the Pythia8 framework. Predictions obtained with different proton and Pomeron PDFs are compared with H1 measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^*$ photoproduction at HERA. We also present predictions for the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction at the LHC. Our analysis indicates that the diffractive contribution exceeds 15\% at low $p_T$ and forward rapidities, suggesting that diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction could be accessible in future LHC runs. In addition, measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions can help constrain the proton and Pomeron PDFs.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes inclusive and diffractive D-meson photoproduction in ep and ultraperipheral pPb collisions using Pythia8, comparing predictions with H1/HERA data and providing LHC rapidity/pT distributions; finds diffractive contribution >15% at low pT/forward y, suggesting observability at LHC, and highlights pPb measurements for constraining proton/Pomeron PDFs.
AI.motivation: To systematically assess inclusive and diffractive D-meson photoproduction across collider systems (HERA, LHC) and evaluate the sensitivity of such processes—particularly in ultraperipheral pPb collisions—to proton and Pomeron parton distribution functions (PDFs).
AI.method: Monte Carlo simulation within the Pythia8 event generator framework, employing multiple proton and Pomeron PDF sets; comparison of predicted inclusive and diffractive D* (HERA) and D0 (LHC, pPb) cross sections and kinematic distributions (rapidity, transverse momentum) with experimental data.
AI.result: Diffractive D0 photoproduction contributes >15% at low pT and forward rapidity in LHC conditions; H1 HERA data on D* are reasonably reproduced; pPb ultraperipheral collisions offer enhanced sensitivity to constrain Pomeron and proton PDFs.
AI.conclusion: Diffractive D-meson photoproduction is significant and measurable at the LHC, especially in forward regions; combined inclusive/diffractive D0 measurements in pPb UPCs provide a novel probe for Pomeron structure and proton PDFs at small-x.

title: Concerning Factorization at Lepton Colliders
summary: We uncover super-leading logarithms in non-global observables at lepton colliders. They arise from Glauber interactions involving colored partons produced by electromagnetic splittings of the incoming leptons. A three-loop analysis establishes the resulting factorization breaking, which we reconcile with the use of lepton PDFs below the soft veto scale. We conjecture that soft--collinear factorization fails for exclusive observables even in pure QED by identifying a genuine Glauber region in massless QED. This reveals a far richer infrared structure than naively expected.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies super-leading logarithms in non-global observables at lepton colliders, arising from Glauber interactions involving colored partons from electromagnetic lepton splittings; it demonstrates factorization breaking at three loops, reconciles it with lepton PDF usage below the soft veto scale, and conjectures soft–collinear factorization failure even in pure QED due to a genuine Glauber region.
AI.motivation: To understand unexpected infrared structures in non-global observables at lepton colliders, particularly whether soft–collinear factorization holds beyond QCD-like settings—including massless QED—and to resolve apparent inconsistencies between Glauber-induced effects and standard factorization frameworks.
AI.method: Three-loop perturbative QCD and QED analysis of Glauber exchanges; systematic study of electromagnetic splittings of incoming leptons into colored partons; examination of soft veto scale dependence and lepton PDF applicability; identification and characterization of the Glauber region in massless QED.
AI.result: Discovery of super-leading logarithms in non-global observables at lepton colliders; demonstration of factorization breaking due to Glauber interactions; successful reconciliation with lepton PDFs below the soft veto scale; identification of a genuine Glauber region in massless QED implying soft–collinear factorization failure for exclusive observables.
AI.conclusion: The infrared structure of lepton collider processes is richer than previously assumed: Glauber exchanges induce super-leading logarithms and break standard soft–collinear factorization—even in pure QED—necessitating refined theoretical frameworks for precision predictions of non-global, exclusive observables.

title: NNLO QCD corrections to radiative and hadronic $Υ(1S)$ decays
summary: We present the complete next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD corrections to radiative and inclusive hadronic $\Upsilon(1S)$ decays in the color-singlet framework at leading order in the heavy-quark velocity expansion. For radiative decay, the NNLO correction reshapes the photon energy spectrum and lowers the partial width in the fiducial window $0.65\leq 2E_\gamma/M_\Upsilon\leq0.92$, bringing the central prediction into good agreement with reconstructed CLEO data. For inclusive hadronic decay, the NNLO correction provides a large negative shift that lowers the predicted width from its inflated NLO value to a level fully consistent with the experimental determination. Although both individual decay widths exhibit larger renormalization-scale uncertainties at NNLO, their ratio demonstrates a significantly reduced scale dependence due to the cancellation of common short-distance dynamics and the nonperturbative matrix element. Using the window ratio inferred from CLEO measurements, we extract the strong coupling constant $\alpha_s^{(5)}(M_Z) = 0.12135^{+0.0039}_{-0.0036}$, compatible with the world average, and evaluate the sensitivity to uncalculated higher orders via the unexpanded quotient.

AI.tldr: This paper computes full NNLO QCD corrections to radiative and inclusive hadronic Υ(1S) decays in the color-singlet model (v² expansion), improving agreement with CLEO data and enabling a precise αₛ(M_Z) extraction via decay width ratio.
AI.motivation: To resolve discrepancies between NLO theory predictions and experimental data for Υ(1S) decays, and to reduce theoretical uncertainty—especially renormalization-scale dependence—in extracting αₛ from bottomonium decays.
AI.method: Complete NNLO QCD calculation within the NRQCD-based color-singlet framework at leading order in the heavy-quark velocity (v) expansion; includes virtual and real radiation contributions; uses fiducial photon energy cuts (0.65 ≤ 2E_γ/M_Υ ≤ 0.92); employs ratio method to cancel common short-distance and nonperturbative uncertainties.
AI.result: NNLO corrections significantly suppress both radiative and inclusive hadronic widths relative to NLO; improves agreement with CLEO data; reduces scale uncertainty in the width ratio; yields αₛ^(5)(M_Z) = 0.12135^{+0.0039}_{-0.0036}.
AI.conclusion: NNLO QCD corrections are essential for quantitative precision in Υ(1S) decays; the width ratio provides a robust, scale-stable observable for αₛ determination, validating the color-singlet NRQCD framework at NNLO and confirming consistency with the global αₛ average.

title: Photon-Mediated Axino-Bino Scattering Process for the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event
summary: We for the first time investigate the photon-mediated endothermic axino-bino scattering process to explain the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy recoil event. We calculate the signals from non-relativistic halo and boosted dark matter (DM), including natural xenon isotopes, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. For a fixed Standard Halo Model (SHM) distribution, a simplified three-bin Poisson analysis yields a best-fit benchmark with mass $m\simeq506\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and mass splitting $\delta\simeq326\,\mathrm{keV}$ at the adopted upper coupling bound $g_\gamma=10^{-3}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. It predicts approximately one accepted event, with $70\%$ in the middle bin. A boosted benchmark with $m\simeq82.87\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and $\delta\simeq0.626\,\mathrm{MeV}$ provides a comparable fit. Broader Gaussian incident energy distributions allow fitted masses down to a few GeV. Thus, both the halo and boosted DM scenarios can fit the LZ signal at different DM mass scales.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes photon-mediated endothermic axino-bino scattering as an explanation for the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy recoil event, fitting both Standard Halo Model and boosted dark matter scenarios with distinct mass and mass-splitting benchmarks.
AI.motivation: To explain the anomalous high-energy recoil event observed by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment using a novel endothermic dark matter interaction mechanism.
AI.method: Calculates signals from non-relativistic halo and boosted dark matter, incorporating natural xenon isotopes, detector efficiency, energy resolution, and performs a three-bin Poisson analysis under the Standard Halo Model; explores broader Gaussian incident energy distributions.
AI.result: Identifies best-fit benchmarks: halo DM with m ≈ 506 GeV, δ ≈ 326 keV, predicting ~1 accepted event (70% in middle bin); boosted DM with m ≈ 82.87 GeV, δ ≈ 0.626 MeV; broader energy distributions allow sub-10 GeV masses.
AI.conclusion: Both halo and boosted DM scenarios—via photon-mediated endothermic axino-bino scattering—can plausibly explain the LZ signal across widely differing mass scales.

title: Predictions for Inclusive Production Cross Sections of the Higgs Boson at the LHC and HL-LHC
comment: 114 pages, including 85 tables, 4 figures, and 272 references. Submitted as part of Report 5 within the LHC Higgs Working Group. Associated data and up-to-date tables can be found at this https URL
summary: We present updated recommendations of the LHC Higgs Working Group (LHCHWG) for the inclusive production cross sections of a Standard Model Higgs boson in proton--proton collisions at centre-of-mass energies between $7$ and $14$ TeV, including the Run-3 energy of $13.6$ TeV, and for Higgs-boson masses between $120$ and $130$ GeV. All the major production modes are covered. The central values remain consistent with those of Yellow Report 4 (YR4) [arXiv:1610.07922] within the uncertainties quoted there, while the theoretical uncertainties are reduced for most production modes. The improvements rest on specific calculations rather than on a uniform advance: the complete N$^3$LO result in the heavy-top limit together with exact NNLO top-quark mass effects for gluon fusion; the N$^3$LO structure-function calculation supplemented by non-factorisable corrections for vector-boson fusion; the completion of the NLO QCD corrections to the loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ channel for $VH$; NNLO QCD matched to NNLL soft-gluon resummation and combined with NLO electroweak corrections for $t\bar{t}H$, and updated predictions for $tH$; and the matched four- and five-flavour-scheme prediction, with its explicit resummation-scale uncertainty, for $b\bar{b}H$. Since no PDF4LHC recommendation exists beyond NNLO, the mismatch between an N$^3$LO matrix element and NNLO distributions has to be carried as an uncertainty, estimated process by process: it is well determined for vector-boson fusion, whereas for gluon fusion it is doubled relative to YR4. PDFs are now the leading source of uncertainty for the most precisely predicted modes, while residual perturbative uncertainties dominate for the remainder. These results supersede the inclusive cross sections of YR4 and the ad interim recommendations of Ref. [arXiv:2402.09955], and form part of Report 5 of the LHCHWG.

AI.tldr: This paper updates the LHC Higgs Working Group's recommended inclusive Higgs boson production cross sections at pp collision energies from 7 to 14 TeV (including 13.6 TeV Run-3), for Higgs masses 120–130 GeV, incorporating higher-order QCD and electroweak calculations across all major production modes—gluon fusion, vector-boson fusion, VH, ttH, tH, and bbH—with reduced theoretical uncertainties compared to Yellow Report 4.
AI.motivation: To provide state-of-the-art, consistent, and uncertainty-quantified predictions for SM Higgs production cross sections at current and upcoming LHC energies, addressing advances in perturbative calculations and clarifying limitations (e.g., PDF order mismatch) that affect reliability and comparability with experimental measurements.
AI.method: Combines latest fixed-order and resummed perturbative calculations: N³LO + exact NNLO top-mass effects (gg→H); N³LO structure-function + non-factorisable corrections (VBF); completed NLO QCD for gg→ZH; NNLO+NNLL+EW for ttH; updated tH; matched 4F/5F schemes with resummation-scale uncertainty for bbH; consistently propagates PDF4LHC21 NNLO PDF uncertainties and estimates matrix-element–PDF order mismatch as process-dependent uncertainty.
AI.result: Central cross sections remain consistent with YR4 within prior uncertainties, but theoretical uncertainties are reduced for most channels; PDF uncertainties now dominate for high-precision modes (e.g., VBF), while residual perturbative uncertainties dominate others (e.g., gg→H); the gluon-fusion PDF–ME mismatch uncertainty is doubled relative to YR4; results supersede YR4 and interim recommendations (arXiv:2402.09955).
AI.conclusion: These updated cross sections constitute the definitive theoretical reference for Higgs physics at the LHC Run-3 and beyond, embedded in LHCHWG Report 5, enabling more precise SM tests and BSM sensitivity studies.

title: Who Moved My $Z$ Boson? Revealing Resonance Features Inside a Neural Network
comment: 10 pages (+4 pages of references, +14 pages of supplementary material, 29 total pages), 7 figures in the main text (+14 figures in the supplementary material, total of 21 pages)
summary: Methods used in mechanistic interpretability have revealed human-aligned concepts inside language and image models. In this paper, we search for physics concepts inside a neural a generative collider physics model trained on real LHC data (ShellFlow). We discover features inside ShellFlow that represent resonances, such as the $Z$, $J/\psi$, and $\Upsilon$. The network was never told which muons come from a resonance, it was only trained to generate the kinematics of the final-state particles. We use these features to alter aspects of the $Z$ boson: we change its mass between $\sim80$ and $105$ GeV, and removing such a feature from the neural network produces a broader $Z$ peak. In both cases the rest of the invariant mass spectrum remains mostly unchanged. The feature was built from the gradients of the neural network, and its selectivity was built using pattern recognition methods. A generative particle physics model trained on unlabeled data can be modified internally to change a physical quantity.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies and manipulates physics-resonance features (e.g., Z, J/ψ, Υ) in ShellFlow—a generative collider physics model trained on unlabeled LHC data—demonstrating that internal neural features encode interpretable, human-aligned physical quantities without explicit supervision.
AI.motivation: To determine whether unsupervised generative models trained on real collider data implicitly learn fundamental physics concepts—specifically resonance structures—and whether such concepts can be isolated and causally manipulated.
AI.method: Applied mechanistic interpretability techniques—including gradient-based feature identification and pattern recognition—to probe internal representations of ShellFlow; performed targeted ablation and activation editing of identified resonance features to alter invariant mass distributions (e.g., Z boson mass shift and peak broadening).
AI.result: Discovered interpretable, resonance-specific features corresponding to Z, J/ψ, and Υ; successfully edited the Z-mass peak (80–105 GeV range) and broadened it via feature ablation while preserving the rest of the invariant mass spectrum.
AI.conclusion: Generative particle physics models trained on unlabeled collider data can internally encode physically meaningful, manipulable concepts—enabling causal interpretation and controllable generation grounded in real physics.

title: Towards Consistent Thermal Resummation: Improved Partial Dressing for Precise Electroweak Phase Transition Predictions
comment: 52 pages, 11 figures, 5 tables, comments are welcome!
summary: Reliable predictions for the electroweak phase transition depend critically on a consistent resummation of thermal fluctuations. However, existing prescriptions often entail sizable uncertainties, motivating the development of a robust and systematically controlled resummation scheme. In this work, we develop an improved partial dressing (IPD) scheme that resolves intrinsic inconsistencies in the original partial dressing prescription, including the overlapping momentum problem and the associated divergences in the gap equations. By consistently incorporating momentum-dependent self-energies and reorganizing the daisy resummation, the IPD scheme provides a more systematic framework for thermal resummation. We perform a comprehensive comparison of 5 different resummation prescriptions in the well-motivated inert doublet model and demonstrate that the choice of resummation scheme can substantially affect the predicted phase transition parameters and the resulting gravitational wave spectra. Notably, the IPD prescription yields a reliable potential and comparatively robust phenomenological predictions, highlighting the importance of a self-consistent treatment of thermal corrections. Our results establish the theoretical consistency of IPD and demonstrate that controlling resummation uncertainties is essential for reliable predictions of cosmological phase transitions and their gravitational wave signatures.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an Improved Partial Dressing (IPD) scheme to resolve inconsistencies in thermal resummation for electroweak phase transition predictions, demonstrating its superiority over four other methods in the inert doublet model regarding potential reliability and gravitational wave spectrum robustness.
AI.motivation: Existing thermal resummation prescriptions suffer from intrinsic inconsistencies (e.g., overlapping momentum problem, divergent gap equations) and sizable uncertainties, undermining reliability of electroweak phase transition and gravitational wave predictions.
AI.method: Development of the Improved Partial Dressing (IPD) scheme—addressing inconsistencies via momentum-dependent self-energies and reorganized daisy resummation—and comparative analysis of five resummation schemes in the inert doublet model using finite-temperature effective potential and gravitational wave spectrum calculations.
AI.result: IPD yields a well-behaved, reliable finite-temperature effective potential; substantially reduces scheme dependence in phase transition strength (α), duration (β/H*), and peak frequency/amplitude of gravitational wave spectra compared to other prescriptions.
AI.conclusion: The IPD scheme is theoretically consistent, systematically controlled, and essential for reducing resummation-induced uncertainties in cosmological phase transition predictions and associated gravitational wave observables.

title: $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings at the Large Hadron Collider
summary: Constraining the $Z$-boson couplings of the $b$ quark, or even ruling out the possibility of an opposite-sign coupling, is considered very challenging at the LHC. Utilizing signatures of new physics resulting from contact operators accompanying the modification of $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings from Standard Model predictions, we show that the ATLAS measurement of $pp\to Zh$ already ruled out the opposite-sign couplings by more than 9.5 standard deviations. We also argue that $pp\to Zhb$, which receives a contribution from the same contact term, would lead to even better sensitivity. Furthermore, we show that with future data this indirect method can provide the strongest constraints on $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings, and can even probe the anomaly in these couplings left over from the LEP era.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that ATLAS's $pp\to Zh$ measurement already excludes opposite-sign $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings at >9.5σ, and proposes $pp\to Zhb$ as a more sensitive probe; it argues that indirect constraints from such processes will surpass direct ones, including those needed to resolve the LEP-era $Zb\bar{b}$ anomaly.
AI.motivation: The challenge of directly constraining or ruling out opposite-sign modifications to the $Zb\bar{b}$ coupling at the LHC motivates an indirect approach via new physics signatures linked to contact operators affecting this coupling.
AI.method: The authors analyze how deviations in $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings—parameterized via effective contact operators—affect the $pp \to Zh$ and $pp \to Zhb$ cross sections; they reinterpret existing ATLAS $Zh$ data and perform sensitivity projections for $Zhb$ using SM and BSM signal yields.
AI.result: ATLAS $pp \to Zh$ data excludes opposite-sign $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings at >9.5σ; $pp \to Zhb$ is shown to have superior sensitivity; future integrated luminosity enables indirect constraints stronger than current direct limits and capable of probing the residual LEP anomaly.
AI.conclusion: Indirect constraints from $Zh$ and especially $Zhb$ production provide the most powerful present and future probes of $Zb\bar{b}$ coupling modifications, surpassing traditional direct measurements and offering resolution of longstanding electroweak anomalies.

title: Weyl-induced ultrasoft renormalization of the static QCD potential
summary:
We derive the leading curvature-dependent ultrasoft anomalous dimension of the static color-singlet potential in potential nonrelativistic QCD. In a Ricci-flat background the electric Weyl tensor introduces a $t^{-2}$ term in the short-time chromoelectric correlator. The resulting dipole self-energy is ultraviolet divergent at order $\alpha_s^2$ in the curvature sector, two orders earlier than the flat-space contribution. For $W=C_{\mu\alpha
u eta}r^\mu u^\alpha r^

u\,\partial_
