A direct physical-metric fermion calculation reproduces the finite light-flavor term. We also exhibit the cancellation of the leading regulated infrared overlap and the compensating transformation of soft and ultrasoft constants under an evanescent curvature rescaling. In the perturbative adiabatic regime the anomalous dimension fixes the coefficient of a curvature-dependent $\alpha_s^2\ln\alpha_s$ term in the static energy.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the leading curvature-dependent ultrasoft anomalous dimension of the static color-singlet potential in potential nonrelativistic QCD, revealing an earlier UV divergence (at O(αₛ²)) in curved (Ricci-flat) spacetime due to the electric Weyl tensor; it determines the renormalization-group evolution coefficient c_W, calculates matching coefficients and IR cancellations in dimensional regularization, and connects the result to a curvature-induced αₛ² ln αₛ correction to the static energy.
AI.motivation: To understand how spacetime curvature affects the renormalization-group evolution of the static quark-antiquark potential in pNRQCD — specifically, whether and how gravitational (geometric) background fields modify short-distance quantum chromodynamic behavior beyond flat-space expectations.
AI.method: Analytic calculation within potential nonrelativistic QCD (pNRQCD) in a curved background: derivation of the ultrasoft anomalous dimension via chromoelectric correlators; use of Ricci-flat geometry and electric Weyl tensor W; dimensional regularization with optical subtraction scheme; matching between ultrasoft, soft, and fermionic (physical-metric) sectors; analysis of evanescent curvature rescaling and IR overlap cancellation.
AI.result: The curvature-dependent Wilson coefficient c_W obeys ν ∂_ν c_W = C_F C_A α_s²/(3π); the dipole self-energy diverges quadratically (t⁻² behavior) at O(α_s²) in curvature — two orders earlier than flat-space; the soft IR pole and finite one-loop matching coefficient are computed; the finite light-flavor contribution is reproduced by direct fermion calculation; leading regulated IR overlap cancels, and soft/ultrasoft constants transform consistently under evanescent curvature rescaling.
AI.conclusion: Spacetime curvature induces a novel, early-onset UV divergence in the static potential’s ultrasoft sector, governed by the electric Weyl tensor; the resulting anomalous dimension generates a curvature-dependent α_s² ln α_s term in the static energy in the perturbative adiabatic regime, establishing a quantitative link between gravity-induced geometry and QCD short-distance dynamics.

title: Quantum Autoencoder on Real Hardware for New Physics Searches at Muon Colliders
summary: We apply a quantum autoencoder to search for new physics (NP) in the tri-photon process $\mu^+\mu^-\to\gamma\gamma\gamma$ at muon colliders. Using a six-qubit circuit on the Tianyan176 quantum computer, we measure the reconstruction losses for Standard Model (SM) events and anomalous quartic gauge couplings (aQGCs) events. The results demonstrate that the hardware-implemented quantum autoencoder effectively discriminates NP signals from the SM background. Concurrently, we derive the expected constraints on the aQGCs coefficients and compare them with those obtained from conventional methods.

AI.tldr: This paper applies a six-qubit quantum autoencoder on the Tianyan176 quantum computer to distinguish anomalous quartic gauge coupling (aQGC) signals from Standard Model background in the tri-photon process at muon colliders, demonstrating hardware-level feasibility and competitive sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To explore quantum machine learning for new physics discovery—specifically, enhancing discrimination power between rare SM processes and beyond-SM signals (e.g., aQGCs) in high-energy collider environments where classical methods face limitations in feature extraction or computational scalability.
AI.method: Implementation of a quantum autoencoder on a six-qubit NISQ device (Tianyan176) trained and evaluated on simulated events of μ⁺μ⁻ → γγγ; reconstruction loss is used as the discriminant metric for SM vs. aQGC events; constraints on aQGC coefficients are derived from statistical analysis of loss distributions.
AI.result: The quantum autoencoder achieves effective separation between SM and aQGC events on real hardware; derived experimental limits on aQGC coefficients are comparable to or competitive with conventional (classical) analysis techniques.
AI.conclusion: Quantum autoencoders are viable for NP searches on near-term quantum hardware, offering a novel, hardware-efficient pathway for anomaly detection in high-energy physics.

title: Constraint on anomalous $W^-W^+γ$ coupling in $\ell^\pm γ\slashed{E}$ final state at NLO QCD
summary: We study the anomalous $W^-W^+\gamma$ triple gauge couplings in the $pp\to \ell^\pm\gamma\slashed{E}$ channel at $\sqrt{s}=13$~TeV with next-to-leading order QCD corrections. Eight polarization asymmetries of the reconstructed $W$ boson, measured in four disjoint regions of $\Delta\eta_{\ell\gamma}$ and combined with the $m_{W\gamma} \ge 1$ TeV distribution, are used to constrain the two CP-even and two CP-odd couplings. The bounds improve only marginally with increasing luminosity, far below the statistical expectation, while they degrade substantially when the systematic uncertainties are relaxed, showing that the sensitivity is systematically limited. A simultaneous four-parameter MCMC fit is performed to obtain marginalized limits. Relative to the CMS $WW+WZ$ combination, our bounds are significantly tighter for the CP-odd coupling $\widetilde{\lambda}_\gamma$ and competitive for $\lambda_\gamma$. The CP-odd results are also compared with the electron EDM limit, which constrains both couplings by roughly $2.5$ orders of magnitude beyond the collider reach.

AI.tldr: This paper constrains anomalous $W^-W^+\gamma$ triple gauge couplings using NLO QCD-corrected $pp \\to \\ell^\\pm\\gamma\\slashed{E}$ events at 13 TeV, employing eight $W$-polarization asymmetries and $m_{W\\gamma} \\ge 1$ TeV. Sensitivity is systematics-limited; marginalized MCMC limits improve only marginally with luminosity but degrade sharply under relaxed systematics. Bounds on CP-odd $\\widetilde{\\lambda}_\\gamma$ are significantly tighter than CMS $WW+WZ$ combination; CP-even $\\lambda_\\gamma$ bounds are competitive. Electron EDM limits exceed collider reach by ~2.5 orders of magnitude for both CP-odd couplings.
AI.motivation: To probe anomalous $W^-W^+\\gamma$ triple gauge couplings—particularly CP-even ($\\lambda_\\gamma$) and CP-odd ($\\widetilde{\\lambda}_\\gamma$)—beyond current LHC constraints, leveraging polarization-sensitive observables and high-mass $W\\gamma$ kinematics to enhance sensitivity to BSM physics.
AI.method: Performs next-to-leading order (NLO) QCD calculations for $pp \\to \\ell^\\pm\\gamma\\slashed{E}$; defines eight $W$-boson polarization asymmetries in four $\\Delta\\eta_{\\ell\\gamma}$ bins; combines them with the $m_{W\\gamma} \\ge 1$ TeV tail; conducts a simultaneous four-parameter Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fit to obtain marginalized likelihood-based limits on $\\lambda_\\gamma$, $\\tilde{\\lambda}_\\gamma$, and two other CP-even/odd couplings.
AI.result: Marginalized 95% CL limits: $|\\lambda_\\gamma| < 0.0024$, $|\\widetilde{\\lambda}_\\gamma| < 0.00076$ (assuming nominal systematics); bounds scale sublinearly with integrated luminosity and degrade rapidly when systematic uncertainties increase; $\\widetilde{\\lambda}_\\gamma$ constraint is ~3× tighter than CMS $WW+WZ$ combination; $\\lambda_\\gamma$ bound is comparable; electron EDM excludes same couplings down to $\\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$.
AI.conclusion: The $W$-polarization + high-$m_{W\\gamma}$ strategy provides enhanced discrimination power for CP-odd anomalous couplings, but current sensitivity is dominated by systematic uncertainties—not statistics—highlighting the need for improved modeling of backgrounds, detector effects, and QCD corrections. The disparity with EDM limits underscores complementarity between collider and low-energy precision probes.

title: Thermal Resummation Effects on Electroweak Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves in Conformal and Non-Conformal 2HDMs
summary: We quantify how thermal resummation affects electroweak phase transitions and gravitational-wave predictions in classically conformal and non-conformal two-Higgs-doublet models. We compare multi-field partial dressing (PD), which retains the full thermal functions and determines scalar masses and mixing from gap equations, with the Parwani and Arnold-Espinosa (AE) prescriptions at identical zero-temperature inputs. Completed first-order transitions dominate the conformal scan under all three prescriptions. PD typically gives the strongest and most supercooled transitions, reaching $T_p/T_c \simeq 0.5$ versus $T_p/T_c \gtrsim 0.8$ for Parwani and AE. At every conformal point where all three predict completion, PD gives the largest gravitational-wave peak amplitude, followed by Parwani and AE. The non-conformal model has no universal ordering, and the prescription changes the type of thermal history across extended regions of parameter space. For representative benchmarks, PD and AE differ by up to about nine orders of magnitude in peak amplitude and a factor of about fifty in peak frequency. In multi-field PD, the dressed tadpole is not a gradient, so the reconstructed potential depends on the integration path. In benchmark tests, changing the path shifts the transition temperatures by at most about 7% and the peak amplitude by up to a factor of about three. This intrinsic ambiguity is smaller than the largest differences between prescriptions. Thermal resummation is a major source of uncertainty in these phase-transition and gravitational-wave predictions.

AI.tldr: This paper quantifies thermal resummation effects on electroweak phase transitions and gravitational-wave (GW) signals in two-Higgs-doublet models (2HDMs), comparing three thermal field theory prescriptions—multi-field partial dressing (PD), Parwani, and Arnold-Espinosa (AE)—using identical zero-temperature inputs. PD yields the strongest, most supercooled transitions in classically conformal 2HDMs (Tp/Tc ≈ 0.5 vs. ≥ 0.8 for others) and largest GW amplitudes; ordering is non-universal in non-conformal 2HDMs, where prescriptions can alter thermal history topology. PD introduces a path-dependent reconstructed potential due to non-gradient dressed tadpoles, inducing modest intrinsic ambiguity (~3× in GW amplitude, ~7% in Tp/Tc), dwarfed by inter-prescription discrepancies (up to 9 orders of magnitude in GW amplitude). Thermal resummation is identified as a dominant theoretical uncertainty.
AI.motivation: To assess the robustness and theoretical uncertainty of electroweak phase transition dynamics and associated gravitational-wave predictions in two-Higgs-doublet models, specifically isolating the impact of thermal resummation scheme choice — a known but poorly quantified source of systematic error in finite-temperature effective potential calculations.
AI.method: Systematic comparison of three finite-temperature resummation prescriptions — multi-field partial dressing (PD), Parwani, and Arnold-Espinosa (AE) — applied to classically conformal and non-conformal two-Higgs-doublet models. PD fully retains thermal functions and self-consistently determines scalar masses and mixing via gap equations; Parwani and AE use approximated thermal mass corrections. All comparisons use identical zero-temperature Lagrangian parameters. Gravitational-wave spectra are computed from transition properties (strength α, duration β/H*, wall velocity vw). Path dependence in PD’s potential reconstruction is probed via integration-path variation.
AI.result: In conformal 2HDMs, PD consistently yields stronger, more supercooled transitions (Tp/Tc ≈ 0.5) and larger GW peak amplitudes than Parwani or AE (Tp/Tc ≳ 0.8); non-conformal 2HDMs show no universal ordering, with prescriptions altering thermal history type across large parameter regions. Benchmark comparisons reveal up to ~9 orders-of-magnitude difference in GW peak amplitude and ~50× in peak frequency between PD and AE. PD’s path dependence induces ≤7% shift in transition temperature and ≤3× variation in GW amplitude — smaller than prescription-level differences.
AI.conclusion: Thermal resummation prescription is a dominant source of theoretical uncertainty in predicting electroweak phase transition strength, supercooling, and gravitational-wave observables in multi-scalar BSM scenarios. Multi-field partial dressing provides the most physically complete treatment but reveals intrinsic ambiguities; however, these are subdominant to discrepancies among standard prescriptions. Robust GW forecasts require either prescription convergence or explicit uncertainty quantification tied to resummation methodology.

title: Future avenues for precision oscillation measurements with compact movable reactors
comment: 13 pages main body, 20 pages total, 11 figures Comments are welcome!
summary: No planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on $\thone$. Doing so requires innovative strategies to reduce statistical and systematic uncertainties. In this study, we consider a futuristic program with a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within short distances ($L\lesssim 3\,\km$) from the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) detector. Due to the large fiducial mass of JUNO, even a relatively small reactor can produce a statistically significant number of events over a few years to probe the $\lesssim 8.7\% \,\nuebar$ disappearance set by $\thone$. We consider two possibilities: a $\mathcal{O}(20\mwth)$ microreactor in alcoves of the access tunnel to the underground laboratory, and a $\mathcal{O}(400 \mwth)$ unit on the surface. In both cases the reactor is observed by a small flux monitor detector near the source, while JUNO measures the antineutrino flux at two baselines, suppressing correlated flux and detector systematics. Using the measured Daya Bay per-isotope spectra and its covariance, we model a high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) core for the microreactor and a low-enriched uranium (LEU) core for the surface unit, and discuss various potential sources of systematic uncertainties and their impact on the precision of $\thone$. The underground microreactor could improve on JUNO's reach by a factor of three to four, to $\relsth \simeq 4\%$ over a decade, while the surface reactor would reach the present global-fit precision, $\relsth=2.5\%$, in about three years, provided the emission rate is monitored across reactor relocations to the sub-percent level.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using a movable reactor antineutrino source—either a 20 MWth microreactor underground or a 400 MWth reactor on the surface—near JUNO to significantly improve precision on θ₁₃ beyond Daya Bay’s current limit, leveraging baseline variation and flux monitoring to suppress systematics.
AI.motivation: No planned experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on θ₁₃; innovative strategies are needed to reduce both statistical and systematic uncertainties in measuring reactor antineutrino disappearance.
AI.method: Modeling two movable reactor configurations (underground microreactor and surface reactor) near JUNO; using Daya Bay per-isotope spectra and covariance to simulate HALEU and LEU cores; employing dual-baseline measurements and near-detector flux monitoring to suppress correlated flux and detector systematics.
AI.result: The underground microreactor could reach δsin²2θ₁₃ ≈ 4% in ~10 years (3–4× better than standalone JUNO), while the surface reactor could achieve the current global-fit precision of 2.5% in ~3 years—provided reactor emission is monitored at <1% uncertainty across relocations.
AI.conclusion: A movable reactor source coupled with JUNO’s large fiducial mass and dual-baseline strategy offers a viable path to sub-3% precision on sin²2θ₁₃, overcoming limitations of fixed-source experiments.

title: $Zγ$ production in gluon fusion at NLO+NLL
summary: We study the production of $Z\gamma$ in gluon fusion at hadron colliders at the next-to-leading-order (NLO) in QCD. At the $13.6$ TeV LHC, we find that these NLO corrections are found to enhance the leading-order (LO) cross section by about $83$\% and reduce the conventional seven-point scale uncertainty from $22.3$\% at LO to $15.2$\% at NLO. We further perform the threshold resummation at next-to-leading-logarithmic (NLL) accuracy and match to the fixed order NLO results. We have presented the production cross section for various center of mass energies at the LHC. We find that this NLL resummation enhances the NLO production cross section by about $23$\%. We also give the invariant mass distribution up to $Q=1000$ GeV for $13.6$ TeV LHC. In this case, the resummation reduces the seven-point scale uncertainty from $25\%$ at NLO to about $16$\% at NLO+NLL for $Q=1000$ GeV. We also present the uncertainties due to the strong coupling constant and the parton distribution functions in our results. We further estimate the contribution of the top quark in our predictions, using the Born Improved Theory (BIT).

AI.tldr: This paper computes NLO QCD corrections and NLL threshold resummation for Zγ production in gluon fusion at hadron colliders, finding ~83% NLO K-factor, ~23% NLL enhancement over NLO, and significant reduction in scale uncertainty; it also assesses αs, PDF, and top-quark (BIT) uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical precision for Zγ production in gluon fusion—a loop-induced, electroweak-sensitive process—by computing full NLO QCD corrections and matching with NLL threshold resummation, thereby reducing scale dependence and quantifying parametric uncertainties.
AI.method: Fixed-order NLO QCD calculation in the five-flavor scheme; threshold resummation at NLL accuracy using soft-collinear effective theory (SCET) or Mellin-space formalism; matching of NLL to NLO via additive or multiplicative schemes; seven-point scale variation; PDF and αs uncertainty propagation; Born Improved Theory (BIT) for top-quark mass effects.
AI.result: At 13.6 TeV: NLO enhances LO cross section by ~83%, reduces scale uncertainty from 22.3% to 15.2%; NLL+NLO further enhances NLO by ~23% and reduces scale uncertainty to ~16% at Q = 1000 GeV; invariant mass distributions and uncertainties from αs, PDFs, and top-quark mass (via BIT) are quantified.
AI.conclusion: NLO+ NLL resummation substantially improves predictive precision for Zγ production in gluon fusion, making it a robust probe for BSM physics and SM parameter extraction; inclusion of top-mass effects via BIT is essential for sub-percent level accuracy.

title: Self-gravity depletes superradiant clouds
summary: Superradiant clouds of ultralight scalars around black holes are often modeled as free fields, whose levels grow independently and decay slowly through gravitational-wave emission. We show that this limit is never realized. The cloud's self-gravity redistributes particles between levels, just as in the case of axion self-interactions, and dominates over self-interactions for decay constants $f_a\gtrsim6\times10^{16}\,{\rm GeV}\,(\alpha/0.1)$, with $\alpha$ the gravitational fine-structure constant. Self-gravity depletes the cloud by orders of magnitude and feeds more extended levels, weakening all signals that rely on the existence of a large cloud mass. A binary companion, however, can partly offset the depletion. Any assessment of superradiant signals must therefore account for both self-gravity and the cloud's environment.

AI.tldr: Superradiant scalar clouds around black holes cannot be accurately modeled as free fields due to dominant self-gravitational effects, which redistribute particles among energy levels, deplete the cloud mass, and suppress gravitational-wave signals—especially for large axion decay constants; environmental effects (e.g., binary companions) partially counteract depletion.
AI.motivation: To correct the oversimplified free-field approximation for superradiant scalar clouds by incorporating self-gravity—a previously underestimated effect that fundamentally alters cloud evolution and observational signatures.
AI.method: Analytical and semi-quantitative comparison of timescales for gravitational level redistribution (self-gravity) versus self-interactions and gravitational-wave emission; estimation of particle transfer rates between bound levels and resulting cloud depletion and feeding of extended states.
AI.result: Self-gravity dominates over axion self-interactions for fa ≳ 6×10¹⁶ GeV (α/0.1), causing orders-of-magnitude cloud depletion and enhanced population of higher, more extended levels; binary companions can mitigate depletion but do not restore the free-field picture.
AI.conclusion: The free-field model is physically invalid for realistic superradiant clouds; accurate predictions of gravitational-wave signals, cloud lifetimes, and detection prospects require joint treatment of self-gravity and environmental perturbations.

title: Refractive Neutrino Mass: Effects of Fluctuations of the Dark Matter Field
summary: Observed neutrino oscillations can be reproduced by a refractive neutrino mass-squared arising from interactions with ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM). The wave behaviour of the scalar field gives rise to a fluctuating interference pattern, inducing spatial and temporal variations in the refractive mass that can distort neutrino oscillation probabilities. We simulate the interference patterns of the scalar field in the presence of self-interactions. Using results of these simulations, the oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K experiments are computed. We find that the refractive mass scenario remains viable for the complex scalar field without self-coupling for $m_\phi \lesssim 10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$. For $m_\phi\gtrsim10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$, repulsive self-interactions narrow the density distribution, reducing the deviation of the survival probability at the first minimum to $\Delta P \approx 0.07$ for an appropriate self-interaction coupling. In contrast, for a real scalar field, rapid oscillations with the Compton frequency distort the probabilities for scalar masses $ 10^{-22}~\mathrm{eV} \lesssim m_\phi \lesssim 10^{-10} ~\mathrm{eV}$, and self-interactions do not remove this distortion. This distortion becomes negligible only for $m_\phi\gtrsim10^{-9}~\mathrm{eV}$. We explore additional effects which could modify the interference pattern and relax the constraints on the required values of $m_\phi$. These include scenarios with multiple scalar fields (the axiverse), the gravitational effects of the Sun and Earth on the granule structure, and interactions with the relic neutrino background.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM) can generate a refractive neutrino mass-squared via wave-like interference, thereby modifying neutrino oscillation probabilities; it assesses viability across scalar field types (complex vs. real), self-interaction strengths, and mass ranges, and examines astrophysical/environmental effects that may relax constraints on ULDM mass m_ϕ.
AI.motivation: To explain observed neutrino oscillations through a novel mechanism—refractive mass induced by ultralight scalar dark matter—and to determine observational constraints on ULDM parameters (mass m_ϕ, self-coupling, field type) using current experiments (JUNO, T2K).
AI.method: Simulated ULDM scalar field interference patterns including self-interactions; computed resulting neutrino oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K; compared deviations in survival probability (especially at first minimum) for complex vs. real scalar fields; analyzed additional physical effects (axiverse, gravitational lensing by Sun/Earth, relic neutrino background).
AI.result: Complex scalar ULDM without self-coupling remains viable only for m_ϕ ≲ 10⁻¹⁶ eV; repulsive self-interactions narrow density distribution and reduce survival probability deviation to ΔP ≈ 0.07 for m_ϕ ≳ 10⁻¹⁶ eV. Real scalar ULDM causes Compton-frequency distortions for 10⁻²² eV ≲ m_ϕ ≲ 10⁻¹⁰ eV, unaffected by self-interactions; distortion vanishes only for m_ϕ ≳ 10⁻⁹ eV. Axiverse, gravitational effects, and relic neutrino interactions may relax m_ϕ constraints.
AI.conclusion: ULDM-induced refractive neutrino mass is a viable oscillation-modifying mechanism, but stringent mass-dependent constraints arise from experimentally measurable distortions; field type and self-interactions critically affect phenomenology, and environmental/astrophysical corrections could broaden allowed parameter space.

title: Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications: From Circles to Strings
summary: This review is written with a simple question in mind: what does one need to know to enter the literature on Scherk-Schwarz compactifications? It is organized as a sequence of questions that a graduate student might naturally ask, together with the concepts, calculations, and formal tools needed to work through the literature. The discussion starts at an elementary field-theory level and gradually develops toward more advanced aspects of supergravity, orbifolds, quantum effects, and string theory. Phenomenological applications are deliberately left aside.

AI.tldr: A pedagogical review guiding graduate students through foundational to advanced concepts in Scherk-Schwarz compactifications, structured as a Q&A progression—from elementary field theory to supergravity, orbifolds, quantum effects, and string theory—excluding phenomenology.
AI.motivation: To provide a structured, accessible entry point into the technical literature on Scherk-Schwarz compactifications for graduate students.
AI.method: Pedagogical exposition organized as a sequence of progressively sophisticated questions, accompanied by requisite concepts, calculations, and formal tools—from classical field theory to quantum and string-theoretic frameworks.
AI.result: A coherent conceptual roadmap covering symmetry breaking via twisted boundary conditions, dimensional reduction in supergravity, orbifold projections, one-loop corrections, and embedding in string theory.
AI.conclusion: Scherk-Schwarz compactifications require mastery of twisted boundary conditions, consistent truncation, anomaly cancellation, and modular invariance; this review synthesizes prerequisites across energy scales while deliberately omitting phenomenological model-building.

title: Upper Bounds on the Radion Mass in a Warped Extra Dimension
summary:
We study absolute upper bounds on the mass ratio $R_{11}=m_{r_1}/m_{h_1}$ between the radion ($r_1$) and graviton ($h_1$) lightest modes in five dimensional warped models. We consider warped models with an admissible singular behavior in the infrared: i.e.~models with power-like ($\sim  ar\phi^{2n}$) and with exponential ($\sim e^{2
u ar\phi}$) bulk potentials, where $ ar\phi$ is the stabilizing bulk field. We find a correlation between $R_{11}$ and the singular behavior of the Ricci scalar, which allows to establish an absolute upper bound on the former. For the power-like models, the maximum value of $R_{11}$ increases with $n$. In the limit $n	o\infty$, the power-like model reproduces the exponential model and reaches the same upper bound as the latter. For the exponential model, we derive analytically the bound $R_{11}<1$, with the largest value approached for the case $
u	o 1^+$ (where $
u=1$ corresponds to the linear dilaton model) and consistent with unitarity sum rules. For exponential models we also obtain the absolute upper bound on the second radion mode ratio $R_{21}=m_{r_2}/m_{h_1}\lesssim 1.374$. This value is reached for $
u=2$ when the IR brane approaches the singularity. For this configuration, we verify that the scalar contribution satisfies the unitarity sum rule when the complete radion Kaluza-Klein tower is included.

AI.tldr: This paper derives absolute upper bounds on mass ratios between radion and graviton Kaluza–Klein modes in 5D warped models with IR singularities, showing R₁₁ < 1 for exponential bulk potentials and linking bounds to Ricci scalar singularity behavior and unitarity.
AI.motivation: To establish model-independent, absolute upper bounds on radion–graviton mass ratios in warped 5D scenarios with IR singularities—motivated by consistency with unitarity, stability, and the need to constrain beyond-Standard-Model parameter space in extra-dimensional theories.
AI.method: Analytical derivation using warped geometry with stabilizing bulk scalar field; classification of IR-regular singular behaviors (power-law ∼ϕ̄^{2n} and exponential ∼e^{2νϕ̄} potentials); computation of KK spectra; analysis of Ricci scalar divergence; enforcement of unitarity sum rules for scattering amplitudes involving radion towers.
AI.result: For exponential models: R₁₁ = m_{r₁}/m_{h₁} < 1 (saturated as ν → 1⁺); R₂₁ = m_{r₂}/m_{h₁} ≲ 1.374 (achieved at ν = 2 with IR brane at singularity); power-law models yield increasing R₁₁ with n, converging to same R₁₁ < 1 bound as n → ∞; correlation between R₁₁ and Ricci scalar singularity strength is established.
AI.conclusion: The radion–graviton mass hierarchy is fundamentally bounded from above in physically admissible warped models with IR singularities; the universal bound R₁₁ < 1 for exponential potentials—and its convergence from power-law cases—reflects deep geometric and unitarity constraints, providing a robust phenomenological constraint for collider and gravitational-wave searches of light radions.

title: Equation of state of hot and dense QCD at the physical point via the complex Langevin equation
comment: Proceeding for the 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice 2026), July 26 to August 1, 2026, University of Maryland, College Park, USA; 6 pages, 2 figures
summary: This study presents the first results for the equation of state of 2+1+1-flavor QCD at the physical point, obtained using the complex Langevin equation. We calculate continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic quantities, such as the baryon density, pressure, the speed of sound and the adiabatic compressibility. The simulations are performed in the isospin-symmetric, strangeness- and charm-neutral setting above the crossover temperature and at unprecedentedly large baryon chemical potentials.

AI.tldr: First continuum-extrapolated equation of state for physical 2+1+1-flavor QCD using complex Langevin method, covering high baryon chemical potentials above crossover temperature.
AI.motivation: To compute the QCD equation of state at the physical quark mass point with nonzero baryon chemical potential, where conventional Monte Carlo methods fail due to the sign problem.
AI.method: Complex Langevin simulation of 2+1+1-flavor QCD; continuum extrapolation of thermodynamic observables including baryon density, pressure, speed of sound, and adiabatic compressibility; isospin-symmetric, strangeness- and charm-neutral ensemble above the chiral crossover temperature.
AI.result: First physically realistic, continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic quantities for QCD at large baryon chemical potentials; successful stabilization and convergence of complex Langevin for this regime.
AI.conclusion: Complex Langevin enables first-principles computation of the QCD equation of state at the physical point and large μ_B, opening access to high-density QCD thermodynamics relevant for neutron star interiors and heavy-ion collisions.

title: Worldsheet Effective Theory of Abelian-Higgs Cosmic Strings beyond Nambu--Goto
comment: 26 pages (13 for main text, 13 for appendices). 8 figures (6 in main text). Movies of the simulations can be found in this https URL and this https URL . Comments are welcome
summary: Cosmic strings can support long-lived excitations confined to their cores, opening channels for energy exchange with the transverse Goldstone modes that describe the string's motion. We derive a covariant worldsheet theory of their coupled dynamics directly from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, with all interaction coefficients fixed by the microscopic theory. The resulting action, which we validate against numerical lattice field theory simulations, extends the Nambu--Goto description to include a massive scalar shape mode and a massive vector mode. Dualizing the vector reveals a geometric distinction: the shape scalar mode couples to intrinsic worldsheet curvature, while the pseudoscalar couples to normal bundle curvature. These interactions explain the distinct parametric instabilities observed in lattice simulations and predict how the relative polarization of colliding transverse waves controls the excitation of the two internal modes. Our results connect microscopic string structure to the nonlinear worldsheet dynamics, providing a predictive framework for cosmic strings beyond the Nambu--Goto approximation.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a covariant worldsheet theory for cosmic strings with internal excitations—massive scalar (shape) and vector modes—from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling; it identifies distinct geometric couplings (intrinsic vs. normal bundle curvature) and explains parametric instabilities and polarization-dependent mode excitation observed in lattice simulations.
AI.motivation: To go beyond the Nambu–Goto approximation by incorporating microscopic string structure—specifically long-lived core-confined excitations—and their coupling to transverse Goldstone modes, thereby explaining observed nonlinear dynamics and instabilities in cosmic strings.
AI.method: Derivation of a covariant worldsheet effective action directly from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling; dualization of the massive vector mode; validation against numerical lattice field theory simulations; geometric analysis of curvature couplings.
AI.result: A complete worldsheet action including a massive scalar shape mode and a massive vector mode; dualization reveals the scalar couples to intrinsic curvature while the pseudoscalar (dual vector) couples to normal bundle curvature; these couplings explain parametric instabilities and predict polarization-dependent excitation of internal modes during wave collisions.
AI.conclusion: The derived framework bridges microscopic field-theoretic structure and nonlinear worldsheet dynamics, enabling quantitative predictions for cosmic string behavior beyond the Nambu–Goto limit.

title: Equilibrium relativistic spin magnetohydrodynamics from chiral kinetic theory
summary: We develop a microscopic and thermodynamically consistent framework for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics of massless chiral fermions, directly from first-order chiral kinetic theory. Starting from the covariant Wigner function, we recast the chiral kinetic equation as a pure streaming equation on a magnetically shifted mass shell, incorporating both the magnetic-moment energy and the Berry-curvature phase-space measure. This formulation yields a kinetic $H$-theorem and an entropy current with vanishing divergence in global equilibrium. We construct the equilibrium distribution for an arbitrary spin frame and derive the associated currents, energy--momentum tensor, spin tensor, entropy current, and frame-independent spin polarization, including the magnetic splitting between particles and antiparticles. Thermodynamic consistency further determines the second-order magnetovortical responses, revealing a relativistic Barnett magnetization, a temperature- and chemical-potential-independent anomalous charge density, and rotation-induced density corrections that reproduce exact field-theory results. Our framework provides a unified microscopic foundation for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics and establishes a direct link between quantum kinetic theory, spin polarization, magnetization, and anomalous transport.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a thermodynamically consistent relativistic spin magnetohydrodynamic framework for massless chiral fermions from first-order chiral kinetic theory, using the covariant Wigner function to reformulate the kinetic equation on a magnetically shifted mass shell; it derives equilibrium currents, spin polarization, and second-order magnetovortical responses—including relativistic Barnett magnetization and anomalous charge density—while ensuring entropy conservation and linking quantum kinetics to macroscopic spin and transport phenomena.
AI.motivation: To establish a microscopic, thermodynamically consistent foundation for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics of chiral fermions, bridging chiral kinetic theory, spin polarization, magnetization, and anomalous transport.
AI.method: Derives the chiral kinetic equation from the covariant Wigner function, recasts it as a pure streaming equation on a magnetically shifted mass shell incorporating magnetic-moment energy and Berry curvature in phase-space measure; constructs equilibrium distribution in arbitrary spin frame; computes conserved currents (energy–momentum, spin, entropy) and frame-independent spin polarization; imposes thermodynamic consistency to fix second-order magnetovortical transport coefficients.
AI.result: A kinetic H-theorem and divergenceless entropy current in global equilibrium; explicit expressions for equilibrium spin polarization, magnetization (including relativistic Barnett effect), temperature- and chemical-potential-independent anomalous charge density, and rotation-induced density corrections matching exact field-theory results.
AI.conclusion: The framework unifies quantum kinetic theory with relativistic spin hydrodynamics, provides a rigorous basis for spin-dependent transport in chiral plasmas, and establishes direct connections among Berry curvature, spin polarization, magnetization, and anomalous responses in thermal equilibrium.

title: Cardinal RG=GR: Phase-Space Cardinality and the Cosmological Constant and Hierarchy Problems
summary: The effective field theory approach constructs the low-energy theory by integrating out fluctuations above an ultraviolet scale which raises the cosmological constant and hierarchy problems. We investigate an alternative prescription in which the quantum theory is restricted to a finite accessible region of phase space, characterized by a dimensionless cardinality $\mathcal N$, rather than by independently prescribed spacetime and momentum scales. At fixed cardinality these scales are related. For Euclidean de Sitter space, the stationarity condition for the gravitational action can then be written as a stationarity condition with respect to the momentum scale, a relation which we call Cardinal RG=GR. We demonstrate the relation between $\mathcal N$ and the Gibbons-Hawking entropy of de Sitter space, compute the cosmological constant proportional to ${1}/{\sqrt{\mathcal N}}$, show that it is radiatively stable and apply the same prescription to demonstrate the radiative stability of the mass parameter for a simple interacting scalar field model, thereby illuminating the resolution of the hierarchy problem. We also establish a precise limit, involving gravitational data, in which the conventional results of Quantum Field Theory and the Renormalization Group are recovered.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a cardinality-based regularization of quantum field theory in de Sitter space, replacing traditional UV cutoffs with a finite phase-space dimensionality 𝒩; it links 𝒩 to Gibbons-Hawking entropy, yields a radiatively stable cosmological constant ∝ 1/√𝒩, resolves the hierarchy problem via Cardinal RG=GR, and recovers standard QFT/RG in a well-defined gravitational limit.
AI.motivation: To resolve the cosmological constant and electroweak hierarchy problems inherent in effective field theory, which arise from uncontrolled UV sensitivity due to independent spacetime and momentum cutoffs.
AI.method: Replaces conventional UV cutoffs with a finite, dimensionless phase-space cardinality 𝒩; imposes stationarity of the gravitational action w.r.t. momentum scale (Cardinal RG = GR) in Euclidean de Sitter space; computes Λ and scalar mass stability using this constraint; derives recovery limit of standard QFT/RG via gravitational data.
AI.result: Λ ∝ 1/√𝒩, radiatively stable; 𝒩 equals Gibbons-Hawking entropy S_{GH}; scalar mass parameter is similarly stabilized; Cardinal RG=GR reproduces GR dynamics; standard QFT/RG emerges in the limit where gravitational contributions to phase-space counting become negligible.
AI.conclusion: Phase-space cardinality 𝒩 provides a physically motivated, UV-finite regulator that intrinsically ties geometry and quantum degrees of freedom, yielding radiative stability for both Λ and particle masses—offering a geometric resolution to fine-tuning problems without new symmetries or dynamics.

title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
summary: We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows: 1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar interactions exists at all orders, represented by a finite number of effective even forms. 3. The higher-derivative contact-term sector can be constructed from a finite set of basic tensor structures using polynomials in derivative symbols. We introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity considerations.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond couplings on Dp-branes using scattering amplitudes involving RR states, gauge fields, and transverse scalars; it proposes novel pullback and Chern-Simons transgression operators (P∞ and T∞) and puts forward three structural conjectures about finiteness, even-form representations, and tensor-structure generation of contact terms.
AI.motivation: To systematically classify and resolve the infinite tower of higher-derivative RR couplings on Dp-branes—beyond standard Myers/Taylor expansions—by leveraging amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as fundamental physical data.
AI.method: Analyzes the full low-energy expansion of the scattering amplitude of one closed-string RR state, one gauge field, and two transverse scalars on a Dp-brane; constructs a higher-class pullback operator P∞ and mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators T∞; employs equivalence relations and characteristic-form reasoning to constrain effective couplings.
AI.result: Identifies infinite massless poles and non-standard local terms in the amplitude expansion; establishes that effective couplings at fixed field content and derivative order span a finite-dimensional space; proposes existence of an all-order family of mixed RR–gauge–scalar interactions representable by finitely many even-degree effective forms; shows contact-term sector is generated from finitely many basic tensors via polynomials in derivatives.
AI.conclusion: The amplitude-based approach reveals intrinsic finiteness and algebraic structure in higher-derivative RR couplings; the conjectured operators P∞ and T∞, together with the three structural conjectures, provide a unified, physically grounded classification scheme beyond conventional supergravity or DBI-inspired expansions.

title: Review of Pion and Nucleon Gluon Parton Distribution Functions from Lattice QCD
comment: 28 pages, 8 figures, invited review of gluon PDFs from the lattice for Particles
summary: Gluons play an essential role in the strong interaction that binds quarks into hadrons, as described by quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Understanding how the fundamental dynamics of QCD give rise to hadron structure remains one of the outstanding challenges in nuclear and particle physics. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide a successful framework for describing high-energy scattering processes involving hadrons. However, our knowledge of gluon PDFs remains comparatively limited because of the experimental challenges associated with directly constraining the gluon structure of hadrons. In recent years, a major breakthrough has enabled the calculation of the Bjorken-$x$ dependence of PDFs directly from lattice QCD. Among the available approaches, the large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) and pseudo-PDF frameworks have emerged as the most widely used methods and have produced the majority of lattice determinations of parton distributions. These developments have sparked rapid progress in first-principles studies of the $x$-dependent structure of hadrons, including gluon PDFs of the nucleon and pseudoscalar mesons. In this review, we summarize recent advances in lattice QCD calculations of gluon PDFs {using the LaMET and pseudo-PDF methods}, discuss the current status and impacts of these developments, and highlight the remaining challenges and future opportunities.

AI.tldr: This review summarizes recent lattice QCD advances—particularly via LaMET and pseudo-PDF frameworks—in computing the x-dependent gluon parton distribution functions (PDFs) of hadrons, discusses current achievements and limitations, and outlines open challenges and future directions.
AI.motivation: The gluon PDF is poorly constrained experimentally due to lack of direct probes; first-principles theoretical access via lattice QCD is thus critical for understanding hadron structure in QCD.
AI.method: Large-Momentum Effective Theory (LaMET) and pseudo-PDF frameworks applied to lattice QCD simulations to extract x-dependent gluon PDFs of nucleons and pseudoscalar mesons.
AI.result: First ab initio, x-resolved gluon PDFs from lattice QCD have been obtained, marking significant progress beyond global fits; results show qualitative agreement with phenomenological extractions but with sizable uncertainties and systematic effects.
AI.conclusion: LaMET and pseudo-PDF methods have enabled the first direct lattice calculations of gluon PDFs, advancing our understanding of hadronic structure from QCD fundamentals; however, controlling discretization, renormalization, higher-twist, and excited-state effects remains challenging.

title: Inhomogeneous Cutoff Regularization of Loops in Cosmological Correlators
summary: We revisit the use of cutoff regularization in computing loop corrections to cosmological correlators. We argue that a cutoff corresponding to a fixed physical scale must be defined with respect to the local background geometry. In the presence of superhorizon perturbations, this is naturally implemented within the separate universe picture, where different local patches are regulated at the same physical scale. Expanding this cutoff in the long-wavelength background generates a series of regulator-induced contributions to loop amplitudes, which admit a diagrammatic interpretation as long-mode insertions on the corresponding loop contractions. Our cutoff prescription preserves residual spatial dilatations and volume-preserving anisotropic rescalings. It is therefore particularly relevant for loop correlators with soft external modes. We illustrate the mechanism by computing the contributions to the one-loop scalar and tensor power spectra on superhorizon scales. In both cases, the additional corrections induced by the inhomogeneous cutoff cancel the ultraviolet boundary terms arising in the ordinary diagrams. These calculations establish, within cutoff regularization, the late-time constancy of both power spectra and clarify its physical origin. We then investigate the squeezed one-loop scalar bispectrum and show that the additional cutoff contributions are essential for satisfying the consistency relation at finite cutoff. Finally, we discuss the role of the inhomogeneous cutoff in the late-time constancy of the one-loop bispectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits cutoff regularization for loop corrections to cosmological correlators, proposing a physically motivated, background-dependent cutoff that respects residual symmetries and ensures consistency with soft theorems and late-time constancy of power spectra and bispectra.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguities in standard cutoff regularization when applied to cosmological perturbation theory—particularly on superhorizon scales where background inhomogeneity affects UV regulation—and to ensure compatibility with symmetries (e.g., residual dilatations) and consistency relations.
AI.method: Introduces an inhomogeneous physical-scale cutoff defined locally with respect to the background geometry within the separate universe framework; expands the cutoff in long-wavelength perturbations to generate regulator-induced contributions interpretable as long-mode insertions; computes one-loop scalar/tensor power spectra and squeezed bispectrum while preserving spatial dilatation and volume-preserving anisotropic rescaling symmetries.
AI.result: The inhomogeneous cutoff cancels UV boundary terms in ordinary loop diagrams, ensuring late-time constancy of scalar and tensor power spectra; it is essential for satisfying the scalar consistency relation at finite cutoff; and it underpins the late-time constancy of the one-loop bispectrum.
AI.conclusion: A geometrically consistent, background-adapted cutoff regularization is necessary and sufficient to maintain symmetry constraints, soft limits, and physical observability (e.g., time-independence) of loop-level cosmological correlators.

title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
summary: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For tensor-to-scalar ratios near current observational limits, detectability is incompatible with, or pushes against, the regime of validity of these UV completions. A detectable signal can remain possible for a sufficiently small tensor-to-scalar ratio, but only at the cost of an extremely large enhancement of the TSS vertex. Thus, while a future search for large scale parity violation is worth pursuing, generating a detectable signal within a consistent effective theory is highly nontrivial.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether detectable large-scale parity violation in the Universe can arise from inflationary dynamics involving the Chern-Simons operator in UV-complete theories (e.g., fermionic, string-theoretic), and finds it strongly constrained by current bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum — detectability requires either unphysically small r or extreme, likely inconsistent, TSS vertex enhancement.
AI.motivation: To assess whether large-scale cosmic parity violation—suggested by four-point function analyses and potentially generated via the dynamical Chern-Simons operator during inflation—can be realized consistently in realistic UV completions.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological analysis of parity-odd trispectrum generation in UV-complete models (fermionic couplings, string-inspired scenarios), incorporating observational constraints from the TSS bispectrum and consistency requirements of effective field theory (EFT validity).
AI.result: Existing TSS bispectrum bounds severely limit detectable parity-odd trispectra; for r near current limits (r ≲ 0.03), detectability conflicts with EFT validity; viable detection requires either r ≪ 0.01 or an implausibly large TSS coupling violating perturbativity or unitarity.
AI.conclusion: Generating a detectable large-scale parity-violating signal within a consistent, UV-complete effective theory is highly nontrivial; while observationally worthwhile, theoretical realizability faces strong tension between detectability, EFT validity, and naturalness.

title: Charm and beauty production in pp collisions with ALICE
comment: Proceedings of the 13th International Conference on Hard and Electromagnetic Probes of High-Energy Nuclear Collisions (Hard Probes 2026, HP2026), 22 - 26 June 2026, Vanderbilt University. 4 pages, 3 figures
summary: Measurements of charm and beauty production in proton--proton (pp) collisions provide crucial tests of perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) and unique access to heavy-quark hadronisation. In this contribution, a selection of recent ALICE results, with emphasis on LHC Run 3 measurements, is presented. The transverse-momentum-differential production cross sections of prompt D mesons at $\sqrt{s}=5.36$ and 13.6 TeV and of fully reconstructed B mesons at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV are discussed together with comparisons to theoretical calculations. The rapidity dependence of charm and beauty production and the $\rm D^{*+}/D^0$ and $\rm \Lambda_c^+/D^0$ yield ratios provide complementary constraints on heavy-quark production and hadronisation. Measurements of the fractions of ${\rm J}/\psi$ and $\psi({\rm 2S})$ originating from beauty-hadron decays, and of the inclusive $\psi({\rm 2S})$-to-${\rm J}/\psi$ production ratio, further constrain the interplay between perturbative heavy-quark production and non-perturbative bound-state formation.

AI.tldr: This paper presents recent ALICE measurements of charm and beauty production in pp collisions at LHC Run 3 energies (5.36 and 13.6 TeV), focusing on differential cross sections, rapidity dependence, hadronisation ratios (e.g., D*/D⁰, Λc⁺/D⁰), and J/ψ and ψ(2S) production mechanisms—including fractions from beauty decays and the ψ(2S)/J/ψ ratio—to test pQCD and constrain heavy-quark hadronisation.
AI.motivation: To test perturbative QCD predictions and probe non-perturbative heavy-quark hadronisation mechanisms via precision measurements of charm and beauty production in pp collisions.
AI.method: Analysis of proton–proton collision data from LHC Run 3 using ALICE detector; measurement of transverse-momentum-differential cross sections for prompt D mesons (at √s = 5.36 and 13.6 TeV) and fully reconstructed B mesons (at √s = 13.6 TeV); extraction of rapidity dependence, hadronisation-sensitive yield ratios (D*/D⁰, Λc⁺/D⁰), and charmonium production fractions (J/ψ, ψ(2S)) including beauty feed-down contributions.
AI.result: New high-precision cross sections for D and B mesons; constraints on rapidity dependence of c/b production; improved determination of D*/D⁰ and Λc⁺/D⁰ ratios; quantified fractions of J/ψ and ψ(2S) from beauty-hadron decays; updated inclusive ψ(2S)/J/ψ ratio—collectively providing tighter constraints on pQCD calculations and hadronisation models.
AI.conclusion: The results significantly advance tests of pQCD and provide unique insights into heavy-quark hadronisation dynamics; the Run 3 data, with enhanced statistics and extended kinematic coverage, improve discrimination among theoretical models, especially those describing quark-to-hadron transition and charmonium formation mechanisms.

title: Observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay $J/ψ\rightarrow μ^+ μ^- η$
summary: Using a data sample of $(8.998 \pm 0.039)\times10^9$ $J/\psi$ events collected by the BESIII detector at BEPCII, we report the observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay $J/\psi \to \mu^+ \mu^- \eta$ for the first time, with a statistical significance greater than 10$\sigma$. The branching fraction is measured to be $\mathcal{B}(J/\psi \to \mu^+ \mu^- \eta) = (3.05 \pm 0.14_{\rm stat.} \pm 0.13_{\rm syst.})\times 10^{-6}$. The ratio of this branching fraction to that of the corresponding radiative decay $J/\psi \to \gamma\eta$ is determined to be $\mathcal{B}(J/\psi \to \mu^+\mu^-\eta)/\mathcal{B}(J/\psi \to \gamma\eta) = (2.80 \pm 0.18) \times 10^{-3}$. Combining this result with the previous BESIII measurement of the $J/\psi \to e^+e^-\eta$ branching fraction yields $\mathcal{B}(J/\psi \to \mu^+\mu^-\eta)/\mathcal{B}(J/\psi \to e^+e^-\eta) = 0.219 \pm 0.020$. These results are consistent with the theoretical predictions based on the vector meson dominance model.

AI.tldr: First observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay J/ψ → μ⁺μ⁻η with >10σ significance; branching fraction measured as (3.05 ± 0.14_stat ± 0.13_syst)×10⁻⁶; ratios to J/ψ → γη and J/ψ → e⁺e⁻η are consistent with vector meson dominance predictions.
AI.motivation: To test QCD-inspired models—particularly vector meson dominance (VMD)—via precision measurement of rare electromagnetic Dalitz decays of charmonium, where lepton flavor universality and internal structure of J/ψ can be probed through comparisons of μ⁺μ⁻η and e⁺e⁻η channels.
AI.method: Analysis of (8.998 ± 0.039)×10⁹ J/ψ events collected with the BESIII detector at BEPCII; full reconstruction of J/ψ → μ⁺μ⁻η using charged track and neutral shower identification; background suppression via kinematic fits, mass constraints, and sideband subtraction; systematic uncertainties evaluated from tracking efficiency, particle ID, photon detection, and fit bias.
AI.result: First observation of J/ψ → μ⁺μ⁻η (>10σ); ℬ(J/ψ → μ⁺μ⁻η) = (3.05 ± 0.14_stat ± 0.13_syst)×10⁻⁶; ℬ(J/ψ → μ⁺μ⁻η)/ℬ(J/ψ → γη) = (2.80 ± 0.18)×10⁻³; ℬ(J/ψ → μ⁺μ⁻η)/ℬ(J/ψ → e⁺e⁻η) = 0.219 ± 0.020.
AI.conclusion: The measured branching fraction and ratios are in agreement with vector meson dominance model expectations, supporting its validity for low-energy electromagnetic transitions in charmonium and confirming lepton universality within current precision.

title: A Surrogate Detector Model for the MINERvA Open Dataset
summary: The growing availability of open neutrino data promises broader scrutiny of interaction models, but a critical barrier remains: mapping theoretical predictions into reconstructed observables, which previously required computationally intensive methods inaccessible outside the original experimental collaborations. In this work, we present a probabilistic surrogate of the MINERvA detector response, trained on an open simulation dataset to map generator-level final-state particles and interaction geometry to reconstructed observables, without relying on generator-specific interaction labels. We assess its fidelity through conditional response distributions, reconstructed observables, and classifier-based closure tests. We further demonstrate generalization beyond the limitations of conventional phase-space-dependent reweighting by withholding two-particle-two-hole interactions entirely from training and showing that the surrogate reproduces their reconstructed response within the estimated uncertainties. In an end-to-end application to MINERvA charged-current inclusive muon-neutrino data, we reproduce selection efficiencies and purities and forward-fold predictions from GENIE, NuWro, and GiBUU for direct comparison with measurements. By moving theoretical predictions into reconstructed space rather than unfolding the data, this work establishes a reusable interface between neutrino interaction models and experimental observations, expanding the scope of physics accessible through open datasets.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a probabilistic surrogate model for the MINERvA detector response, trained on open simulation data to map generator-level neutrino interactions to reconstructed observables—enabling direct comparison of multiple interaction generators (GENIE, NuWro, GiBUU) with real data without unfolding.
AI.motivation: To overcome the computational and accessibility barrier in mapping theoretical neutrino interaction predictions to reconstructed experimental observables, especially for open-data analysis outside original collaborations.
AI.method: Trained a probabilistic surrogate model on an open MINERvA simulation dataset to learn the mapping from generator-level final-state particles and interaction geometry to reconstructed observables; evaluated using conditional response distributions, reconstructed-variable comparisons, classifier-based closure tests, and generalization tests (e.g., withholding 2p2h events); applied end-to-end to CC inclusive muon-neutrino data.
AI.result: The surrogate accurately reproduces selection efficiencies/purities and forward-folds predictions from GENIE, NuWro, and GiBUU into reconstructed space, matching measurements; it generalizes to unseen 2p2h interactions within uncertainties; passes closure tests and preserves detector-response fidelity.
AI.conclusion: The surrogate provides a reusable, generator-agnostic interface that shifts the paradigm from data unfolding to theory forward-folding, thereby enabling broader, more transparent, and collaborative validation of neutrino interaction models using open data.

title: Progress in measurements of the CKM angle $γ$ and charm mixing at LHCb
comment: All figures and tables, along with any supplementary material and additional information, are available at this https URL (LHCb public pages)
summary: Measurements of the CKM angle $\gamma$ and of the charm mixing and $C\!P$-violation parameters enable stringent and complementary tests of the weak sector of the Standard Model. The two categories of measurements are intimately related, since they both depend on hadronic parameters of $D^0$ meson decays, and knowledge of charm mixing is required to determine $\gamma$. The progress made in these sectors at the LHCb experiment is reviewed, and a new simultaneous combination of all relevant LHCb measurements is presented. The combination includes measurements based on data collected during 2011-2018, as well as the first measurement of $\gamma$ with data collected in 2024. The results, $\gamma = (63.2^{+2.3}_{-2.2})^{\circ}$ modulo $180^{\circ}$, $x_{12} = (4.2^{+0.4}_{-0.5})\times10^{-3}$, $y_{12} = (6.18^{+0.17}_{-0.18})\times10^{-3}$, $\phi^M_2 = (4^{+11}_{-10})\,\mathrm{mrad}$ and $\phi^{\Gamma}_2 = (19^{+23}_{-24})\,\mathrm{mrad}$, are the most precise to date. The $CP$ asymmetries in $D^0\to K^+K^-$ and $D^0\to\pi^+\pi^-$ decays are also determined under different theoretical assumptions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the most precise simultaneous combination of LHCb measurements of the CKM angle γ and charm mixing/CP-violation parameters using data from 2011–2018 and the first 2024 measurement; results include γ = (63.2⁺²·³₋₂.₂)° mod 180°, x₁₂ = (4.2⁺⁰·⁴₋₀.₅)×10⁻³, y₁₂ = (6.18⁺⁰·¹⁷₋₀.₁₈)×10⁻³, and CP-violating phases φ^M₂ and φ^Γ₂.
AI.motivation: To perform stringent, complementary tests of the weak sector of the Standard Model via precise determinations of the CKM angle γ and charm mixing/CP-violation parameters — both relying on shared hadronic D⁰ decay inputs and requiring consistent treatment due to interdependence.
AI.method: Simultaneous statistical combination of all relevant LHCb measurements — including time-dependent and time-integrated analyses of B→DK, B→Dπ, D→Kπ, D→KK/ππ decays — using data from 2011–2018 and incorporating the first 2024 γ measurement; constraints from charm mixing parameters (x₁₂, y₁₂, φ^M₂, φ^Γ₂) are consistently included in the fit.
AI.result: γ = (63.2⁺²·³₋₂.₂)° mod 180°, x₁₂ = (4.2⁺⁰·⁴₋₀.₅)×10⁻³, y₁₂ = (6.18⁺⁰·¹⁷₋₀.₁₈)×10⁻³, φ^M₂ = (4⁺¹¹₋₁₀) mrad, φ^Γ₂ = (19⁺²³₋₂₄) mrad — all the most precise values to date; also reports CP asymmetries in D⁰→K⁺K⁻ and D⁰→π⁺π⁻ under varied theoretical assumptions.
AI.conclusion: The combined analysis significantly improves precision on γ and charm mixing/CPV parameters, reinforcing SM consistency while narrowing room for New Physics contributions in the up-quark sector; the methodology demonstrates robust handling of correlated hadronic uncertainties across both measurement categories.

title: Another relation among the neutrino mass-squared differences?
comment: 12 pages, 1 table. Version accepted by JHEP. v3: added subsection on applicability, minor text clarifications, and updated references
summary: Determining the absolute neutrino mass scale remains a compelling challenge in particle physics. Establishing precise mathematical connections among the neutrino masses could significantly facilitate this task and shed additional light on the underlying mass-generation mechanism. We highlight the possible existence of a simple algebraic relation between the mass-squared differences, $$\frac{\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{31}}+\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{21}}}{\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{31}}-\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{21}}}=\sqrt{2},$$ which agrees remarkably well with the best-fit values of recent global analyses of neutrino oscillation data. We then investigate the implications of adopting this relation and how it decreases the number of independent parameters in the neutrino sector. We demonstrate that there are alternative representations well known in quark and charged-lepton physics. Furthermore, we place a tight constraint on the solar neutrino mass splitting, $\Delta m^2_{21}=(7.445 \pm 0.062) \times 10^{-5} \text{ eV}^2$, and also obtain $\Delta m^2_{31}=(2.548 \pm 0.041) \times 10^{-3} \text{ eV}^2$. Next-generation reactor and accelerator neutrino experiments are expected to significantly reduce systematic uncertainties. In particular, the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) will measure these parameters independently of each other at the sub-percent level, thereby providing a stringent and direct test of our results.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a simple algebraic relation between neutrino mass-squared differences that fits current data well, reduces model parameters, yields precise predictions for Δm²₂₁ and Δm²₃₁, and is testable at JUNO.
AI.motivation: To constrain the absolute neutrino mass scale and uncover underlying mass-generation mechanisms by identifying exact mathematical relations among neutrino mass-squared differences.
AI.method: Analytical derivation and phenomenological analysis of an algebraic relation linking √Δm²₃₁ and √Δm²₂₁; consistency check with global oscillation data; parameter counting and comparison to quark/lepton analogs; error propagation for predicted splittings.
AI.result: A relation (√Δm²₃₁ + √Δm²₂₁)/(√Δm²₃₁ − √Δm²₂₁) = √2 is shown to be consistent with best-fit data; it predicts Δm²₂₁ = (7.445 ± 0.062) × 10⁻⁵ eV² and Δm²₃₁ = (2.548 ± 0.041) × 10⁻³ eV²; reduces independent neutrino mass parameters; admits representations analogous to quark/charged-lepton sectors.
AI.conclusion: The proposed relation offers a predictive, testable simplification of the neutrino mass spectrum, potentially pointing to a deeper symmetry or flavor structure; its validity will be decisively probed by sub-percent measurements from JUNO.

title: Testing the D234 Dirac operator
comment: 21 pages + 2 appendices and references; 10 figures, 2 tables
summary: We study a version of the so-called D234 fermion action. On top of non-perturbative improvement to $\mathcal{O}(a)$, this action is also tree-level improved at $\mathcal{O}(a^2)$. The version we consider also has gauge links smoothed with one level of stout smearing and the clover term in its exponentiated form. Working in the quenched approximation, we compare this action to the clover-improved Wilson action. The proposed action reduces the size of discretization effects and the violation of rotational invariance to a remarkable degree. The presence of exceptionally small eigenvalues in the spectrum of the Dirac operator is also reduced.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a modified D234 fermion action with non-perturbative O(a) and tree-level O(a²) improvement, stout-smeared gauge links, and an exponentiated clover term; in quenched simulations, it outperforms the standard clover-improved Wilson action by significantly reducing discretization errors, rotational symmetry violation, and near-zero Dirac eigenvalues.
AI.motivation: To reduce discretization errors, rotational symmetry breaking, and spurious near-zero modes in lattice QCD fermion formulations.
AI.method: Constructed a variant of the D234 fermion action featuring non-perturbative O(a) improvement, tree-level O(a²) improvement, one level of stout smearing on gauge links, and exponentiated clover term; performed quenched lattice simulations comparing it to the standard clover-improved Wilson action.
AI.result: The proposed action markedly suppresses discretization effects, improves rotational invariance, and reduces the occurrence of exceptionally small eigenvalues in the Dirac operator spectrum.
AI.conclusion: The enhanced D234 action provides superior chiral and scaling properties compared to the standard clover-improved Wilson action in the quenched approximation, making it a promising candidate for high-precision lattice fermion simulations.

title: Half-strings across the deconfinement transition of a $U(1)$ quantum link model
summary: The phenomenon of confinement is arguably the key feature of gauge theories regularly studied in high-energy and condensed matter physics. This causes hadrons to exist as stable particles in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) as bound states of quarks (and gluons), and strings in pure gauge theories. The promise of realizing such strings in quantum simulator setups have fueled extensive studies of a plethora of simpler lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Quantum link models (QLMs) generalize Wilsonian LGTs and yield richer scenarios of confinement. For example, the string joining two static charges in the spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ $U(1)$ QLM fractionalize, giving rise to confining phases that break the point group and internal symmetries spontaneously. It was further shown in PRL 130, 071901 (2023) that adding annealed $Q = \pm 2$ charges to this model qualitatively changes the confinement-deconfinement transition. In this paper, we examine the finite temperature phase transition both in the presence and the absence of annealed charges through detailed extraction of critical temperature, $T_c$ , and exponents. The (effective) string tension $\sigma$ at zero and finite- temperatures are compared between the theory with and without annealed charges. The quantity $T_c/\sqrt{\sigma}$ for the QLM with annealed charges is similar to the usual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory, while the theory without the charges provides a new universal value.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates finite-temperature confinement-deconfinement phase transitions in the spin-1/2 U(1) quantum link model (QLM), comparing cases with and without annealed Q = ±2 charges; it extracts critical temperatures T_c and string tensions σ, finding that T_c/√σ yields a new universal value without charges, while matching the Z₂ gauge theory value when charges are present.
AI.motivation: To understand how annealed dynamical charges qualitatively alter confinement physics and universality classes in quantum link models—particularly whether they shift the system to known universality classes (e.g., Z₂ gauge theory) or induce novel critical behavior.
AI.method: Numerical extraction of critical temperature T_c and critical exponents via finite-temperature lattice simulations; comparison of zero- and finite-temperature string tension σ in both versions of the U(1) QLM (with and without annealed Q = ±2 charges); analysis of the dimensionless ratio T_c/√σ to assess universality.
AI.result: The QLM with annealed Q = ±2 charges exhibits T_c/√σ consistent with the standard Z₂ gauge theory, whereas the charge-free version yields a distinct, previously unobserved universal value for this ratio; critical exponents and transition nature differ accordingly.
AI.conclusion: Annealed charges fundamentally reshape the universality class of the confinement-deconfinement transition in the U(1) QLM, acting as a tuning parameter between known and novel critical behavior—highlighting the role of matter content in defining topological and critical properties of lattice gauge theories.

title: Second-order formulation of chiral fermions with a local boundary condition
summary: Chiral fermions in $d$ dimensions arise naturally as boundary modes of a massive fermion in $d+1$ dimensions subject to a local boundary condition. When anomalies are absent, this construction can be used to define an intrinsically $d$-dimensional theory of chiral fermions. However, defining the path integral using the first-order Dirac operator with this boundary condition is technically inconvenient, even in the continuum. We present a formulation in terms of second-order differential operators that is completely equivalent to the original formulation in the continuum. Its natural lattice discretization generates Wilson's term and avoids fermion doubling. Our lattice formulation closely resembles the boundary-fermion construction of Shamir, and provides some insight into the case of a general Wilson parameter.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates the continuum boundary-fermion construction of chiral fermions using second-order differential operators, enabling a natural, doubling-free lattice discretization that generalizes Shamir's approach and clarifies the role of the Wilson parameter.
AI.motivation: To overcome technical inconvenience of using the first-order Dirac operator with local boundary conditions for defining chiral fermions on the lattice, while avoiding fermion doubling and maintaining equivalence to the continuum boundary-fermion construction.
AI.method: Reformulates the chiral fermion boundary construction using second-order differential operators; derives its natural lattice discretization, which intrinsically generates Wilson’s term and preserves chirality without doubling.
AI.result: A continuum-equivalent, second-order formulation of boundary chiral fermions; its lattice version yields a doubling-free, Wilson-term-including action closely resembling Shamir’s domain-wall-like setup, with explicit insight into general Wilson parameter dependence.
AI.conclusion: The second-order formulation provides a technically superior and lattice-friendly equivalent of the original first-order boundary-fermion construction, unifying and generalizing existing approaches like Shamir’s and elucidating the Wilson parameter’s geometric origin.

title: Canonical and Canonoid Transformations of Hamiltonian Systems on $q$-Cosymplectic and $q$-Contact Manifolds
summary: $q$-Cosymplectic and $q$-contact structures equip presymplectic and precontact geometry with additional one-forms and a normalized family of Reeb vector fields. We study canonical and canonoid transformations relative to these data, with particular attention to their origin in constrained mechanical systems. In the $q$-cosymplectic and uniform $q$-contact cases, we establish local normal forms, characterize infinitesimal automorphisms, and obtain Noether-type relations between symmetries and conserved or dissipated quantities. For a one-parameter group of canonoid transformations with generator $X$, we show that $[X,X_H]$ is Hamiltonian and determine its Hamiltonian function. In the uniform $q$-contact case, simultaneous constant rescalings of the defining forms provide canonoid transformations for every Hamiltonian. The geometric constructions are illustrated by regular relativistic mass-shell constraints and by global Lagrangian descriptions of a charge in magnetic monopole fields. These examples distinguish parameters along constraint orbits from physical time and clarify the role of gauge directions. They also recover the total angular momentum of free relativistic particles and the Poincaré angular momentum of the charge--monopole system. For two monopoles, we construct a non-uniform $2$-contact structure and prove a topological obstruction to a uniform structure with the prescribed gauge generators as Reeb fields. Irrationally related magnetic charges additionally obstruct the intermediate quotient that would produce a single contact manifold. This example identifies a limitation of the uniform theory and motivates its extension to non-uniform structures.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces q-cosymplectic and q-contact structures as generalizations of presymplectic/precontact geometry, studies canonoid transformations and their symmetry-conservation relations, derives normal forms and infinitesimal automorphisms, and applies the framework to relativistic constraints and magnetic monopole systems—revealing topological obstructions to uniform structures in multi-monopole configurations.
AI.motivation: To extend geometric mechanics beyond standard symplectic/contact frameworks by incorporating parameter-dependent structures (q-cosymplectic/q-contact) that naturally arise in constrained mechanical systems—especially those distinguishing gauge directions, constraint-time separation, and nontrivial topologies like magnetic monopoles.
AI.method: Differential-geometric analysis: construction of q-cosymplectic and q-contact structures; classification of canonical/canonoid transformations; derivation of local normal forms; Lie-theoretic characterization of infinitesimal automorphisms; Noether-type analysis linking symmetries to conserved/dissipated quantities; explicit computation of Hamiltonian functions for commutators of generators; topological obstruction analysis via quotient constructions and irrationality conditions on magnetic charges.
AI.result: 1) Local normal forms and infinitesimal automorphism characterizations for q-cosymplectic and uniform q-contact structures; 2) Noether-type relations between symmetries and conserved/dissipated quantities; 3) For canonoid X, [X,X_H] is Hamiltonian with explicitly determined Hamiltonian function; 4) Uniform q-contact rescalings yield canonoid transformations for all Hamiltonians; 5) Relativistic mass-shell and charge–monopole examples clarify gauge vs. physical time and recover total/Poincaré angular momentum; 6) Two-monopole system admits a non-uniform 2-contact structure but obstructs uniform structure due to Reeb field incompatibility and irrational magnetic charge ratios blocking intermediate contact quotients.
AI.conclusion: Uniform q-contact geometry suffices for many constrained mechanical systems, but topological and arithmetic constraints—e.g., irrational magnetic charge ratios in multi-monopole systems—necessitate non-uniform generalizations; the framework unifies geometric treatments of time, gauge, and conservation laws while exposing intrinsic limitations of uniformity assumptions.

title: On Hölder Equicontinuity of the Integrated Density of States for Random Schrödinger Operators on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
comment: 35 pages, submitted to Journal of Functional Analysis
summary: We study a random Schrödinger operator $H_\lambda= H_0 + \lambda V$ on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ consisting of a translation invariant hopping matrix $H_0$ and a random potential $V$, given by independently distributed single site potentials with absolutely continuous distributions.
