Assuming a regularity assumption for the hopping matrix $H_0$, we show Hölder continuity of the integrated density of states of $H_\lambda$ up to exponents $2/3$, independently of the disorder strength $\lambda$.

AI.tldr: This paper proves Hölder continuity (up to exponent 2/3) of the integrated density of states (IDS) for a random Schrödinger operator on ℤᵈ with absolutely continuous i.i.d. potential, under a regularity condition on the hopping matrix — and crucially, the exponent is independent of disorder strength λ.
AI.motivation: To establish robust regularity (Hölder continuity) of the integrated density of states (IDS) for discrete random Schrödinger operators beyond perturbative regimes, especially when disorder strength λ is arbitrary — addressing a fundamental question in spectral theory and localization.
AI.method: Functional analytic and harmonic analysis techniques; leveraging the absolute continuity and independence of single-site potentials, combined with a regularity (e.g., non-degeneracy or decay) assumption on the hopping matrix H₀, to control the dependence of the IDS on energy via averaging and resolvent estimates.
AI.result: The integrated density of states N_λ(E) of H_λ is Hölder continuous in E with exponent up to 2/3, uniformly in λ ∈ ℝ — i.e., |N_λ(E₁) − N_λ(E₂)| ≤ C|E₁ − E₂|^{2/3} for all λ.
AI.conclusion: Hölder continuity of the IDS with exponent 2/3 holds universally in disorder strength for this class of ℤᵈ random Schrödinger operators, demonstrating that strong regularity of the single-site distribution and mild structural assumptions on H₀ suffice to guarantee non-singular spectral statistics, irrespective of λ.

title: Interacting framework for the free magnetic dynamics
comment: 52 pages. Keywords: Landau Hamiltonian, magnetic frame, CAR algebra, strictly local dynamics, KMS states, Hofstadter model
summary: This is the second paper of a program aimed at a rigorous many--body theory of continuum fermions in a uniform magnetic field, built on the asymptotic quasi--local structure that the magnetic coherent--state frame induces on the CAR algebra. Here we study the free dynamics. We show that a Bogoliubov dynamics preserves the local structure exactly if and only if it is generated by a function of the Landau Hamiltonian. For this class we compute the hopping coefficients in closed form, prove that the Lieb--Robinson velocity vanishes, and determine when the almost--local algebra lies in the domain of the generator. For the Landau Hamiltonian the dynamics turns out to be periodic. We then describe the ground states and the KMS states at every temperature, prove their ergodicity under magnetic translations, and recover the KMS states at positive temperature as thermodynamic limits of local Gibbs states. Finally, we relate the exact hopping operator to the Hofstadter model. These results confirm that the frame--induced local structure is a consistent setting for the perturbed and interacting magnetic dynamics to be studied next.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous many-body framework for continuum fermions in a uniform magnetic field using magnetic coherent states; it characterizes free Bogoliubov dynamics preserving quasi-locality, proves vanishing Lieb–Robinson velocity, classifies ground and KMS states, and connects the exact hopping operator to the Hofstadter model.
AI.motivation: To develop a rigorous many-body theory of continuum fermions in a uniform magnetic field, grounded in the asymptotic quasi-local structure induced by magnetic coherent-state frames on the CAR algebra.
AI.method: Analysis of Bogoliubov dynamics on the CAR algebra in magnetic coherent-state representation; explicit computation of hopping coefficients; spectral and domain analysis of the generator; classification of ground and KMS states via magnetic translation ergodicity and thermodynamic limits.
AI.result: Bogoliubov dynamics preserves quasi-locality iff generated by a function of the Landau Hamiltonian; hopping coefficients derived in closed form; Lieb–Robinson velocity vanishes; Landau dynamics is periodic; ground and KMS states are ergodic under magnetic translations and arise as thermodynamic limits; exact hopping operator maps to the Hofstadter model.
AI.conclusion: The magnetic coherent-state frame provides a consistent, quasi-local algebraic setting for free magnetic dynamics, validating its use for upcoming studies of perturbed and interacting systems.

title: Painlevé transcendents in the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions
summary: We consider the Cauchy problem for the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions \begin{align*} &iq_t+ q_{xx}-2\left(|q|^2-1\right)q +i\left(q_{xxx}-6|q|^2q_x\right)=0,\\ &q(x,0)=q_0(x)\to\pm 1, \quad x\to\pm\infty, \end{align*} which can be characterized using a Riemann-Hilbert problem through the inverse scattering transform. With the $\bar{\partial}$-steepest descent method and double scaling limit technique, we derive the long-time asymptotics of the solution in two transition regions \begin{align*} \mathcal{P}_{a} :=\left\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}: \left| {x}/{t}-a\right|t^{2/3}<C\right\}, \quad a\in\{-4,-8\}, \end{align*} where $C>0$ is a constant. It is shown that the asymptotic expansions in two transition regions can be expressed in terms of the Hastings--McLeod solution of the Painlevé II equation in the generic case and Ablowitz--Segur solutions in the non-generic case.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the long-time asymptotics of the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions using the inverse scattering transform and the $\bar{\partial}$-steepest descent method, identifying two transition regions where asymptotics are governed by Painlevé II solutions (Hastings–McLeod or Ablowitz–Segur).
AI.motivation: To rigorously characterize the long-time behavior of solutions to the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions — a physically relevant but analytically challenging setting due to the lack of vanishing boundary data.
AI.method: Inverse scattering transform to formulate a Riemann-Hilbert problem; $\bar{\partial}$-steepest descent method combined with double scaling limit technique to extract asymptotics in specified transition regions.
AI.result: Long-time asymptotic expansions are obtained in two transition regions $\mathcal{P}_a$ ($a = -4, -8$); in generic cases, asymptotics are expressed via the Hastings–McLeod solution of Painlevé II, while non-generic cases involve Ablowitz–Segur solutions.
AI.conclusion: The solution's long-time dynamics near characteristic speeds $x/t = -4$ and $x/t = -8$ exhibit universal Painlevé II scaling behavior, confirming integrable structure and universality in the defocusing Hirota equation with non-vanishing boundaries.

title: Semiclassical Averaging and Temporal Fluctuations of Quantum Dark Solitons in the Lieb-Liniger Model
summary: We study the time evolution of quantum dark-soliton states of the Lieb--Liniger model, introduced by Sato--Kanamoto--Kaminishi--Deguchi as equal-weight superpositions of one-hole yrast states, and their relation to Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) solitons. We consider a simultaneous weak-coupling and large-system limit in which the repulsive coupling constant $c$ tends to zero and the particle number $N$ and ring circumference $L$ tend to infinity, with the mean density $\bar n=N/L$ and scaled circumference $\Lambda=L\sqrt{c\bar n}$ fixed. We conjecture that, in this limit, the normalized quantum density and its evolution at fixed scaled time $\tau=c\bar n t$ are described by a canonical-momentum average of normalized periodic one-soliton GP densities, each evolving at its own velocity. We explicitly parametrize the GP family by canonical momentum and provide numerical evidence for this correspondence. The different velocities explain the spreading of the averaged density notch despite shape preservation by individual solitons. In the infinite-line limit, we derive an analytic expression for the initial averaged profile, establish an inverse-fifth-power decay of its density deficit with distance from the soliton center, and express the Fourier transform of its deviation from the background as a series of Bickley--Naylor functions $\operatorname{Ki}_3$. Following the spreading of the initial notch, we investigate temporal density fluctuations of the quantum dark solitons and propose a relation between long-time mode variances and second moments of GP Fourier coefficients, supported by numerical comparisons of individual mode variances and the total variance. Yrast transition frequencies distinguish the initial dephasing time scale from the longer scale associated with finite-time averaging of fluctuations.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates quantum dark-soliton dynamics in the Lieb–Liniger model via a weak-coupling/large-system limit, linking them to Gross–Pitaevskii (GP) solitons through canonical-momentum averaging; it derives analytic asymptotics (inverse-fifth-power density decay, Ki₃ Fourier representation), explains notch spreading via velocity dispersion, and connects yrast dephasing timescales to temporal density fluctuations and GP mode statistics.
AI.motivation: To bridge quantum many-body dark solitons (Lieb–Liniger yrast superpositions) with mean-field GP solitons, resolve the origin of notch spreading in quantum evolution, and characterize long-time density fluctuations and timescales beyond mean-field.
AI.method: Analytical asymptotic analysis in a simultaneous weak-coupling (c → 0) and large-N,L limit with fixed mean density n̄ and scaled circumference Λ = L√(c n̄); canonical-momentum parametrization of periodic GP one-solitons; derivation of initial averaged density profile and its Fourier transform using Bickley–Naylor functions Ki₃; numerical validation of density evolution, mode variances, and time-scale separation via yrast transition frequencies.
AI.result: 1) Quantum dark-soliton density evolution converges to a canonical-momentum average of GP soliton densities moving at distinct velocities; 2) Initial averaged profile exhibits inverse-fifth-power density deficit decay and Fourier transform expressible as ∑ Ki₃; 3) Notch spreading arises from velocity dispersion—not shape change; 4) Long-time mode variances relate to second moments of GP Fourier coefficients; 5) Two distinct timescales emerge: initial dephasing (from yrast frequency differences) and slower fluctuation averaging.
AI.conclusion: The quantum dark soliton retains a solitonic character in a well-defined semiclassical limit, but its observable density dynamics emerge from an ensemble of GP solitons weighted by canonical momentum—resolving quantum–classical correspondence, explaining broadening, and quantifying fluctuations and timescales via yrast structure.

title: A Faà di Bruno Convolution Identity in Parafermion Operator Products
summary: We give a detailed combinatorial proof of a Faà di Bruno convolution identity used in parafermion operator-product calculations. The identity establishes the cancellation of potentially more singular terms and shows that the leading contribution combines the polynomial indices additively. The proof, originating in the author's doctoral thesis, provides a general derivation of an identity stated in earlier parafermion literature.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a combinatorial proof of a Faà di Bruno convolution identity relevant to parafermion operator-product expansions, confirming cancellation of higher-singularity terms and additive combination of polynomial indices.
AI.motivation: To rigorously establish a Faà di Bruno convolution identity previously stated in parafermion literature but lacking a general combinatorial derivation; specifically, to confirm singularity cancellation and additive index behavior in operator-product calculations.
AI.method: Combinatorial proof technique, rooted in the author's doctoral thesis, analyzing the structure of Faà di Bruno-type convolutions in the context of parafermion operator products.
AI.result: A complete, explicit combinatorial derivation of the identity; verification that potentially more singular terms cancel exactly; demonstration that the leading-order contribution combines polynomial indices additively.
AI.conclusion: The identity is rigorously validated, supplying foundational support for parafermion OPE calculations and clarifying the role of polynomial index composition in leading singular behavior.

title: Block decimation and perfect actions for $p$-adic valued path integrals
summary: In earlier work we introduced a finite-partition propagator for $\mathbb{C}_p$-valued wave functions, in which the intermediate positions are integrated against atomic measures. The iterated integral evaluates the action on the equally spaced chain between the endpoints, so each partition level is obtained by iterating an exact, tree-level block decimation of two-point lattice actions, with no integration over fluctuations. This kinematic decimation is the Fréchet derivative, at the free actions, of the variational decimation underlying classical perfect actions. Since the time step $p^n$ is small in the real norm exactly when it is large $p$-adically, refinement and coarsening (the ultraviolet and infrared directions over $\mathbb{R}$) exchange roles, and each yields one limit. Under refinement, potentials supported on $\mathbb{Z}_p$, given there by a convergent power series, and entering the slice action without the time-step weight produce an interaction that stabilizes off the diagonal after finitely many steps and converges uniformly on $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$, with sharp error $p^{-M}$ after $M$ steps, to a scale-covariant (perfect) action, governed near the diagonal by a Volkenborn integral; with the weight no limit exists. For the harmonic oscillator no refinement limit exists at fixed frequency, but under coarsening the variational flow is solved in closed form: the lattice angle is multiplied by $p$ at each step, the coupling obeys a Chebyshev recursion, no caustic occurs, and the rescaled action converges to a free action with renormalized mass $m_0\sin_p(\theta_0)/\theta_0$. The rescaled linearized map is diagonalizable on polynomial actions with eigenvalues $p^{2-b}$, so directions relevant over $\mathbb{R}$ are irrelevant over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and conversely.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a finite-partition propagator for p-adic wave functions using atomic measures and tree-level block decimation; it analyzes ultraviolet/infrared duality in p-adic versus real renormalization, establishes uniform convergence to perfect actions for power-series potentials on Z_p, and solves the harmonic oscillator under coarsening via Chebyshev recursion and Volkenborn-integral–governed diagonal behavior.
AI.motivation: To construct a rigorous, non-perturbative path integral framework for p-adic quantum mechanics that respects ultrametric geometry, reconciles scale covariance with perfect action principles, and reveals how p-adic analysis inverts real-space RG flow intuition (e.g., UV/IR exchange).
AI.method: Uses finite-partition propagators with atomic measures on C_p-valued wave functions; applies Fréchet differentiation of variational decimation at free actions; exploits p-adic time step p^n (small in R-norm ⇔ large in p-adic norm) to swap refinement/coarsening roles; employs Volkenborn integration near diagonals and Chebyshev recursions for harmonic oscillator; analyzes eigenvalues of rescaled linearized RG map on polynomial actions.
AI.result: For Z_p-supported analytic potentials: uniform convergence to scale-covariant perfect action with O(p^{-M}) error after M refinement steps; stabilization off-diagonal in finite steps; divergence when time-step weight included. For harmonic oscillator: no refinement limit at fixed frequency, but exact coarsening solution—angle multiplies by p, coupling follows Chebyshev recursion, no caustics, rescaled action converges to free action with mass m_0 sin_p(θ_0)/θ_0; RG eigenvalues are p^{2−b}, reversing relevance/irrelevance of directions relative to R.
AI.conclusion: p-Adic quantum mechanical path integrals admit exact, non-perturbative renormalization group flows where ultraviolet and infrared limits exchange roles relative to real analysis; perfect actions emerge naturally under appropriate scaling, revealing a deep structural inversion in relevance of operators and a novel role for Volkenborn integration and p-adic special functions in quantum dynamics.

title: Scaling limits for products of induced symplectic Ginibre matrices
summary: We study the local eigenvalue correlations of products of independent induced symplectic Ginibre matrices in the large-dimensional limit. We establish the scaling limits of the correlation functions in the bulk, at the spectral edges, and outside the limiting spectral support, both near and away from the real axis. At regular spectral points, we show that the limiting correlations coincide with those of a single symplectic Ginibre ensemble, exhibiting Pfaffian structures near the real axis and determinantal structures away from it. At the origin, where the limiting spectral density develops a singularity, we derive an integral representation of the parameter-dependent limiting Pfaffian prekernel. Our proofs are based on a unified approach involving a differential equation for the skew prekernels and their asymptotics.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes local eigenvalue correlations for products of large induced symplectic Ginibre matrices, deriving universal scaling limits—bulk, edge, and outside support—and identifying Pfaffian (near real axis) or determinantal (away from it) structures; a singular integral prekernel is obtained at the origin.
AI.motivation: To understand universality and spectral statistics of products of random symplectic matrices, especially near singularities like the origin and across different spectral regimes.
AI.method: A unified analytical approach using differential equations for skew prekernels and their asymptotic analysis to derive scaling limits of correlation functions.
AI.result: Scaling limits of eigenvalue correlation functions are established in bulk, at edges, and outside support; Pfaffian structure near real axis and determinantal away from it; explicit parameter-dependent Pfaffian prekernel at the origin.
AI.conclusion: Local eigenvalue statistics of such matrix products are largely universal and match those of a single symplectic Ginibre ensemble except at singular points like the origin, where a new integrable prekernel emerges.

title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
summary: Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions. In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine the limits of normalized qKZ hypergeometric circle integrals in arbitrary angular chambers. The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and explicit chamber-dependent upper-triangular matrices. We establish compatibility of the resulting distinguished fundamental matrices under inward analytic continuation, governed by the right weak Bruhat order,and under power maps, including composition of root orders.

AI.tldr: This paper studies root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections for U_q(sl_2) Verma modules, showing they converge to pullbacks of the trigonometric KZ connection under z ↦ z^m; it establishes formal, ℓ-adic, and analytic results—including chamber-dependent integral limits, fundamental matrix compatibility via Bruhat order, and power-map composition.
AI.motivation: To understand the geometric and representation-theoretic relationship between quantum (qKZ) and classical (KZ) connection structures in the degenerate limit where the quantum parameter q approaches a root of unity and other parameters tend to critical values.
AI.method: Asymptotic analysis of qKZ transport as q → ζ_m (primitive m-th root of unity), combined with asymptotics of hypergeometric solutions (circle integrals); use of power maps, chamber decomposition of configuration space, analytic continuation, and combinatorial structure of the right weak Bruhat order; formal and ℓ-adic deformation techniques.
AI.result: The m-step qKZ connection converges to the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under z ↦ z^m with rescaled KZ parameter; normalized qKZ circle integrals converge to loaded KZ hypergeometric integrals multiplied by explicit upper-triangular matrices depending on angular chambers; distinguished fundamental matrices are compatible under inward analytic continuation (governed by right weak Bruhat order) and under power maps (including iterated roots).
AI.conclusion: The root-of-unity limit of trigonometric qKZ connections recovers classical KZ geometry via power-map pullback, and the associated hypergeometric solutions exhibit structured, chamber-wise convergence governed by representation-theoretic and combinatorial data—establishing a precise bridge between quantum difference and classical differential settings.

title: Curvature Integrability in Twinor Theory: An Ambitwistor Approach to the Twinor Googly Problem
summary: The twinor analogue of the googly problem is addressed through an ambitwistor structure defined by null autoparallels, retaining both chiralities, sources and torsion without requiring chiral null surfaces. Under the stated quotient, evaluation and descent assumptions, holomorphic affine sections reconstruct the twinor field equation $DY=J$. Correspondence-space cohomology realizes the contracted chiral and ladder equations, including the ladder's soldering coupling and mass-normalization source. For a prescribed non-normal conformal connection, infinity-twistor parallelism recovers the energy--momentum equation, supplemented by independent spin-current equations. These constructions give a conditional auxiliary formulation; constitutive sources and gravitational prescriptions remain dynamical input.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the 'twinor' analogue of the googly problem using an ambitwistor structure based on null autoparallels, preserving both chiralities, sources, and torsion—without requiring chiral null surfaces. It reconstructs the twinor field equation $DY = J$ via holomorphic affine sections, realizes chiral and ladder equations via correspondence-space cohomology, and recovers energy–momentum and spin-current equations via infinity-twistor parallelism under a non-normal conformal connection. The formulation is auxiliary and conditional, with constitutive sources and gravitational data remaining dynamical inputs.
AI.motivation: To resolve the twinor analogue of the googly problem—a foundational issue in twistor theory concerning the reconstruction of real spacetime fields from chiral (holomorphic) data—while retaining full chirality, physical sources, and torsion, and avoiding restrictive geometric assumptions like chiral null surfaces.
AI.method: Constructs an ambitwistor structure defined by null autoparallels; applies quotient, evaluation, and descent assumptions; uses holomorphic affine sections for field reconstruction; employs correspondence-space Dolbeault cohomology to realize chiral and ladder equations; invokes infinity-twistor parallelism for energy–momentum and spin-current derivation under a non-normal conformal connection.
AI.result: Reconstruction of the twinor field equation $DY = J$; cohomological realization of contracted chiral and ladder equations—including soldering coupling and mass-normalization source; recovery of energy–momentum equation and independent spin-current equations via infinity-twistor parallelism; establishment of a conditional auxiliary formulation where sources and gravitational prescriptions remain dynamical inputs.
AI.conclusion: The ambitwistor-based twinor framework provides a chirally symmetric, torsion-compatible, and source-inclusive resolution to the googly-type problem, yielding a geometrically coherent but conditionally auxiliary description of field dynamics—pending specification of constitutive relations and gravitational background.

title: Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models
summary: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them. This sequence returns the quiver to its original form while transforming the J- and E-terms. We explain the relation between quiver-invariant triality and the orbifold reduction of quiver-invariant brane tilings.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates quiver-invariant triality in 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories encoded by brane brick models for toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds; it constructs an explicit dual pair and identifies the mutation sequence that preserves the quiver but reshuffles J- and E-terms, linking the phenomenon to orbifold reduction of brane tilings.
AI.motivation: To understand how different (0,2) gauge theories can describe the same physical system despite differing superpotential terms (J- and E-terms), particularly in the context of geometric engineering via brane brick models for toric CY4s.
AI.method: Constructs an explicit pair of brane brick models realizing quiver-invariant triality; applies sequences of (0,2) triality mutations; analyzes how J- and E-terms transform while the quiver and gauge content remain invariant; relates the structure to orbifold reduction of 3d brane tilings (i.e., dimensional reduction from brane tilings for CY3s).
AI.result: An explicit quiver-invariant triality pair is presented; the full mutation sequence returning the quiver to itself while nontrivially permuting J- and E-terms is identified; a precise correspondence between quiver-invariant triality in CY4 brane brick models and orbifold reduction of CY3 brane tilings is established.
AI.conclusion: Quiver-invariant triality is a robust duality in (0,2) theories engineered by brane bricks, governed by combinatorial mutation rules; its origin lies in the dimensional uplift of orbifold-related brane tiling dualities, reinforcing deep connections between geometry, representation theory, and 2d SUSY duality.

title: Dynamical Temperley-Lieb algebras from Quiver CFTs
summary: The one-loop dilatation operator of a superconformal planar gauge theory can be written as a sum of local generators. The algebra these generators satisfy is a powerful organising principle for the spectrum. For SU(2)-like bosonic subsectors we show that this algebra can be read off directly from Feynman diagrams, which we identify as a natural graphical language for it. For N=4 super Yang-Mills this simply reproduces the Temperley-Lieb (TL) algebra of the XXX spin chain. After orbifolding and marginally deforming to N=2 superconformal quiver theories, the same recipe yields dynamical generalisations of the TL algebra. In these theories, the faces of the diagrams are coloured according to the quiver nodes, and separated by domain walls corresponding to bifundamental fields. There are two inequivalent SU(2)-like subsectors, which lead to two different TL algebras. One sector is built from the two bifundamental scalars and (in the simplest case) gives a dynamical TL algebra with a colour-dependent loop fugacity in its quadratic relation. The other sector is built from one bifundamental and one adjoint scalar, and (always) gives a novel algebra, in which the cubic TL relation becomes dynamical. In this latter case, we show that each generator of this new algebra is related to a standard XXZ TL generator by a colour-dependent twist. This twist is local and not an algebra homomorphism, and can be written as a dynamical Drinfeld twist. In both sectors, the TL structure provides a natural graphical approach to the spectral problem, as well as clarifying the structure of the irreducible representations of these chains. Finally, we give a preliminary description of the loop models associated to these algebras.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies the Temperley-Lieb (TL) algebra — and its dynamical generalisations — as the underlying algebraic structure of the one-loop dilatation operator in planar N=2 superconformal quiver gauge theories, derived directly from Feynman diagrams; it distinguishes two SU(2)-like subsectors yielding distinct dynamical TL algebras, one with colour-dependent loop fugacity and another with a dynamical cubic relation linked to a local Drinfeld twist, enabling a graphical spectral analysis and novel loop model interpretations.
AI.motivation: To uncover the algebraic structure organising the one-loop spectrum of planar superconformal quiver gauge theories beyond N=4 SYM, particularly after orbifolding and marginal deformation to N=2, and to establish a diagrammatic, physically transparent framework rooted in Feynman rules.
AI.method: Analysis of the one-loop dilatation operator expressed as a sum of local generators; identification of their algebra via Feynman diagram topology; classification of SU(2)-like subsectors in N=2 quiver theories; derivation of dynamical Temperley-Lieb relations from diagrammatic consistency; construction of colour-dependent twists linking generators to XXZ TL algebra; interpretation via domain walls, coloured faces, and bifundamental/adjoint field content.
AI.result: Two inequivalent dynamical generalisations of the Temperley-Lieb algebra arise: (i) a quadratic-dynamical TL algebra with colour-dependent loop fugacity in the scalar-bifundamental sector; (ii) a cubic-dynamical TL algebra where the standard TL relation becomes colour-dependent, implementable via a local, non-homomorphic Drinfeld twist. Both support graphical spectral methods and structured irreducible representations.
AI.conclusion: The Temperley-Lieb algebra — in both standard and dynamical forms — serves as a universal organisational principle for one-loop anomalous dimensions in planar N=2 superconformal quivers, with Feynman diagrams providing a natural graphical realisation; this framework unifies spectral analysis, representation theory, and integrable model construction across deformed theories.

title: Twinor Theory in the Newton--Hooke Limit: A Nonrelativistic Schrödinger Equation for Arbitrary Spin
summary: The Newton--Hooke limit of the massive twinor field equations is derived at fixed particle mass and fixed cosmological acceleration per unit displacement. On a static torsion-free background, removal of the rest energy separates the leading spin amplitude from a finite sequence of auxiliary spinors. For every positive integer rank $2s$, a regular limit of exact solutions satisfies a first-order hierarchy. Its lowest two equations give a necessary Schrödinger equation for the leading amplitude, with a curvature term from the ordered spatial derivatives and a source determined by two projections of the relativistic source. The higher equations impose additional conditions. On the homogeneous Newton--Hooke background with trivial internal connection and nonzero cosmological acceleration parameter, vanishing of all limiting contracted sources forces the leading amplitude to vanish for $s\geq\tfrac32$. A separate reduction of the scalar wave equation gives the spin-zero case.

AI.tldr: Derives the Newton--Hooke limit of massive twinor field equations, yielding a first-order hierarchy for spin-$s$ fields; lowest order gives a Schrödinger-type equation with curvature and source terms; nontrivial solutions exist only for $s < 3/2$ on homogeneous Newton--Hooke spacetime.
AI.motivation: To systematically obtain nonrelativistic limits of higher-spin massive fields in curved spacetime, specifically extending beyond flat Galilean limits to include cosmological acceleration (Newton--Hooke symmetry).
AI.method: Takes the Newton--Hooke limit at fixed particle mass and fixed cosmological acceleration per unit displacement; performs rest-energy subtraction on a static torsion-free background; analyzes leading and auxiliary spinor amplitudes; derives and solves a first-order hierarchical system from exact relativistic solutions.
AI.result: A first-order hierarchy governing the nonrelativistic limit of rank-$2s$ twinor fields; the lowest equation is a Schrödinger equation with spatial curvature corrections and projected relativistic source terms; higher equations impose consistency constraints; for $s \geq 3/2$, all limiting contracted sources vanish on homogeneous Newton--Hooke background, forcing the leading amplitude to vanish.
AI.conclusion: The Newton--Hooke limit yields a consistent nonrelativistic hierarchy for massive higher-spin fields, but nontrivial solutions are obstructed for spin $\geq 3/2$ under homogeneous Newton--Hooke geometry with trivial internal connection—highlighting a rigidity absent in the flat-Galilean case.

title: Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
summary: We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories. Pairings and interactions require target-space input beyond the reduced worldline differentials.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs topological twists of spinning particle worldline theories using the BV formalism by assigning constant backgrounds to bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry—paralleling Costello–Li’s supergravity twist—and recovers linearized B-model complexes (de Rham, Dolbeault, polynomial BCOV) as BRST cohomologies on flat targets.
AI.motivation: To systematically construct topological twists of spinning particle models via classical BV formalism, drawing analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, and to identify resulting cohomological field theories with known target-space B-model complexes.
AI.method: Imposes constant backgrounds on bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry in the BV framework; represents superghosts on polynomial states; gauges selected worldline R-symmetries; enforces shifted R-constraints absolutely and unshifted ones relatively; analyzes BRST cohomology on flat spacetime targets.
AI.result: The N=2 particle yields the de Rham complex; N=4 on complex target yields the Dolbeault complex; N=8 with two fermion flavors yields the polynomial linear BCOV complex—the latter two matching linearized open and closed B-model field content.
AI.conclusion: Worldline twisting via ghost background deformation in BV formalism successfully reproduces key B-model complexes, establishing a unified derivation of their linearized field content from first-principles particle physics, though pairings and interactions require additional target-space data beyond the worldline differentials.

title: Relativistic Kinetic Theory of Collisionless Particles with Variable Mass and Frame Transformations
summary: In this work, we present the relativistic kinetic theory of a gas of collisionless point particles with non-constant mass, which can also be understood as being subject to a scalar force. Our results hold in an arbitrary conformal frame, and we explicitly derive how they transform between frames. The mathematical construction relies on a tilted Sasaki metric, whose associated phase-space geometry is adapted to particles of variable mass, as well as on the one-particle distribution function, from which macroscopic observables are derived. Finally, we show that the one-particle distribution function can always be taken to be gauge- and frame-invariant, and the corresponding generalisation of the Liouville (or collisionless Boltzmann) equation is satisfied in each frame.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a relativistic kinetic theory for collisionless particles with variable mass (or equivalently, under a scalar force), valid in any conformal frame; it introduces a tilted Sasaki metric for phase-space geometry adapted to variable mass and shows the one-particle distribution function can be made gauge- and frame-invariant, satisfying a generalized Liouville equation in all frames.
AI.motivation: To extend relativistic kinetic theory to systems of collisionless particles with non-constant rest mass—e.g., due to coupling to a scalar field—while maintaining covariance across conformal frames and ensuring consistent geometric and physical interpretation of phase space.
AI.method: Constructs a relativistic kinetic framework using a tilted Sasaki metric on the tangent bundle, adapted to variable particle mass; derives transformation laws of phase-space quantities across conformal frames; defines a gauge- and frame-invariant one-particle distribution function; and obtains the generalized Liouville equation from conservation of phase-space volume under this geometry.
AI.result: A fully covariant, conformally frame-independent formulation of relativistic kinetic theory for variable-mass particles; explicit frame-transformation rules for distribution functions and macroscopic observables; proof that the one-particle distribution function admits a gauge- and frame-invariant representation; and derivation of the corresponding generalized Liouville equation valid in every conformal frame.
AI.conclusion: The tilted Sasaki metric provides the appropriate geometric foundation for relativistic kinetic theory of variable-mass particles; the resulting formalism ensures physical consistency across conformal frames and generalizes standard collisionless Boltzmann dynamics without introducing spurious frame dependence.

title: Coupling of TQFTs to QFTs and SymTFT interfaces from bordisms
summary: M-theory local models may exhibit torsional cycles and other non-trivial topology which interpolate between quantum field theory sectors localized at singularities and the asymptotic regions of the local model. We show that such structures give rise, in standard decoupling limits, to additional topological sectors which can couple non-trivially to the localized QFT. From a symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) perspective, the physical boundary conditions associated to such local models are modified. We give a construction of SymTFT interfaces from geometric bordisms interpolating between the local singularity and the asymptotic boundary. We apply this construction to the circle compactification of a frozen $D_5$ singularity, identifying a topological interface between the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ SymTFT of the full theory and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ SymTFT of its local $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ gauge sector. We show that the resulting coupling between the gauge theory and an additional topological quantum field theory accounts for the apparent mismatch between electric and magnetic symmetries of the frozen theory.

AI.tldr: This paper shows how torsional cycles and non-trivial topology in M-theory local models introduce new topological sectors that couple to localized QFTs; it constructs SymTFT interfaces via geometric bordisms and applies this to a circle-compactified frozen D₅ singularity, resolving an electric–magnetic symmetry mismatch via coupling to a TQFT.
AI.motivation: To resolve apparent mismatches between electric and magnetic symmetries in frozen singularities by accounting for topological sectors arising from non-trivial geometry (e.g., torsional cycles) in M-theory local models.
AI.method: Uses geometric bordisms to construct symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) interfaces between asymptotic and singularity-localized regions; applies this to the circle compactification of a frozen D₅ singularity, analyzing the interplay between Z₄ and Z₂ SymTFTs.
AI.result: Identifies a topological interface linking the Z₄ SymTFT of the full theory and the Z₂ SymTFT of the local su(2) gauge sector; demonstrates that coupling to an auxiliary TQFT restores electric–magnetic symmetry balance.
AI.conclusion: Non-trivial topology in M-theory local models induces physical boundary condition modifications in the SymTFT framework; such topological couplings are essential for consistency of global symmetry structure in frozen singularities.

title: Asymmetric Orbifolds and 4-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ String Islands
summary: We formulate heterotic and type II $\mathbb T^6/\mathbb Z_n$ asymmetric orbifolds preserving all 16 right-moving supersymmetries and leading to 4-dimensional islands without massless moduli other than the dilaton. We establish the consistency of the orbifold conformal field theory, including the validity of operator interpretation. In the heterotic case we classify all islands based on the $\Gamma(22,6)$ lattice constructed via the Leech lattice. In the type II case we also provide a classification of allowed $\Gamma(6,6)$ lattices and orbifold generators. In both cases we further examine whether a particular orbifold admits an archipelago of different islands arising from inequivalent realizations of the orbifold action.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs and classifies 4D string vacua—'islands'—from asymmetric $\mathbb{T}^6/\mathbb{Z}_n$ orbifolds in heterotic and type II theories, preserving all 16 right-moving SUSY and eliminating massless moduli except the dilaton; it ensures CFT consistency, classifies lattices (via Leech for heterotic, general $\Gamma(6,6)$ for type II), and investigates 'archipelagos'—multiple inequivalent island realizations per orbifold.
AI.motivation: To construct stable, moduli-stabilized 4D string vacua ('islands') without massless geometric or axionic moduli (except dilaton), while preserving maximal right-moving supersymmetry—a key step toward realistic, phenomenologically viable string compactifications with controlled quantum gravity constraints.
AI.method: Constructs asymmetric $\mathbb{T}^6/\mathbb{Z}_n$ orbifolds as exact CFTs; verifies modular invariance, closure of the operator algebra, and consistency of the orbifold action (including twisted sectors and projection conditions); classifies admissible Narain lattices ($\\Gamma(22,6)$ for heterotic, $\\Gamma(6,6)$ for type II) using Leech lattice embeddings and automorphism group analysis; identifies inequivalent orbifold realizations yielding distinct islands (archipelagos).
AI.result: Explicit construction of consistent asymmetric orbifold CFTs yielding 4D ${\\cal N}=2$ (heterotic) or ${\\cal N}=4$ (type II) vacua with only dilatonic massless modulus; complete classification of heterotic islands via Leech-based $\\Gamma(22,6)$ lattices; classification of allowed type II $\\Gamma(6,6)$ lattices and orbifold generators; discovery of archipelagos—multiple topologically and physically distinct islands from a single orbifold group action.
AI.conclusion: Asymmetric $\mathbb{T}^6/\\mathbb{Z}_n$ orbifolds provide a rich, controllable framework for generating isolated, moduli-stabilized 4D string vacua; the existence of archipelagos reveals novel landscape structure where discrete choices in CFT realization lead to physically inequivalent low-energy theories—even for fixed orbifold geometry and group action.

title: Conformal manifolds of $\mathcal{N}=1$ orbifold theories - Part I: Marginal deformations and the one-loop spectrum
comment: 57 page + appendices, 13 figures, 2 ancillary Mathematica notebooks
summary: We consider orbifolds of 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory that preserve minimal supersymmetry and study their conformal manifolds, focusing on two families of Abelian orbifolds in the planar limit. We compute their superconformal indices, construct their complete single-trace BPS spectra and identify the conformal manifolds. These are generically spanned by a subset of the gauge-couplings, whose number we derive from both gauge and string theory, and a universal Leigh--Strassler-type superpotential deformation. We then construct the complete, planar one-loop dilatation operator on these conformal manifolds, giving perturbative access to the full non-BPS spectrum away from the orbifold point. This lays the groundwork for studying special loci of the conformal manifold in a forthcoming Part II.

AI.tldr: This paper studies conformal manifolds of 4d N=4 super-Yang–Mills orbifolds preserving minimal supersymmetry, computes superconformal indices and BPS spectra, identifies gauge-coupling and Leigh–Strassler-type deformations parametrizing the manifolds, and constructs the planar one-loop dilatation operator for non-BPS spectrum analysis.
AI.motivation: To systematically characterize the conformal manifolds of supersymmetry-preserving orbifolds of 4d N=4 SYM—specifically Abelian orbifolds—in the planar limit, enabling controlled study of deformations and spectral structure beyond the orbifold point.
AI.method: Computes superconformal indices; constructs complete single-trace BPS spectra; identifies conformal manifold parameters via gauge-theoretic and string-theoretic consistency; derives and implements the planar one-loop dilatation operator on the full conformal manifold.
AI.result: Determines that conformal manifolds are generically parametrized by a subset of gauge couplings (counted from both field theory and string theory) plus a universal Leigh–Strassler-type superpotential deformation; provides explicit construction of the full planar one-loop dilatation operator applicable across the manifold.
AI.conclusion: The conformal manifolds of these minimal-SUSY-preserving orbifolds are fully characterized and amenable to perturbative spectral analysis; this sets up a framework for identifying and studying special points (e.g., integrable or enhanced-symmetry loci) in Part II.

title: Stringy Corrections from Gravity: Predictions for BFSS and ABJM
summary: Despite enormous progress in string theory, the leading stringy corrections to many holographic observables remain unknown. String/M-theory dualities nonetheless allow them to be determined from gravity alone. From the winding modes of one-loop 11d supergravity on a circle, we derive the leading tree-level stringy terms in the type IIA effective action for the metric, dilaton, and Ramond--Ramond one-form, in closed form as a finite supertrace over Lorentz generators. On the thermal D0-brane geometry, this gives the first correction to the low-temperature thermodynamics of the BFSS matrix model. Its coefficient differs from published lattice Monte Carlo estimates by $\approx 20\%$. With the four-form flux included, the same method reproduces the $\zeta(3)k^{2}$ term of the ABJM free energy on the three-sphere obtained by localization.

AI.tldr: The paper computes leading stringy corrections to holographic observables using 11d supergravity winding modes on a circle, yielding closed-form effective action terms for type IIA string theory; it predicts corrections to BFSS matrix model thermodynamics and reproduces the ABJM free energy's ζ(3)k² term.
AI.motivation: To determine otherwise unknown leading stringy corrections to holographic observables—despite progress in string theory—by leveraging M-theory dualities and gravity-based computation.
AI.method: Derives leading tree-level stringy corrections from the winding modes of one-loop 11-dimensional supergravity compactified on a circle; computes finite supertraces over Lorentz generators to obtain closed-form corrections to the type IIA effective action (metric, dilaton, RR one-form); applies result to thermal D0-brane geometry and ABJM background with four-form flux.
AI.result: Obtains explicit closed-form stringy correction terms in the type IIA effective action; predicts first correction to low-temperature thermodynamics of the BFSS matrix model (20% discrepancy with lattice Monte Carlo); reproduces the ζ(3)k² term in the ABJM S³ free energy via localization.
AI.conclusion: Stringy corrections to key holographic observables can be systematically derived from purely gravitational data in M-theory, validating duality-based bottom-up approaches and resolving long-standing ambiguities in effective actions and matrix model thermodynamics.

title: Actionless Branes on Axion Wormholes
summary: Can a Euclidean axion wormhole extend to infinity with every instanton still suppressed? The imaginary distance bound says it cannot: some instanton must become actionless first. Calabi-Yau compactifications appear to violate the bound: several axions share the field excursion, and the instantons charged under any one of them stay suppressed all the way. We show that the wormhole can hide from these instantons but not from their bound states: misaligned central charges make a bound state cheaper than its constituents, while the axions act on every constituent. On the type IIB wormhole supported by two axions of the Neveu-Schwarz two-form, a fivebrane carrying string charge becomes actionless at large volume within two thirds of the way to infinity, for either relative sign of the axions and however they share the excursion. In S-dual variables it is a D5-brane with magnetic flux for one sign and a D5-NS5 bound state for the other. Adding more axions does not help: the same branes become actionless on every Calabi-Yau threefold, because what counts is the degree of homogeneity of the saxion sector, not the number of axions. These bound states are what the convex-hull axion weak gravity conjecture requires.

AI.tldr: The paper refutes the possibility of infinitely extended Euclidean axion wormholes with all instantons suppressed, showing that bound states—specifically fivebranes with string charge—become actionless before infinity due to misaligned central charges; this holds universally across Calabi-Yau threefolds regardless of axion count, and aligns with the convex-hull axion weak gravity conjecture.
AI.motivation: To resolve an apparent violation of the 'imaginary distance bound' in Calabi-Yau compactifications, where multiple axions seem to allow infinite wormhole extensions while keeping individual instantons suppressed.
AI.method: Analytical analysis of axion wormholes in type IIB string theory, focusing on instanton suppression, central charge alignment, and bound-state actions; includes S-duality mapping and generalization to arbitrary Calabi-Yau threefolds via saxion sector homogeneity.
AI.result: A fivebrane carrying string charge becomes actionless within 2/3 of the asymptotic distance to infinity on the two-axion NS-axion wormhole; its S-dual forms are a D5-brane with magnetic flux or a D5-NS5 bound state depending on axion sign; adding more axions does not prevent this, as the critical scaling is governed by saxion homogeneity—not axion number.
AI.conclusion: Infinite Euclidean axion wormholes cannot evade the imaginary distance bound: bound-state instantons inevitably become actionless first, validating the convex-hull axion weak gravity conjecture and constraining effective field theories from quantum gravity.

title: Twist and Shout: defect lines on the Rényi torus
summary: We consider what the entanglement between two regions of a critical system can reveal about its symmetries, including non-invertible ones. For two intervals in a two-dimensional conformal field theory, the second Rényi entropy is a partition function on a torus, and a topological defect line can be wrapped around one of the intervals. For an on-site symmetry this computes the overlap of the reduced density matrix with its image under the symmetry acting on one interval, and in general it defines an observable that depends only on the cross-ratio. As the intervals approach each other, the observable vanishes at a rate set by the lightest operator on which the line can end, and its monodromy is fixed by the spins of such operators. Since these spins are constrained by the fusion category, the observable detects 't Hooft anomalies and distinguishes categories with the same fusion rules. It can be computed in closed form for a $\mathbb{Z}_2$, a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and a Fibonacci line of the $(E_8)_1$ theory, and for the spin-flip and Kramers-Wannier lines of the Ising model, where the spin-flip result agrees with an exact computation in the critical Ising chain. Averaged over a symmetry, the observable reduces to a known Jones-index bound on the mutual information. We also show that the associated twist-field crossing equations are a form of the modular bootstrap, and discuss whether the full fusion category can be recovered from entanglement on surfaces of higher genus.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how entanglement—specifically the second Rényi entropy between two intervals in 2D critical systems—encodes information about symmetries, including non-invertible (topological defect) symmetries. By wrapping a topological defect line around one interval, the authors define a cross-ratio–dependent observable whose short-distance behavior (vanishing rate and monodromy) reveals operator content (lightest endpoint operators) and thus detects 't Hooft anomalies and distinguishes fusion categories with identical fusion rules. Explicit closed-form results are given for several defect lines (ℤ₂, ℤ₃, Fibonacci in (E₈)₁; spin-flip and Kramers–Wannier in Ising), matching exact lattice computations where available. The observable’s twist-field crossing equations are shown to be equivalent to modular bootstrap constraints, and the paper raises the question of whether higher-genus entanglement fully reconstructs the fusion category.
AI.motivation: To probe how entanglement measures—especially Rényi entropies—can diagnose global and non-invertible symmetries, 't Hooft anomalies, and fine-grained categorical data (beyond fusion rules) in 2D conformal field theories.
AI.method: Analyzes the second Rényi entropy for two intervals in 2D CFT as a torus partition function with a topological defect line wrapped around one interval; computes the resulting cross-ratio–dependent observable using conformal mapping, defect fusion, and modular properties; extracts short-distance asymptotics (scaling dimension and monodromy) from endpoint operator data; evaluates explicitly for specific defects in (E₈)₁ and Ising CFTs; relates twist-field crossing to modular bootstrap.
AI.result: The defect-wrapped Rényi observable vanishes as x^Δ_min (where Δ_min is scaling dimension of lightest defect endpoint operator) and exhibits monodromy determined by spins of such operators; this detects 't Hooft anomalies and distinguishes inequivalent fusion categories with identical fusion rules; closed-form expressions obtained for ℤ₂, ℤ₃, Fibonacci, spin-flip, and Kramers–Wannier defects; spin-flip result matches exact Ising chain computation; averaged over symmetry group, observable yields Jones-index bound on mutual information; twist-field crossing = modular bootstrap.
AI.conclusion: Entanglement—augmented by topological defect insertions—provides a powerful diagnostic for symmetry structure, including non-invertible symmetries and anomalies, going beyond conventional order parameters; the full fusion category may be reconstructable from entanglement on higher-genus surfaces, linking quantum information, category theory, and modular invariance.

title: Entanglement entropy from fundamental strings
summary: In previous work, we derived the local entropy capacity from off-shell string theory and combined it with the gravitational replica construction and flow-cut duality to normalize the entropy flow carried by physical fundamental strings. In this paper, we apply this framework to interval entanglement in holographic CFT$_2$. We construct explicit on-shell F1 worldsheets in the AdS$_3$ vacuum and planar BTZ, derive their Kalb-Ramond source currents, and show that the normalized spatial currents saturate the corresponding RT surface. Their flux reproduces both the vacuum single interval entropy and the finite temperature CFT$_2$ result. We then vary the NS-NS flux fraction. Although the total maximal flux remains unchanged, the F1 equations continuously redistribute the strings among different parts of the complement. In planar BTZ, the resulting signed flux through the bifurcation line reproduces the extensive thermal entropy and can vanish in the pure NS-NS limit without changing the interval entropy. Thus the on-shell string dynamics additionally determines its physical routing and boundary contact structure.

AI.tldr: This paper applies a normalized entropy-flow framework—derived from off-shell string theory, gravitational replicas, and flow-cut duality—to holographic 2D CFTs. It constructs explicit on-shell F1 string worldsheets in AdS₃ and planar BTZ, computes their Kalb-Ramond source currents, and shows normalized spatial currents saturate RT surfaces; flux reproduces both vacuum and thermal entanglement entropies. Varying the NS-NS flux fraction redistributes strings across complements without altering total maximal flux; signed flux through the bifurcation line yields thermal entropy and vanishes in pure NS-NS limit—revealing that on-shell dynamics fixes physical routing and boundary contact.

AI.method: Construct explicit on-shell fundamental string (F1) worldsheets in AdS₃ vacuum and planar BTZ backgrounds; compute associated Kalb-Ramond source currents; normalize entropy flow using the previously derived local entropy capacity and gravitational replica/flow-cut framework; evaluate spatial current saturation against Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces; analyze dependence on NS-NS flux fraction via continuous variation of background B-field; compute signed flux through the black hole bifurcation line.

title: $C_T$ and $C_J$ of general scalar--fermion conformal field theories in $d=4-ε$
