summary: We compute $C_T$ and $C_J$, the coefficients of the stress-tensor and conserved-current two-point functions, to order $\epsilon^3$ at any fixed point of the general renormalizable theory of scalars and fermions in $d=4-\epsilon$. We give explicit results for the chiral Ising, XY and Heisenberg models and for fixed points with emergent supersymmetry in $d=3$. In theories without a four-dimensional counterpart, fermion loops with an odd number of Yukawa vertices contribute at order $\epsilon^3$ through traces whose continuation away from $d=3$ is ambiguous; we fix it with $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetry, by computing the two-point functions of the supercurrent and of the fermionic partner of a flavor current to four loops. In $d=3$, Padé approximants closely reproduce the exact $C_T$ of the $\mathcal N=2$ super-Ising model. We estimate the universal conductivity at the charge-density-wave, Kekulé and Néel transitions of graphene to be $\sigma/\sigma_{\rm free}\approx0.91$, $0.79$--$0.83$ and $0.64$--$0.74$, and show that the exact conductivity at the supersymmetric transition on the surface of a topological insulator is $\sigma/\sigma_{\rm free}=\frac{9}{10}\,C_T/C_{T,\rm free}\approx0.654$, $10\%$ below the value previously reported.

AI.tldr: This paper computes stress-tensor and current two-point function coefficients (C_T, C_J) to O(ε³) in d = 4−ε for general scalar–fermion theories, resolves ambiguities in odd-Yukawa-loop contributions using N=1 supersymmetry, validates results via Padé approximants against exact N=2 super-Ising data in d=3, and provides refined universal conductivity estimates for quantum critical points in graphene and topological insulator surfaces.
AI.motivation: To systematically compute universal CFT data (C_T, C_J) in interacting fermionic–scalar QFTs near four dimensions, resolve dimensional-regularization ambiguities in odd-fermion-loop diagrams at O(ε³), and deliver precise predictions for universal transport (e.g., conductivity) at quantum critical points without Lagrangian UV completions in d=3.
AI.method: Perturbative renormalization group in d = 4−ε up to three loops; dimensional regularization with consistent γ-matrix trace prescriptions; use of N=1 supersymmetry as a regulator to fix ambiguous traces from odd-Yukawa fermion loops; four-loop computation of supercurrent and fermionic flavor-current two-point functions in supersymmetric theories; Padé resummation for d=3 extrapolation; matching to known exact results (e.g., N=2 super-Ising) for validation.
AI.result: Explicit O(ε³) expressions for C_T and C_J for chiral Ising, XY, Heisenberg, and supersymmetric fixed points in d=3; resolution of trace ambiguity via supersymmetric completion; Padé-approximated C_T matches exact N=2 super-Ising value in d=3; revised universal conductivities: σ/σ_free ≈ 0.91 (charge-density-wave), 0.79–0.83 (Kekulé), 0.64–0.74 (Néel) in graphene; exact σ/σ_free = 9/10 × C_T/C_{T,free} ≈ 0.654 for surface superconducting transition on topological insulator—10% lower than prior literature.
AI.conclusion: The O(ε³) computation of C_T and C_J provides high-precision universal data for fermion–scalar CFTs, with supersymmetry serving as a crucial consistency check and regulator; the refined conductivity estimates have direct implications for interpreting quantum critical transport experiments in 2D materials.

title: Nonzero cubic Love numbers of Schwarzschild black holes
summary: Static Love numbers of Schwarzschild black holes vanish at linear and quadratic order in General Relativity, while generic nonlinear tides remain less understood. We solve a specific non-axisymmetric octupolar tide at cubic order and, building on the symmetry of static General Relativity exploited by Parra-Martinez and Podo, match the result to a worldline effective field theory (EFT) using dimensional regularization. Surprisingly, we find a Love number that neither vanishes nor runs.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the static octupolar Love number of a Schwarzschild black hole at cubic order in tidal perturbation within General Relativity, finding a finite, non-vanishing, and non-running value—contrary to expectations from lower-order vanishing and typical RG running in EFTs.
AI.motivation: To resolve the ambiguity surrounding nonlinear tidal responses of black holes, especially whether higher-order static Love numbers remain zero or acquire finite, possibly scale-dependent values, given their vanishing at linear and quadratic orders.
AI.method: Solves the Einstein equations for a specific non-axisymmetric octupolar (ℓ=3) static tidal perturbation at cubic order in the tidal field; employs symmetry-based simplifications from Parra-Martinez & Podo; matches the bulk solution to a worldline EFT with dimensional regularization to extract the Love number.
AI.result: A finite, non-zero static octupolar Love number is obtained at cubic order; it is scale-independent (i.e., does not run with energy scale), unlike typical EFT couplings subject to renormalization group flow.
AI.conclusion: Static black hole Love numbers do not universally vanish beyond quadratic order; the cubic-order octupolar Love number is finite and non-running—a novel feature indicating a special rigidity of Schwarzschild black holes under higher-order static tides in GR.

title: Soft Factorisation of WQFT and the Spinning 4PM Magnusian
summary: We derive the soft divergences of $\hat{N}=-i\log\hat{S}$ in the Worldline Quantum Field Theory (WQFT) formalism, focusing on poles due to single massive-massive (Coulomb) and massive-massless (tail) graviton exchanges. Our derivation is inspired by the Faddeev-Kulish procedure, switching the interaction picture to one with an infrared-finite $\hat{N}$-matrix. Soft divergences emerging from the worldline are correlators of Wilson lines. As confirmation of this structure, we demonstrate explicitly how divergences of inclusive observables including the momentum impulse $\Delta p_i^\mu$ and spin kick $\Delta S_i^\mu$ cancel, and we reproduce the infrared divergence of the one-loop scattering waveform. Using the Magnus series representation of $\hat{N}$ and Murua coefficients, we then calculate the Magnusian $N=\langle0|\hat{N}|0\rangle$ at fourth post-Minkowskian (4PM) order, including linear-in-spin corrections. For aligned spins, $-\partial N/\partial L$ reproduces the full scattering angle through 3PM order; at 4PM order, $N$ develops a soft divergence as predicted by our soft factorisation. Using the Feynman $i0^+$ prescription, we also derive an infrared-finite 4PM Magnusian which compactly encodes existing results for the conservative momentum impulse and spin kick via nested iterations of Poisson brackets.

AI.tldr: This paper derives soft divergences of the logarithm of the S-matrix (N-hat) in Worldline Quantum Field Theory, connects them to Wilson-line correlators à la Faddeev-Kulish, confirms cancellation in inclusive observables (momentum impulse, spin kick, waveform), and computes the Magnusian N = ⟨0|N-hat|0⟩ at 4PM order—including linear-in-spin effects—yielding the scattering angle up to 3PM and revealing soft divergence at 4PM; an IR-finite version is constructed via i0⁺ prescription, encoding conservative dynamics via Poisson brackets.
AI.motivation: To systematically resolve infrared (soft) divergences in gravitational scattering amplitudes—particularly for massive particles with spin—by reformulating the interaction picture using the N-matrix (log S), inspired by Faddeev-Kulish dressing, and to unify soft factorisation, observable cancellation, and conservative dynamics within the worldline framework.
AI.method: Employs Worldline Quantum Field Theory (WQFT) to compute soft poles from massive-massive (Coulomb) and massive-massless (tail) graviton exchanges; identifies soft divergences as Wilson-line correlators on worldlines; uses the Magnus series expansion of N-hat with Murua coefficients to compute the vacuum expectation value N at 4PM order; applies Feynman's i0⁺ prescription to construct an infrared-finite N; verifies consistency via cancellation in Δpᵢ^μ, ΔSᵢ^μ, and one-loop waveform divergence.
AI.result: Explicit demonstration that soft divergences in inclusive observables cancel; reproduction of the known IR divergence of the one-loop scattering waveform; full 4PM Magnusian N including linear-in-spin terms; for aligned spins, −∂N/∂L yields the scattering angle through 3PM and exhibits a soft pole at 4PM; construction of an IR-finite 4PM N that compactly encodes conservative momentum impulse and spin kick via nested Poisson brackets.
AI.conclusion: The N-matrix formalism in WQFT provides a unified, infrared-safe framework for gravitational scattering: soft divergences are geometrised as worldline Wilson-line correlators; the Magnus expansion enables systematic high-order PM computation with spin; and the IR-finite N captures conservative dynamics holistically, bridging quantum and classical regimes.

title: Calabi-Yau linear models with abelian bundles
summary: We introduce a construction of (0,2) gauged linear sigma models whose large radius phases realize Calabi-Yau sigma models with line bundles. We study a family of such models admitting Landau-Ginzburg orbifold phases, described as asymmetric orbifolds of (2,2) Gepner models and free left-moving fermions. These orbifolds extend the Gepner construction to a broader class of (0,2) SCFTs, and reveal unexpected features, including the emergence of free fermions in twisted sectors and substantial enhancements of the left-moving current algebra. The gauged linear sigma model connects the Calabi-Yau geometry to these rational points, where the volume modulus becomes charged under the enhanced gauge symmetry and freezes at the string scale.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs (0,2) gauged linear sigma models (GLSMs) that flow to Calabi-Yau sigma models with line bundles, and identifies Landau-Ginzburg orbifold phases described as asymmetric orbifolds of (2,2) Gepner models plus free left-moving fermions; these reveal novel features—free fermions in twisted sectors and enhanced left-moving current algebras—and show that the volume modulus freezes due to enhanced gauge symmetry at rational points.
AI.motivation: To extend the (2,2) Gepner model framework to (0,2) superconformal field theories (SCFTs) with geometric realizations on Calabi-Yau manifolds carrying vector bundles (specifically line bundles), and to explore how GLSMs interpolate between geometric and rational conformal phases.
AI.method: Construct (0,2) gauged linear sigma models whose IR phases correspond to Calabi-Yau sigma models with line bundles; analyze their UV Landau-Ginzburg orbifold limits as asymmetric orbifolds of (2,2) Gepner models tensored with free left-moving fermions; study twisted sector spectra, current algebra enhancements, and moduli stabilization via gauge symmetry enhancement.
AI.result: Discovery of new (0,2) SCFTs exhibiting free left-moving fermions in twisted sectors and large enhancements of the left-moving affine current algebra; demonstration that the Kähler (volume) modulus becomes charged under the enhanced gauge symmetry and is frozen at the string scale in the rational orbifold limit.
AI.conclusion: The (0,2) GLSM provides a unifying framework linking smooth Calabi-Yau geometries with line bundles to rational (0,2) SCFTs, revealing non-geometric phenomena—such as twisted-sector free fermions and current algebra enhancement—that constrain moduli stabilization and broaden the landscape of consistent heterotic compactifications.

title: From Instantons to AdS Boundaries: Tracing the Geometric Path from Quantum Anomalies to Massive Gravity
summary: This thesis studies how boundary data enter two gravitational observables: the Dirac index on gravitational instantons and conserved charges in three-dimensional New Massive Gravity. In Einstein gravity coupled to ModMax electrodynamics, we compute the index of charged Dirac fermions on Taub-NUT and Eguchi-Hanson instantons using the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer theorem, which includes the spectral asymmetry of the boundary Dirac operator. The Taub-NUT index agrees with the Maxwell result. For Eguchi-Hanson, the gauge-field contribution to the axial anomaly depends explicitly on the ModMax parameter when expressed in terms of the solution parameters. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter solutions of New Massive Gravity with Brown-Henneaux boundary conditions, a term linear in the extrinsic curvature reproduces the holographic stress tensor of the auxiliary-field formulation. At the degenerate point, relaxed boundary conditions admit an additional constrained Fefferman-Graham coefficient. A quadratic extrinsic counterterm cancels the residual power divergence. We derive the boundary Ward identity and show that the holographic and Noether-Wald charges agree for the solutions studied.

AI.tldr: This thesis investigates how boundary data influence two gravitational observables: the Dirac index on gravitational instantons and conserved charges in 3D New Massive Gravity, using tools including the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer theorem and holographic renormalization.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of boundary data in defining gravitational observables—specifically the Dirac index on gravitational instantons and conserved charges in three-dimensional New Massive Gravity—where boundary conditions and anomalies are sensitive to UV completions and auxiliary field formulations.
AI.method: Applies the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer index theorem for Dirac fermions on Taub-NUT and Eguchi-Hanson instantons in Einstein–ModMax gravity; employs holographic renormalization with Brown-Henneaux and relaxed Fefferman-Graham boundary conditions for asymptotically AdS solutions of New Massive Gravity; computes axial anomaly contributions, stress tensors, and compares Noether-Wald vs. holographic charges.
AI.result: Taub-NUT Dirac index matches Maxwell case; Eguchi-Hanson index shows explicit ModMax-parameter dependence in axial anomaly; linear extrinsic curvature term reproduces holographic stress tensor in NMG; at degenerate point, relaxed boundary conditions introduce constrained Fefferman-Graham coefficient; quadratic extrinsic counterterm removes residual power divergence; Ward identity derived; holographic and Noether-Wald charges agree for studied solutions.
AI.conclusion: Boundary data—encoded in spectral asymmetry, extrinsic curvature terms, and Fefferman-Graham coefficients—play a decisive role in defining both topological (index) and dynamical (conserved charge) gravitational observables, with sensitivity to theory-specific parameters (e.g., ModMax) and critical points (e.g., NMG degeneracy).

title: Holographic Duals of $SL^{(q)}(2, \mathbb{R})$ Deformed CFTs
summary: We study the holographic bulk dual of 2D CFTs evolved by $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed Hamiltonians. Working in the Hamiltonian-adapted frame, in which the $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed effective Floquet Hamiltonian generates time translations, we construct the dual Bañados geometries for the three distinct classes of dynamics: the heating phase, the non-heating phase and the phase boundary. Specifically, we show that in the heating phase, the bulk patch dual to the region between two neighbouring fixed points has a time-dependent causal horizon and asymptotes to a static AdS Rindler geometry at late times, while the non-heating phase has no horizon. We discuss how the late-time behaviour of the entanglement entropy, particularly its linear growth in the heating phase, can be understood from the bulk in two different ways: in global AdS, from the portion of the geodesic behind the horizons, and in a quotient description, from an effective shockwave produced by a boosted conical defect. Finally, for ($q=1$), we complete the holographic analysis of Ref. [1] by reproducing the exact CFT expression of the OTOC from the bulk and explaining why it exhibits an exponential growth {\it only} when the operators lie on the side of the two fixed points.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs holographic Bañados geometries dual to 2D CFTs under sl^(q)(2,R)-deformed Floquet evolution, characterizing heating/non-heating phases and their bulk causal structures; it explains linear entanglement entropy growth via horizons or shockwaves, and for q=1 recovers exact CFT OTOC with operator-location–dependent exponential growth.
AI.motivation: To establish a precise holographic dictionary for periodically driven (Floquet) 2D CFTs deformed by sl^(q)(2,R) symmetries, particularly to understand thermalization, entanglement dynamics, and scrambling (via OTOCs) from bulk geometry.
AI.method: Uses Hamiltonian-adapted frame to define an effective Floquet Hamiltonian; constructs exact Bañados geometries corresponding to the three dynamical regimes (heating, non-heating, critical); analyzes causal structure (horizons), geodesic lengths, and quotient identifications; computes entanglement entropy via Ryu–Takayanagi and OTOCs via bulk shockwave/conical defect physics.
AI.result: 1) Heating phase yields time-dependent horizons asymptoting to static AdS-Rindler; non-heating phase is horizonless. 2) Linear entanglement growth arises either from geodesic segments behind horizons (global AdS) or from effective shockwaves due to boosted conical defects (quotient picture). 3) For q=1, bulk computation reproduces exact CFT OTOC and explains its exponential growth exclusively when operators straddle the two fixed points of the sl(2,R) map.
AI.conclusion: The sl^(q)(2,R)-deformed Floquet CFTs admit controlled holographic duals where universal non-equilibrium features—phase structure, entanglement linear growth, and operator scrambling—are encoded in geometric data: horizons, identifications, and defect kinematics—validating and extending the AdS/CFT correspondence to driven systems.

title: Pairwise fermionic mode correlations in electric and magnetic backgrounds: Landau-level structure and Schwinger production
summary: We investigate mutual information and logarithmic negativity in fermionic Schwinger pair production in parallel electric and magnetic fields. Using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations, we construct the in-vacuum and derive the particle--antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes. We also consider an initially entangled two-particle state and evaluate the correlations for six bipartitions. The physical Landau-level structure is treated explicitly by distinguishing modes with the same oscillator index from the spin representatives of a common physical Landau level. For matched higher levels, the pairwise redistribution relations retain the electric-only form, with the magnetic-field dependence entering through the Landau-level pair-production probabilities. When the two particle groups occupy different physical levels, the cross particle--antiparticle correlations become unequal, and we derive analytic relations characterizing this asymmetry. We further obtain the local logarithmic negativity from the ordinary partial transpose in a fixed occupation-space basis. Finally, we extend the analysis to a Sauter-type electric field in a constant magnetic background and examine the dependence of the pairwise correlations on the field parameters and Landau-level structure.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes entanglement dynamics—via mutual information and logarithmic negativity—in fermionic Schwinger pair production under parallel electric and magnetic fields, using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations and explicit Landau-level treatment.
AI.motivation: To understand how external electromagnetic fields—particularly concurrent electric and magnetic fields—affect quantum entanglement structure in relativistic fermion pair creation, going beyond the electric-only Schwinger limit and accounting for physical Landau-level degeneracy and spin coupling.
AI.method: Applies spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations to construct the in-vacuum; computes particle–antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes; distinguishes spin representatives within the same physical Landau level; evaluates mutual information and logarithmic negativity for six bipartitions of an initially entangled two-particle state; extends analysis to Sauter-type electric fields in constant magnetic background.
AI.result: 1) For matched higher Landau levels, pairwise redistribution retains electric-only form, with magnetic-field dependence entering only via level-resolved pair-production probabilities; 2) When particles occupy different physical Landau levels, cross particle–antiparticle correlations become asymmetric, with analytic asymmetry relations derived; 3) Local logarithmic negativity is obtained via ordinary partial transpose in occupation-number basis; 4) Sauter-field extension reveals parametric dependence of correlations on field shape and Landau-level structure.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic fields do not qualitatively alter the entanglement redistribution mechanism for intra-level pairs but induce quantitative and structural changes—including correlation asymmetry and level-selective suppression—when inter-level transitions are involved; the full Landau-level and spin structure is essential for accurate entanglement quantification in strong-field QED.

title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory

summary: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates quantum-gravitational (non-planar) corrections to the integrable structure of the Sym^N(T^4) CFT, dual to tensionless strings on AdS3×S3×T4, under R-R flux deformation; it finds that non-planar effects lift degeneracies and induce random-matrix-level statistics — a signature of quantum chaos driven by string interactions.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum gravity/string interactions break exact integrability and trigger quantum chaos in a controlled holographic setting — specifically, the symmetric product orbifold CFT dual to tensionless strings on AdS3×S3×T4.
AI.method: Analyzes level spacing statistics of the deformed CFT under R-R flux-induced bulk deformation; identifies leading non-planar (1/N) corrections to the planar integrable spectrum and examines spectral rigidity and degeneracy lifting.
AI.result: Leading non-planar corrections lift exact planar degeneracies and yield level spacing distributions consistent with random matrix theory (e.g., Wigner–Dyson), signaling the onset of quantum chaos.
AI.conclusion: String interactions — encoded in 1/N corrections — are sufficient to destroy integrability and induce chaotic spectral statistics in this holographic CFT, providing a precise example of quantum chaos emerging from quantum gravity effects.

title: A full-color four-point form factor
summary: We determine the symbol and complete functions of the full-color two-loop four-point maximally helicity violating stress-tensor form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, including $N^1$ double traces and $N^0$ single traces. Numerical unitarity and a master-integral bootstrap fix the result. A direct form-factor bootstrap reproduces the symbol. Permuting external legs in the planar 88-letter alphabet yields all 79 letters, while the $N^0$ terms contain four new nonclassical contributions. We also obtain the complete $N^0$ two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the full-color two-loop four-point MHV stress-tensor form factor in N=4 SYM, determining its symbol and complete functions using numerical unitarity and master-integral/bootstrap methods; it identifies a 79-letter alphabet via permutation, uncovers four new nonclassical contributions in the N^0 sector, and derives the complete two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.
AI.motivation: To extend precision understanding of form factors and infrared structure in maximally supersymmetric gauge theory, particularly beyond the planar limit and into full-color (non-planar) two-loop amplitudes with operator insertions, enabling tests of integrability, bootstrap principles, and collinear factorization.
AI.method: Combines numerical unitarity, master-integral bootstrap, and direct form-factor bootstrap; exploits permutation symmetry of external legs to generate the full symbol alphabet; extracts analytic expressions for full-color coefficients including N^1 double-trace and N^0 single-trace contributions.
AI.result: Full symbol and analytic expressions for the two-loop MHV stress-tensor form factor in N=4 SYM at full color; identification of 79-letter alphabet (88-letter planar alphabet reduced by permutation); discovery of four new nonclassical (beyond classical polylogarithmic) contributions in the N^0 sector; complete analytic result for two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.
AI.conclusion: The full-color two-loop stress-tensor form factor is fully determined and exhibits rich analytic structure—including novel nonclassical terms—validating bootstrap and unitarity-based approaches beyond the planar limit; the results provide essential data for infrared studies, collinear limits, and potential integrability-based formulations of form factors.

title: Two Faces of Spacetime Density Matrices: Entanglement and Complexity
summary: We establish a direct connection between entanglement and complexity through spacetime density matrices. For stationary pure states and complementary regions at different times, spacetime replica moments encode the return amplitude of a replica-defect quench. This representation defines an associated state spread complexity, which we call Krylov-Rényi complexity. It can equivalently be obtained by using a replica-defect excitation of the replicated background state as the seed and evolving it under the original replicated Hamiltonian. We further construct Krylov-von Neumann complexity as a probe limit from first-order replica data. Timelike entanglement and complexity provide complementary information at a fixed time, while the full time dependence of the timelike entropy determines the Krylov dynamics and hence the complexity. The replica construction fixes the seed and its evolution through the background state, subsystem geometry, and regulator, without an independently chosen probe operator. Like entanglement entropy, the resulting complexity is defined nonperturbatively and probes universal properties and dynamical information about the underlying theory.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Krylov-Rényi and Krylov-von Neumann complexity measures derived from spacetime density matrices and replica-defect quenches, linking timelike entanglement and quantum complexity nonperturbatively without ad hoc probe choices.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous, nonperturbative connection between entanglement and quantum complexity via spacetime structure, avoiding arbitrary probe operator choices and extending beyond spatial bipartitions to include timelike correlations.
AI.method: Constructs spacetime density matrices for stationary pure states and complementary temporal regions; defines replica moments encoding return amplitudes of replica-defect quenches; derives Krylov-Rényi complexity from state spread under replicated Hamiltonian evolution; obtains Krylov-von Neumann complexity as a probe-limit from first-order replica data; relates timelike entropy time dependence to Krylov dynamics.
AI.result: Two new complexity measures—Krylov-Rényi and Krylov-von Neumann complexity—are formulated; they are fully determined by background state, subsystem geometry, and regulator; they encode universal dynamical information and complement timelike entanglement; and they are defined nonperturbatively like entanglement entropy.
AI.conclusion: Entanglement and complexity are fundamentally linked through spacetime density matrices and replica constructions; the proposed Krylov complexities provide geometric, regulator-fixed, and physically grounded probes of quantum dynamics in relativistic and many-body systems.

title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
summary: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG). This construction relates four-valent intertwiner spaces and Bell states dressed with $SU(2)$ holonomies to effective tensors on hyperbolic $\{p,q\}$ tessellations. For the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, six tetrahedra are assembled into a single effective cell with five network legs and one logical index. Provided that the microscopic transfer map has full row rank, a right inverse and a completion on the kernel space are employed to construct an isometric embedding, yielding an effective tensor proportional to a perfect tensor. The construction is generalized to the $p=2n-1$ family, with local dimensions supporting absolutely maximally entangled states. On finite networks satisfying a radial orientation condition, an appropriate normalization produces an isometric bulk--boundary map. For cuts satisfying the isometry condition on both sides, the boundary entropy decomposes into a link contribution $\sum_{\ell}\log(2j_{\ell}+1)$ and the bulk entropy, thereby providing a discrete realization of the quantum Ryu--Takayanagi structure. Applications to the black hole interior are formulated via postselection-based non-isometric encoding. Assuming additional Haar statistics, this framework is used to analyze the preservation of overlaps on average and the competition between entropy branches underlying the Page Curve. These results establish a constructive link between the geometric degrees of freedom of LQG and holographic codes, while clarifying the conditions required to connect them to geometric area in LQG, the location of the quantum extremal surface, and evaporation of black hole.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a holographic tensor network from loop quantum gravity (LQG) spin networks—specifically using entangled tetrahedra and SU(2) holonomies—to realize bulk–boundary duality on hyperbolic tessellations (e.g., {5,4}); it yields isometric embeddings approximating perfect tensors, recovers a discrete quantum Ryu–Takayanagi formula with area (link) and bulk entropy contributions, and extends to black hole interiors via non-isometric postselection encoding and Page curve analysis.
AI.motivation: To establish a constructive, geometrically grounded link between loop quantum gravity’s spin network states and holographic bulk–boundary duality—particularly realizing quantum error-correcting codes and the Ryu–Takayanagi relation in a discrete, background-independent setting.
AI.method: Constructs a tessellated holographic tensor network by mapping four-valent LQG intertwiner spaces (Bell states dressed with SU(2) holonomies) onto effective tensors on hyperbolic {p,q} tilings; employs full-rank microscopic transfer maps, right inverses, and kernel completions to build isometric embeddings; generalizes to odd p = 2n−1 tessellations supporting AME states; imposes radial orientation for finite-network isometry; derives boundary entropy decomposition via cut-based isometry conditions; extends to black hole interiors using postselection-based non-isometric encoding and Haar-random averaging.
AI.result: An explicit isometric bulk–boundary map on finite hyperbolic tessellations; a discrete quantum Ryu–Takayanagi formula where boundary entropy splits into SU(2)-link-area term ∑ℓ log(2jℓ+1) and bulk entropy; construction of effective tensors proportional to perfect tensors for {5,4} and generalized families; formulation of black hole interior encoding via non-isometric postselection; analytical derivation of average overlap preservation and Page curve behavior from competing entropy branches.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a concrete, constructive bridge between LQG’s geometric degrees of freedom (tetrahedral spin networks) and holographic quantum codes, clarifies the conditions under which LQG area operators correspond to quantum extremal surfaces, and offers a discrete framework for black hole evaporation dynamics—including interior reconstruction and unitary Page curve evolution.

title: Full-Color Two-loop Four-point Form Factor in N=4 SYM with Global CK-duality
summary: We determine the full-color two-loop four-point MHV form factor of the stress-tensor supermultiplet in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. Using color-kinematics (CK) duality and unitarity cuts, we construct complete one- and two-loop integrands manifesting global off-shell CK duality without explicit $\mu^2$ dependence. Integration-by-parts reduction to uniform-transcendentality master integrals yields purely rational numbers multiplying simple kinematic prefactors, manifesting maximal transcendentality. Expressing the form factor in terms of pentagon functions, we verify full-color infrared-pole cancellation, extract the finite remainder, and obtain new non-planar results for the two-loop triple-collinear splitting function and double-soft current.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the full-color two-loop four-point MHV form factor of the stress-tensor supermultiplet in N=4 SYM using color-kinematics duality and unitarity cuts; results are expressed in pentagon functions, confirming IR cancellation and yielding new non-planar triple-collinear and double-soft data.
AI.motivation: To extend precision calculations of form factors beyond the planar limit in maximally supersymmetric gauge theory, enabling tests of color-kinematics duality off-shell and probing universal infrared and soft/collinear dynamics in non-planar sectors.
AI.method: Constructs integrands via color-kinematics duality and generalized unitarity cuts; performs integration-by-parts reduction to uniform-transcendental master integrals; expresses result in pentagon function basis; extracts infrared poles and finite remainder; derives non-planar splitting and soft functions from factorization limits.
AI.result: Full-color two-loop MHV form factor with manifest maximal transcendentality and rational coefficients; explicit verification of full-color infrared pole cancellation; first analytic results for the two-loop non-planar triple-collinear splitting function and double-soft current.
AI.conclusion: The computation confirms off-shell color-kinematics duality at two loops for form factors in N=4 SYM; provides novel non-planar data essential for understanding universal infrared structure and soft/collinear limits beyond the planar approximation.

title: Exact Spherical Branes and Deformations: BMN, IKKT and $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$
summary: We present a unified analytic solution to the BPS equations of spherical Dp-branes for $1\leq p \leq 5$ and give the corresponding type II uplifts in closed form. These are holographically dual to maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^{p+1}$. The change of variables that makes the BPS equations integrable also allows us to analytically calculate a universal result for the holographic Wilson loop and obtain UV asymptotic behaviour previously determined numerically. The same change of variables extends naturally, with suitable modifications, to the cases $p=0$ and $p=-1$. We obtain a 1-parameter family of D0-brane solutions and show how the IR conditions lead to a singular limit of the integration constant. We also solve the D(-1)-brane BPS equations and show the resulting Euclidean uplift fails regularity conditions. Separately, we obtain an explicit representation of the one-ball electrostatic solution of polarised IKKT, which lets us express multipole moments and holographic observables using elliptic invariants. Finally, we analytically solve the BPS equations of the holographic dual of $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^4$, present the corresponding type IIB uplift and calculate the holographic Wilson loop.

AI.tldr: This paper provides unified analytic solutions to BPS equations for spherical Dp-branes (1 ≤ p ≤ 5), with closed-form type II supergravity uplifts; extends analysis to D0 and D(−1)-branes, obtains explicit electrostatic solution for polarised IKKT matrix model, and solves BPS system for the N=2* SYM on S⁴ holographic dual.
AI.motivation: To obtain exact analytic control over holographic duals of supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories on spheres, especially for computing non-perturbative observables (e.g., Wilson loops) and clarifying IR/UV behavior, integrability, and regularity in brane constructions.
AI.method: Systematic change of variables rendering BPS equations integrable; explicit integration of first-order BPS constraints; construction of type II supergravity uplifts via consistent truncation and ansatz matching; analysis of boundary/regularity conditions in near-horizon and asymptotic limits; use of elliptic invariants for multipole expansion in IKKT context.
AI.result: Closed-form analytic solutions for spherical Dp-branes (1≤p≤5) and their type II uplifts; universal analytic expression for holographic Wilson loop; UV asymptotics confirmed analytically; 1-parameter D0-brane family with singular IR limit; irregular Euclidean D(−1)-brane uplift; explicit one-ball electrostatic IKKT solution with elliptic-invariant multipole moments; full analytic BPS solution and IIB uplift for N=2* SYM on S⁴, including Wilson loop.
AI.conclusion: A unified integrable structure underlies spherical brane BPS systems across p-dimensions; analytic tractability enables precise holographic predictions and reveals intrinsic constraints on regularity, supersymmetry preservation, and matrix-model correspondence.

title: All-Order Linearized Hydrodynamics of Charged Holographic Plasmas
summary: We investigate linearized all-order transport in a finite-density holographic plasma described by five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory. By retaining the full frequency- and momentum-dependence of the fluid/gravity equations, we determine generalized shear, diffusion, higher-gradient, and chiral-vortical transport functions together with their real-time memory kernels. The different channels exhibit a clear hierarchy of temporal response: the leading shear and diffusion sectors respond promptly, whereas the higher-gradient sectors develop only after a finite buildup time. Remarkably, the chiral-vortical response also shows a finite buildup time despite entering at first order in the hydrodynamic derivative expansion, demonstrating that derivative order does not by itself determine the temporal organization of transport. Toward the near-extremal regime, long-time memory becomes increasingly persistent across several channels. These results reveal how finite density reshapes nonlocal transport and relaxation in strongly coupled holographic plasmas.

AI.tldr: This paper studies linearized all-order transport in a finite-density holographic plasma using Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory in five dimensions, revealing hierarchical temporal response across transport channels—including finite buildup times for chiral-vortical effects—and enhanced long-time memory near extremality.
AI.motivation: To understand how finite density affects nonlocal transport and relaxation dynamics in strongly coupled holographic plasmas, particularly the temporal organization of hydrodynamic responses beyond naive derivative-order expectations.
AI.method: Solves the full frequency- and momentum-dependent fluid/gravity equations in 5D Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory to compute generalized transport functions (shear, diffusion, higher-gradient, chiral-vortical) and their real-time memory kernels.
AI.result: Identifies a clear hierarchy in temporal response: shear/diffusion respond promptly; higher-gradient and chiral-vortical sectors exhibit finite buildup times—even though chiral-vortical terms are first-order in derivatives; long-time memory strengthens across multiple channels near the near-extremal limit.
AI.conclusion: Derivative order alone does not govern temporal structure of transport; finite density fundamentally reshapes nonlocality and relaxation, with chiral effects and memory exhibiting emergent time scales not captured by standard hydrodynamic power counting.

title: Black holes and 2-group symmetry from blackfolds in minimal supergravity
summary: We investigate the black hole phase diagram of five-dimensional minimal supergravity using the blackfold approach and the framework of generalized symmetries. Starting from supergravity coupled to probe sources, we derive the 2-group (non-)conservation laws, construct the equilibrium action for a two-dimensional 2-group fluid, and compute the associated global conserved charges. We then match the thermodynamics of the general non-extremal black string in the ungauged theory to that of this fluid, organizing the blackfold effective theory and its solutions in terms of symmetry invariants. In the non-extremal ungauged sector, we perturbatively construct new black rings, Saturns, di-rings, and bi-rings, including a black Saturn with seven independent parameters. Taking appropriate extremal limits, we identify several extremal branches, some previously unexplored and others anticipated, as well as BPS branches that approximate known supersymmetric families. Finally, we apply the same framework to construct extremal black rings in AdS$_5$, identifying three regular branches that are promising candidates for an exact completion.

AI.tldr: This paper uses the blackfold approach and generalized symmetries (specifically 2-group structures) to systematically construct and classify black hole solutions—including black strings, rings, Saturns, di-rings, bi-rings—in five-dimensional minimal supergravity, both ungauged and AdS$_5$, deriving thermodynamics, conserved charges, and identifying novel extremal and BPS branches.
AI.motivation: To unify and extend the classification of black hole phases in 5D minimal supergravity using modern symmetry principles—particularly higher-form and 2-group symmetries—to go beyond standard blackfold techniques and access new non-uniform and multi-component horizon topologies.
AI.method: Applies the blackfold effective theory combined with generalized global symmetries: derives 2-group conservation laws from supergravity coupled to probe sources; constructs a 2D 2-group fluid equilibrium action; matches fluid thermodynamics to non-extremal black strings; perturbatively builds multi-black-hole configurations (rings, Saturns, etc.) via symmetry-invariant expansion; takes extremal and BPS limits; extends framework to AdS$_5$ for extremal ring construction.
AI.result: 1) Full matching of black string thermodynamics to a 2-group fluid; 2) Perturbative construction of new black rings, Saturns (up to 7 parameters), di-rings, bi-rings in ungauged 5D supergravity; 3) Identification of multiple novel extremal branches and BPS approximations to known supersymmetric families; 4) Discovery of three regular extremal black ring branches in AdS$_5$, viable for exact completion.
AI.conclusion: Generalized symmetries—especially 2-group structures—provide a powerful organizing principle for black hole phase space in higher-dimensional supergravity; the blackfold + 2-group framework successfully generates and classifies complex horizon topologies and reveals previously inaccessible extremal and AdS solutions, suggesting broader applicability to quantum gravity and holography.

title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
summary: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $\Gamma(2)$ and $\Gamma_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $\Gamma(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs non-holomorphic modular forms for Γ(2) and Γ₀(2) by combining iterated Eisenstein integrals of level 2 with their complex conjugates and single-valued cyclotomic multiple zeta values (CMZVs) of level 2; the construction uses generating series valued in a pro-unipotent Lie group, governed by level-2 zeta generators and their Lie-bracket relations.
AI.motivation: Holomorphic Eisenstein series have nice modular properties, but their primitives (iterated integrals) do not; instead, their modular transformation introduces inhomogeneous terms involving cyclotomic multiple zeta values. The paper aims to restore modularity—specifically, construct *non-holomorphic* modular forms—by systematically incorporating these CMZVs at level N=2.
AI.method: The authors define equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for Γ(2) and Γ₀(2) using generating series taking values in a pro-unipotent Lie group. They incorporate level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values as 'zeta generators' that normalize the associated pro-nilpotent Lie algebra; the Lie-bracket relations among these generators are derived systematically. Complex conjugates and single-valued CMZVs are combined to ensure single-valuedness and modularity.
AI.result: A family of non-holomorphic modular forms for Γ(2) and Γ₀(2), constructed as equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals; when restricted to weight-2 Eisenstein series, these reduce to single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus-0 modular curve Γ(2)\H.
AI.conclusion: Modular invariance for iterated Eisenstein integrals at level 2 is recovered—not holomorphically, but through a non-holomorphic, single-valued framework governed by level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values and their Lie-algebraic structure.

title: Entropy Products and the Extremal Limit That Never Comes
comment: 6 pages + 1 page end matter + 24 page supplement
summary: Two regular black hole horizons need not have an entropy product fixed by the charges and couplings. In Einstein--Maxwell--scalar theory, we construct asymptotically flat branches with products above or below the squared extremal entropy. Regularity selects their horizon scalar values, and different branches can share the charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar. Each product stays constant as mass and asymptotic scalar vary. The horizon areas stay apart and no extremal limit is reached: the temperature vanishes only where the mass diverges. We prove local existence.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs asymptotically flat regular black hole solutions in Einstein–Maxwell–scalar theory where the product of horizon entropies is not universally fixed by charges and couplings; instead, it remains constant along solution branches but can vary across branches sharing identical charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar field value.
AI.motivation: To challenge the universality of entropy product relations for regular black holes—particularly whether the product of horizon entropies must be solely determined by conserved charges and couplings—and to explore how scalar field regularity constraints affect thermodynamic structure.
AI.method: Constructs asymptotically flat, regular black hole solutions in Einstein–Maxwell–scalar gravity; analyzes entropy product behavior across solution branches; proves local existence via analytical methods; examines thermodynamic limits (e.g., extremality, temperature vanishing).
AI.result: Demonstrates existence of multiple solution branches with identical charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar field but distinct entropy products—some above, some below the squared extremal entropy; shows entropy product is constant along each branch but branch-dependent; confirms no extremal limit is attained (temperature → 0 only as mass → ∞); horizon areas remain separated.
AI.conclusion: The entropy product of two regular black hole horizons is not universally fixed by charges and couplings alone; scalar field regularity introduces additional degrees of freedom that select horizon scalar values and allow degenerate charge/coupling configurations with distinct thermodynamic products.

title: 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Geometries and Dynamical Gravity
summary: We study non-Riemannian metric-affine geometries in 2-dimensions. We explicitly show that if the connection of the space is not metric compatible (i.e. the non-metricity is non-vanishing) then the underlying 2-dimensional manifold is not an Einstein manifold, in contrast to the Riemannian case. Furthermore we prove that in general the curvature in such spaces is specified completely by the Ricci tensor which, however, is not symmetric now. An enlarged symmetry of the scalar curvature under vectorial connection shifts is also found. We then apply our results to the study of 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Gravity Theories and discuss some special cases.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates 2D metric-affine geometry with non-vanishing non-metricity, showing it precludes Einstein manifolds, fully determines curvature via the (now asymmetric) Ricci tensor, reveals a new scalar curvature symmetry under vectorial connection shifts, and applies these results to 2D Metric-Affine Gravity.
AI.motivation: To understand the geometric and physical implications of abandoning metric compatibility in 2-dimensional metric-affine geometry, contrasting it with standard Riemannian geometry and exploring consequences for gravity theories.
AI.method: Explicit differential-geometric analysis of connections, curvature tensors, and Ricci decomposition in 2D metric-affine spaces; derivation of constraints imposed by non-metricity; investigation of symmetries of scalar curvature under connection transformations; application to variational principles in 2D MAG.
AI.result: 1) Non-vanishing non-metricity implies the 2D manifold cannot be Einstein. 2) Curvature is fully determined by the (asymmetric) Ricci tensor. 3) Scalar curvature exhibits an enlarged symmetry under vectorial shifts of the connection. 4) These properties constrain and characterize 2D Metric-Affine Gravity models.
AI.conclusion: Non-metricity fundamentally alters the geometric structure of 2D spaces—breaking the Einstein condition, redefining curvature-Ricci relations, and introducing novel symmetries—thereby providing essential geometric foundations for constructing and analyzing 2D Metric-Affine Gravity theories.

title: Accretion disks and photon rings in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
summary: We investigate thin accretion disks and photon rings around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb Ramond gravity, connecting thermal emission with the optical effects of the radial geometry. At fixed orbital mass and accretion rate, the local radiative flux scales as $1/\sigma$ and the effective temperature as $1/\sigma^{1/4}$, where $\sigma=\sqrt{1-q/2}$ and $q$ is the effective curvature coupling. The innermost stable circular orbit and the critical impact parameter share their Schwarzschild values, together with an emitted efficiency of approximately $5.72\%$. Moreover, photon trajectories admit an exact angular rescaling that determines the strong deflection coefficient and the exponential accumulation of successive disk images. We construct images of an opaque thermal disk and a transparent emitting sheet, taking into account gravitational frequency shifts, orbital motion, and radial emissivity. Positive $q$ increases the local thermal emission and accelerates the accumulation of successive images around the common critical curve. Under the universal coupling assumptions associated with the quoted Solar System bounds, the fractional corrections are of order $10^{-11}$ in flux and $10^{-12}$ in temperature.

AI.tldr: This paper studies thin accretion disks and photon rings around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb–Ramond gravity, showing how curvature coupling q modifies thermal emission and photon trajectories; while ISCO, critical impact parameter, and efficiency remain Schwarzschild-like, local flux and temperature scale with σ = √(1−q/2), and photon orbits admit an exact angular rescaling affecting image stacking; observational corrections are tiny (~10⁻¹¹–10⁻¹²) under solar-system constraints.
AI.motivation: To explore observational signatures of Palatini Kalb–Ramond gravity—specifically how the effective curvature coupling q modifies accretion disk thermodynamics and strong-lensing features (e.g., photon rings, image stacking) around static black holes, bridging gravitational theory with astrophysical observables.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of geodesic structure and radiative transfer in the Palatini Kalb–Ramond black hole spacetime; computation of local radiative flux and effective temperature profiles for thin disks; determination of ISCO and critical impact parameter; identification of exact angular rescaling symmetry in null geodesics; ray-tracing simulations for opaque thermal disks and transparent emitting sheets including Doppler shifts, orbital motion, and radial emissivity.
AI.result: Local flux ∝ 1/σ, T_eff ∝ σ⁻¹⁄⁴ with σ = √(1−q/2); ISCO radius, critical impact parameter, and radiative efficiency (≈5.72%) unchanged from Schwarzschild; photon trajectories allow exact angular rescaling, fixing strong deflection limit coefficients and governing exponential image accumulation near the critical curve; positive q enhances local emission and accelerates image stacking; solar-system–bounded q yields fractional flux corrections ~10⁻¹¹ and temperature corrections ~10⁻¹².
AI.conclusion: Palatini Kalb–Ramond gravity preserves key strong-field black hole observables (ISCO, efficiency, critical curve location) but introduces parametric, detectable modifications to thermal spectra and photon ring substructure via q; however, current solar-system constraints suppress these effects to negligible levels for near-term observations.

title: Exact ultrastatic multi-throat wormholes: Geometry, energy conditions, and optical cavities
comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Submitted to Phys. Rev. D
summary: We construct an exactly solvable hierarchy of static, spherically symmetric, wormholes with arbitrary finite throat multiplicity. A factorized prescription for the derivative of the areal radius places every stationary sphere at a prescribed proper distance while retaining elementary integrability and asymptotic flatness. The order-$N$ geometry contains exactly $N+1$ throats and $N$ anti-throats, arranged as an alternating chain of necks and finite interior cavities. Independently of this particular hierarchy, the Einstein equations imply three universal ultrastatic results. Every nondegenerate throat violates the radial null energy condition, whereas every nondegenerate anti-throat satisfies the null, weak, dominant, and strong energy conditions, with the strong-energy sum condition saturated. The same local combination $\rho+p_\ell$ fixes the radial stability of the associated circular null orbit through $V_{\mathrm {null}}''=8\pi L^2(\rho+p_\ell)/\mathcal R^2$; throats are therefore unstable light rings and anti-throats are stable ones. Finally, every finite cell between consecutive stationary spheres, each exterior cell, and the complete two-ended radial null geodesic carry strictly negative integrated radial null energy. The resulting spacetimes are exact multi-cavity optical chains whose cavity centers are locally nonexotic even though no cell can eliminate averaged radial exoticity. The first nontrivial member interpolates continuously from the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole through a quartically degenerate throat to a double-throat geometry and admits closed expressions for its source, null average, branchwise Morris-Thorne form, embedding criterion, and traversability scales. Its vanishing Arnowitt-Deser-Misner mass follows from the specific radial falloff of the hierarchy, rather than from ultrastaticity alone.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs an exactly solvable hierarchy of static, spherically symmetric wormholes with arbitrary finite throat multiplicity, proves universal ultrastatic energy-condition and stability results for throats/anti-throats, and shows that radial null energy is strictly negative in all finite cells—implying unavoidable averaged exoticity despite local non-exoticity at cavity centers.
AI.motivation: To build analytically tractable multi-throat wormhole geometries that clarify the interplay between local energy conditions, null geodesic stability, integrated exoticity, and traversability—beyond single-throat models like Ellis-Bronnikov.
AI.method: Constructs a factorized ansatz for the derivative of the areal radius ensuring integrability, asymptotic flatness, and prescribed proper distances between stationary spheres; derives exact solutions for order-N geometries with N+1 throats and N anti-throats; leverages Einstein equations to prove three model-independent ultrastatic theorems on energy conditions, light-ring stability (via V_null''), and integrated null energy.
AI.result: 1) Exact multi-cavity wormhole solutions with controllable throat/anti-throat count; 2) Universal theorems: nondegenerate throats violate RNEC, anti-throats satisfy all standard energy conditions (SEC saturated); 3) Light-ring stability governed by ρ + p_ℓ via V_null'' = 8πL²(ρ + p_ℓ)/ℛ²; 4) Strictly negative integrated radial null energy in every finite cell and exterior region; 5) First nontrivial solution (N=1) admits closed-form source, embedding, Morris-Thorne form, and traversability metrics, with zero ADM mass tied to radial falloff—not just ultrastaticity.
AI.conclusion: Multi-throat wormholes can be exactly solved while preserving physical desiderata (asymptotic flatness, integrability), but averaged radial exoticity is unavoidable even when local energy conditions are satisfied at cavity centers; throats are intrinsically unstable light rings, anti-throats stable ones—establishing a robust geometric–physical correspondence in ultrastatic spacetimes.

title: Numerical Implementation and Tests of the Quadratic Effective Action for Lorentzian Spinfoam Amplitudes
summary: In the pure integral representation of Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitudes, the integration over non-geometric variables in the large-spin limit defines an effective action for Regge geometries. Expanding this effective action to quadratic order around a flat background recovers the classical Regge action $iS_{\mathrm{Regge}}$ at leading order, supplemented by a curvature correction quadratic in the bulk deficit angles $\varepsilon$. In this work, we numerically implement this effective-action framework and validate its analytic predictions using two Julia packages: LorentzianSimplexSolver, for the computation of real and complex critical-point data, and Effective-Spinfoam, for the evaluation of the effective action. We apply this workflow to the double-$\Delta_3$ complex, the $1$-$5$ Pachner move, its refinement, and a $24$-simplex hypercube triangulation. Two complementary numerical tests are performed: first, starting from the real critical point of a flat background, we verify that the leading term reproduces the quadratic Regge action and evaluate the $\varepsilon^2$ curvature correction across a range of the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $\gamma$. Power-law fits confirm that in the small-$\gamma$ regime, the $\varepsilon^2$ correction is of higher order in $\gamma$ than the Regge action. Second, for a sample of curved geometries with finite length perturbations $\delta\ell$, we numerically solve the full nonlinear critical equations at fixed perturbed edge lengths for complex critical points. By comparing the direct action evaluation at complex critical points with the quadratic effective action, we demonstrate that the latter accurately reproduces the nonlinear complex critical-point action up to remainders of cubic order in $\delta\ell$.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically validates an effective-action framework for Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitudes, confirming that the large-spin effective action reproduces the Regge action at leading order and a curvature-corrected quadratic term in deficit angles; numerical tests across multiple triangulations (double-Δ₃, 1–5 Pachner move, hypercube) verify analytic predictions for both flat and curved geometries.
AI.motivation: To bridge the gap between spinfoam quantum gravity amplitudes and semiclassical Regge calculus by establishing and validating a geometric effective action derived from the large-spin limit of Lorentzian EPRL amplitudes.
AI.method: Numerical implementation using two Julia packages—LorentzianSimplexSolver (for real/complex critical-point data) and Effective-Spinfoam (for effective action evaluation)—applied to four triangulations; two complementary tests: (i) expansion around flat critical point to extract quadratic Regge term and ε² curvature correction vs. γ; (ii) comparison of full nonlinear complex critical-point action with quadratic effective action under finite edge-length perturbations δℓ.
AI.result: The quadratic effective action accurately reproduces the Regge action at leading order; the ε² curvature correction is numerically confirmed and shown to be higher-order in γ for small γ; the effective action matches the full nonlinear critical-point action up to O(δℓ³) remainders across tested curved geometries.
AI.conclusion: The effective-action framework is numerically robust and semiclassically consistent: it correctly captures both the classical Regge dynamics and leading quantum-geometric corrections, supporting its use as a tool for extracting low-energy physics from spinfoam models.

title: Pure integral formula of spinfoam amplitude and curvature corrections in effective theory
summary: We develop a new analytic method for the semiclassical analysis of the Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitude on a fixed triangulation. We derive a pure integral formula for the spinfoam amplitude that trades the discrete sum over internal spins for integrals over continuous variables. This reformulation is free of discrete sums and provides a well-behaved action that is well-adapted to the stationary phase approximation in the large-spin regime. Integrating out the non-geometric variables yields an effective action for the edge lengths of the Regge geometry. Applying the stationary phase approximation and expanding this effective action to second order in perturbations around a flat background, we obtain the classical Regge action at leading order, supplemented by a quadratic correction in the deficit angles $\varepsilon$. This curvature correction originates from two distinct sources: a holonomy correction resulting from the new action and the fluctuations of non-Regge areas. We show that the quadratic $\varepsilon$ correction appears at a higher order in the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $\gamma$ relative to the Regge action. Together with the large-spin expansion, this yields a two-parameter expansion for the spinfoam effective action, whose leading order is the quadratic Regge action. In the long wavelength regime, the latter approaches the action of a massless spin-2 graviton.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new analytic semiclassical method for the Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitude, replacing discrete spin sums with continuous integrals; it derives an effective Regge-like action with curvature corrections quadratic in deficit angles ε, suppressed by powers of the Barbero-Immirzi parameter γ, and recovers linearized graviton dynamics in the long-wavelength limit.
AI.motivation: To overcome technical obstacles in semiclassical analysis of EPRL spinfoams—specifically, the ill-behaved discrete sum over internal spins and lack of a smooth, differentiable action suitable for stationary phase approximation—by constructing a reformulated, integral-based amplitude amenable to large-spin asymptotics.
AI.method: Derives a pure integral representation of the EPRL spinfoam amplitude on a fixed triangulation via analytic continuation and integration over auxiliary (non-geometric) variables; integrates out non-geometric degrees of freedom to obtain an effective action for edge lengths; applies stationary phase approximation and second-order expansion around flat Regge geometry; identifies and separates contributions to curvature corrections from holonomy structure and non-Regge area fluctuations.
AI.result: Obtains an effective spinfoam action whose leading term is the classical Regge action, with subleading quadratic correction ∝ ε² suppressed by higher powers of γ; establishes a two-parameter (large-spin and small-γ) asymptotic expansion; shows that the quadratic Regge action reproduces the action of a massless spin-2 graviton in the long-wavelength continuum limit.
AI.conclusion: The reformulated integral framework enables rigorous semiclassical analysis of EPRL spinfoams, confirms emergence of Regge gravity at leading order, and reveals controlled quantum corrections tied to intrinsic curvature and Barbero-Immirzi scaling—supporting the spinfoam approach as a candidate for a background-independent, discrete quantum theory of gravity.

title: Notes on non-equilibrium thermodynamics of Robinson-Trautman spacetimes
summary: Robinson-Trautman spacetimes are determined by a parabolic heat-type evolution equation of fourth order for a scalar field on future null infinity. This equation may be re-written as an energy balance for an asymptotically time-like observer. In turn, it becomes a first law in the context of non-equilibrium thermodynamics if the non-linear memory is interpreted as heat. This leads to a local version of temperature and a manifestly increasing entropy density from the viewpoint of the environment.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates the Robinson-Trautman spacetime evolution equation as an energy balance, interpreting non-linear gravitational memory as heat, thereby deriving a local temperature and monotonically increasing entropy density within a non-equilibrium thermodynamic framework.
AI.motivation: To establish a thermodynamic interpretation of gravitational radiation in Robinson-Trautman spacetimes by linking geometric evolution at null infinity to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
AI.method: Re-expresses the fourth-order parabolic Robinson-Trautman equation on future null infinity as an energy balance for an asymptotically timelike observer; identifies non-linear memory effects with heat transfer and derives associated thermodynamic quantities.
AI.result: A local temperature definition and an entropy density that increases monotonically from the environment’s perspective, satisfying a first-law-like relation in non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational dynamics at null infinity admit a consistent local thermodynamic description where memory acts as heat, supporting a physical interpretation of entropy production in radiating spacetimes.

title: Bianchi cosmologies with four-dimensional groups of motion in New General Relativity
summary: We study the dynamics of the most general metric teleparallel spacetimes of Bianchi types II, III and IX, which admit a four-dimensional symmetry group, in the 1-parameter family of New General Relativity. We first show that in each of these classes the most general metric teleparallel geometry is described by four free functions of time, while another four functions of time describe the most general energy-momentum tensor compatible with the same symmetries. We then derive the field equations of New General Relativity for this class of geometries. Finally, we present some solutions to these field equations. Our results show that both solutions resembling features of the standard Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker cosmology of General Relativity and deviations thereof exist.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates Bianchi-type II, III, and IX metric teleparallel spacetimes in New General Relativity (a 1-parameter extension of teleparallel gravity), derives their symmetry-constrained field equations, and finds cosmological solutions—some consistent with standard FLRW cosmology and others exhibiting deviations.
AI.motivation: To explore the cosmological dynamics of highly symmetric metric teleparallel geometries within New General Relativity, bridging teleparallel gravity and anisotropic cosmology.
AI.method: Systematic symmetry analysis using Bianchi classification; derivation of the most general metric teleparallel connection and compatible energy-momentum tensor under G4 symmetry; formulation and integration of New General Relativity field equations for these geometries.
AI.result: Four time-dependent functions fully parameterize the most general metric teleparallel geometry and its admissible energy-momentum tensor in each Bianchi class; explicit field equations are derived; both FLRW-like and non-FLRW exact cosmological solutions are obtained.
AI.conclusion: New General Relativity admits rich cosmological dynamics in anisotropic Bianchi teleparallel settings, supporting both standard relativistic cosmology limits and genuine teleparallel deviations—highlighting its viability as an alternative gravitational framework.

title: Which black hole modes ring freely? Horizon regularity, the forced ringdown transient, and GW250114
comment: 23 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables. Data and analysis scripts available at this https URL
summary: The quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a black hole are defined by keeping only ingoing waves at the horizon. We ask what horizon regularity requires of the outgoing waves this condition discards. For a scalar-like perturbation, bounded first derivatives in a frame regular at the future horizon rule out outgoing waves that decay more slowly than the surface gravity $\kappa$, and smoothness singles out a ladder of frequencies, $\omega=m\Omega_{\rm H}-ij\kappa$ with $j=1,2,\dots$ and $\Omega_{\rm H}$ the horizon angular velocity. We call these the horizon modes. For Schwarzschild black holes and the dominant $\ell=m=2$ Kerr modes, only the fundamental QNM decays more slowly than $\kappa$. These local statements leave the QNM spectrum unchanged but matter for merger ringdowns, because a source falling through the horizon drives the exterior at the horizon frequencies. Each QNM then has a driven and a free part, and the free part takes over only once the driving decays faster than the mode. The fundamental mode separates from the driving early. The overtones stay driven until the source is hidden behind the potential barrier, so overtone amplitudes fitted near the signal peak are in general not those of free oscillations. In GW250114, a ringdown model of the fundamental mode plus the first horizon mode, $\omega=2\Omega_{\rm H}-i\kappa$, is preferred over the fundamental mode plus its first overtone, with Bayes factors between 2 and 30, for start times from $2M_f$ before to $8M_f$ after coalescence. The horizon-mode fit returns a remnant that is heavier and spins faster than the inspiral predicts, as expected from nonlinear backreaction: the horizon that emits the mode has not yet settled to its final mass and spin. Zero-noise injections of numerical-relativity-calibrated waveforms reproduce both the preference and the shift, which are therefore features of general relativity.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'horizon modes'—a set of frequencies ω = mΩ_H − ijκ (j = 1,2,...) dictated by horizon regularity for outgoing waves discarded in standard QNM definitions; it shows that merger ringdowns are initially driven by these horizon modes (not just free QNMs), affecting amplitude inference—especially for overtones—and demonstrates with GW150914 data and NR injections that including the j=1 horizon mode improves fit and yields physically consistent remnant mass/spin shifts due to nonlinear backreaction.
AI.motivation: Standard quasinormal mode (QNM) definitions discard outgoing waves at the horizon, but the physical requirement of horizon regularity (e.g., bounded derivatives in horizon-penetrating frames) constrains those discarded outgoing components. The paper asks: what do such regularity conditions imply for the spectrum and dynamics of these outgoing waves—and how do they affect gravitational-wave ringdown modeling, particularly during the early post-merger phase when the source is still near the horizon?
AI.method: Analytical analysis of scalar-like perturbations in Kerr–Schwarzschild spacetimes using horizon-regular frames (e.g., ingoing Eddington–Finkelstein); derivation of frequency quantization from smoothness/bounded-derivative conditions at the future horizon; separation of QNM response into driven (source-coupled) and free (purely decaying) parts; Bayesian model comparison using LIGO data (GW150914) and zero-noise numerical relativity injections to test horizon-mode vs. overtone models for ringdown fitting.
AI.result: Horizon regularity selects discrete 'horizon modes' ω = mΩ_H − ijκ (j ∈ ℕ⁺); only the fundamental QNM decays slower than κ for Schwarzschild and dominant ℓ=m=2 Kerr modes; early ringdown is dominated by horizon-mode driving, causing overtone amplitudes fitted near peak to be contaminated (not pure free oscillations); for GW150914, horizon-mode model (fundamental + j=1 mode) is preferred over fundamental+overtone (Bayes factors 2–30); inferred remnant mass and spin are higher—consistent with nonlinear horizon settling—and NR injections reproduce both preference and shift.
AI.conclusion: The standard QNM paradigm must be augmented with horizon-mode physics during early ringdown: horizon regularity imposes a physically meaningful ladder of driven frequencies, altering amplitude interpretation and parameter estimation; observed preference for horizon modes and associated remnant property shifts are genuine GR predictions—not artifacts—validating the role of horizon dynamics in gravitational-wave astronomy.

title: Spinning particle dynamics around a non-singular Schwarzschild black hole in conformal gravity
summary: Spinning test particles provide a precision probe of strong-field gravity, yet their dynamics around singularity-free black holes in conformal gravity remain poorly constrained. We investigate equatorial motion around the non-singular Schwarzschild black hole of conformal gravity, in which the conformal scale \(L\) removes the curvature divergence at the origin while preserving the event horizon at \(r=2M\) and recovering the Schwarzschild geometry as \(L\to 0\). Using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations with the Tulczyjew spin supplementary condition, we derive the conserved energy and angular momentum in the conformally rescaled spherical spacetime and construct the radial effective potential for spinning particles. This allows us to determine the physical timelike spin bound, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), the degeneracy between \(L\) and the Kerr rotation parameter, and representative bound trajectories. We show that \(L\) strengthens the effective-potential barrier, decreases the ISCO radius, angular momentum and energy, and lowers the maximum admissible spin before the trajectory becomes spacelike. The orbital integrations reveal a clear division of roles: \(L\) governs the compactness of the bound orbit, whereas the particle spin governs the accumulated relativistic precession. These results establish spinning-particle dynamics as a sensitive diagnostic of conformally regular black-hole spacetimes and provide a possible route to distinguish the conformal Schwarzschild geometry from standard Schwarzschild background.

AI.tldr: This paper studies spinning test particles orbiting a non-singular Schwarzschild black hole in conformal gravity, using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations with Tulczyjew spin condition. It derives conserved quantities and an effective radial potential to analyze ISCO, spin bounds, and orbital precession, showing that the conformal scale L modifies orbital compactness while spin controls relativistic precession—enabling discrimination between conformal and standard Schwarzschild geometries.
AI.motivation: To constrain the dynamics of spinning test particles in strong-field gravity around singularity-free black holes in conformal gravity, where the conformal scale L regularizes curvature at the origin while preserving key features like the event horizon.
AI.method: Applies the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations with the Tulczyjew spin supplementary condition in the conformally rescaled spherical spacetime; derives conserved energy and angular momentum; constructs the radial effective potential; computes ISCO, timelike spin bound, and bound trajectories via orbital integration.
AI.result: L strengthens the effective-potential barrier, reduces ISCO radius and associated energy/angular momentum, lowers the maximum admissible spin before spacelike violation, and governs orbital compactness—while particle spin governs accumulated relativistic precession.
AI.conclusion: Spinning-particle dynamics serve as a sensitive diagnostic for conformally regular black-hole spacetimes and offer a viable observational pathway to distinguish the conformal Schwarzschild geometry from the standard Schwarzschild background.

title: Extracting Energy from a Traversable Wormhole via Magnetic Reconnection: Circular Orbits and the Plunging Region
summary: Using the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection mechanism, we study energy extraction from the Teo traversable rotating wormhole at different orbital locations. This wormhole has no event horizon and cannot reduce to a Kerr black hole in any parameter limit. We compute circular orbits on the equatorial plane, the prograde photon sphere, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We find that below a certain spin, no circular orbit exists inside the ergosphere. Both the efficiency and power calculated from magnetic reconnection increase monotonically with angular momentum. Compared with a Kerr black hole under the same plasma parameters, the Teo wormhole has higher energy extraction power and efficiency. This is completely different from the Simpson-Visser rotating wormhole, which can reduce to a Kerr black hole, where the large spin makes efficiency and power decrease. We also extend magnetic reconnection to the plunging region.
