We find that when the spin is not particularly high, the energy extraction power and efficiency in the plunging region are higher than those in the circular orbit region, while for very high spin the situation is reversed. This conclusion also differs from that obtained from a Kerr black hole, where the power and efficiency in the plunging region are always higher than those in the circular orbit region.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates magnetic reconnection–driven energy extraction from the Teo rotating traversable wormhole using the Comisso-Asenjo mechanism, finding higher efficiency and power than Kerr black holes—unlike Simpson-Visser wormholes—and reveals spin-dependent reversal of plunging vs. circular-orbit energy extraction dominance.
AI.motivation: To explore whether horizonless, non-Kerr-like rotating wormholes (specifically the Teo wormhole) can serve as more efficient astrophysical energy sources via magnetic reconnection than Kerr black holes, and to contrast their behavior with Kerr-reducible wormholes.
AI.method: Applied the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection model to compute energy extraction efficiency and power across equatorial circular orbits, photon sphere, ISCO, and the plunging region of the Teo wormhole; compared results with Kerr black hole and Simpson-Visser wormhole benchmarks under identical plasma parameters.
AI.result: Teo wormhole yields monotonically increasing efficiency and power with spin—exceeding Kerr's—due to absence of horizon and non-Kerr geometry; below critical spin, no circular orbits exist inside ergosphere; for moderate spin, plunging-region extraction dominates circular-orbit extraction, but reverses at very high spin—unlike Kerr, where plunging always dominates.
AI.conclusion: The Teo wormhole is a superior energy extractor via magnetic reconnection relative to Kerr black holes and exhibits qualitatively distinct spin-dependent behavior in orbital and plunging regions, highlighting the role of global spacetime structure (e.g., horizonlessness and non-Kerr limits) in relativistic plasma energy conversion.

title: Probing the Graviton Mass through the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background Last-Scattering Surface
summary: A nonzero graviton mass makes gravitational waves of different momenta travel different distances during the same cosmic interval. A relic stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) with a finite momentum bandwidth therefore samples a shell of finite thickness, rather than the thin source shell of massless propagation from a single epoch. We describe this effective last-scattering surface by mapping the momentum and emission-time distribution into a radial visibility window in an FLRW background. The calculation uses the geometric-optics propagation relation and includes both dispersion and finite emission duration, without a small-mass or narrow-band approximation. We then calculate how radial averaging changes the angular power for an early-produced background whose momentum channels trace a common source-fluctuation field. For a scale-invariant source spectrum, moving a thin shell leaves its angular power unchanged, so the reduction in power isolates the effect of its finite thickness. For a logarithmic momentum width of $0.5$, mass-to-momentum ratios $q=0.3,1,3$ give angular-power ratios of approximately $0.974$, $0.771$, and $0.508$ at $\ell=10$. At a representative frequency of $3\,\mathrm{nHz}$, these ratios correspond to masses of approximately $3.6\times10^{-24}$--$1.2\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}$. We establish a framework that maps the graviton mass to the SGWB angular power spectrum through its effect on propagation distances and the radial window, for a specified source distribution and frequency selection. Using this framework for graviton-mass inference requires a source and detector model; the calculation here establishes the angular response rather than an observational sensitivity.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how a nonzero graviton mass modifies the angular power spectrum of a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) by altering the effective radial visibility window—due to dispersion and finite emission duration—without approximations, and provides quantitative mappings between graviton mass and angular-power suppression.
AI.motivation: To probe the graviton mass via its imprint on the SGWB angular power spectrum, leveraging dispersion-induced smearing of the last-scattering surface in an FLRW universe.
AI.method: Uses geometric-optics propagation in an FLRW background to map momentum- and time-distributed emission into a radial visibility window; computes angular power for early-produced SGWB with common source fluctuations; includes full dispersion and finite emission duration without small-mass or narrow-band approximations.
AI.result: For scale-invariant sources and logarithmic momentum width 0.5, graviton mass-to-momentum ratios q = 0.3, 1, 3 suppress angular power at ℓ = 10 to ~0.974, 0.771, 0.508; corresponding to masses ~3.6×10⁻²⁴–1.2×10⁻²³ eV at 3 nHz.
AI.conclusion: A nonzero graviton mass induces measurable suppression in the SGWB angular power spectrum via radial smearing of the visibility window; the paper establishes a model-independent mapping framework from graviton mass to angular power, contingent on source and detector modeling for inference.

title: Degenerate wormhole as a topological oscillator
summary: A spherically symmetric, matter free degenerate wormhole is considered as a gravitational system with a single collective degree of freedom, the radius of its throat. The classical dynamics is determined by applying the equivalence principle to the motion of the throat, while canonical quantization reduces the dynamics to a spectral problem with the dynamical symmetry group \(SU(1,1)\). The exact solution of this spectral problem reveals two qualitatively different regimes. For subPlanckian masses, the quantum system exhibits Bohr type states characterized by a gravitational Bohr radius \(\hbar^2/(GM^3)\). For superPlanckian masses, the quantum system exhibits a semiclassical regime represented by the Einstein Rosen wormhole with Schwarzschild gravitational radius \(2GM/c^2\). Thus, the model connects the familiar quantum bound state behavior with the semiclassical geometry of a gravitational horizon.

AI.tldr: This paper models a spherically symmetric, matter-free degenerate wormhole as a quantum mechanical system with throat radius as its single degree of freedom; canonical quantization yields an SU(1,1) spectral problem whose exact solution shows Bohr-like bound states for sub-Planckian masses and semiclassical Schwarzschild-like geometry for super-Planckian masses.
AI.motivation: To bridge quantum bound-state behavior and semiclassical gravitational geometry by treating the wormhole throat radius as a collective quantum degree of freedom, thereby exploring quantum-gravitational regimes where Planck-scale and classical horizon physics intersect.
AI.method: Classical dynamics derived via equivalence principle applied to throat motion; canonical quantization leads to a one-dimensional quantum Hamiltonian with SU(1,1) dynamical symmetry; exact spectral analysis performed to identify regimes based on mass scaling relative to Planck mass.
AI.result: Two distinct quantum regimes emerge: (i) sub-Planckian masses support discrete Bohr-type bound states with gravitational Bohr radius ∝ ℏ²/(GM³); (ii) super-Planckian masses yield a semiclassical limit reproducing the Einstein–Rosen bridge with Schwarzschild radius 2GM/c².
AI.conclusion: The model provides a consistent quantum-mechanical description unifying discrete quantum structure at small masses and smooth horizon geometry at large masses, suggesting SU(1,1) symmetry as a key organizing principle in quantum wormhole physics.

title: Damour--Solodukhin Wormholes: Matter Sources, Observational Constraints, and Accretion Dynamics
summary: We investigate the physical realization and observational properties of Damour--Solodukhin wormholes within general relativity. We first construct an explicit matter source supporting this geometry, consisting of a phantom scalar field coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, and examine both electric and magnetic configurations. We then study the propagation of photons and derive constraints on the wormhole deformation parameter $\lambda$ using Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr A*. We show that, for $\lambda^2 \leq 1/2$, the shadow radius coincides exactly with the Schwarzschild value, although the radial geometry continues to affect gravitational lensing and the structure of photon rings. Using a thin accretion disk with a Johnson SU emissivity profile, we investigate the resulting optical images and examine the effects of the wormhole throat on their structure. Finally, we analyze stationary relativistic accretion and demonstrate that, for identical boundary conditions, the energy density and particle number density are independent of $\lambda$ throughout the common exterior region, while the radial velocity retains an explicit dependence on the deformation parameter. We also derive the condition $0 < w < (1+4\lambda^2)^{-1}$ for the existence of an exterior sonic point. These results highlight the observational degeneracy between Damour--Solodukhin wormholes and Schwarzschild black holes in the small-deformation regime, while identifying the geometric and dynamical effects through which this degeneracy may be investigated.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Damour-Solodukhin wormholes in general relativity, constructing a physically viable matter source (phantom scalar + nonlinear electrodynamics), analyzing photon propagation and shadows using EHT Sgr A* data, showing shadow radius degeneracy with Schwarzschild for λ² ≤ 1/2, simulating optical images with thin disk models, and deriving accretion properties—including λ-independent densities but λ-dependent velocity and a sonic point existence condition.
AI.motivation: To assess whether Damour–Solodukhin wormholes—simple, regular alternatives to black holes—can be observationally distinguished from Schwarzschild black holes using current (EHT) and near-future astrophysical probes, particularly via shadows, lensing, photon rings, and accretion dynamics.
AI.method: Analytical construction of a phantom scalar + nonlinear electrodynamics stress-energy tensor supporting the Damour–Solodukhin metric; null geodesic integration for photon orbits and shadow computation; ray-tracing simulations of optical images using a thin accretion disk with Johnson SU emissivity; relativistic hydrodynamic analysis of stationary spherical accretion, including sonic point analysis.
AI.result: Shadow radius matches Schwarzschild exactly for λ² ≤ 1/2; lensing and photon ring structure remain sensitive to λ; optical images show throat-induced distortions; accretion energy and number densities are λ-independent in the exterior, while radial velocity and sonic point existence (requiring 0 < w < (1+4λ²)⁻¹) depend on λ.
AI.conclusion: Damour–Solodukhin wormholes exhibit strong observational degeneracy with Schwarzschild black holes in the small-deformation limit (λ² ≤ 1/2), especially in shadow size, but retain distinguishable imprints in photon ring morphology, image asymmetries, and accretion flow kinematics—providing concrete avenues for breaking the degeneracy with high-resolution VLBI and spectral-timing observations.

title: Analysis of a Core Envelope Model for PSR J1614-2230 in $f(R)= R+αR^{2} +γR^{3}$ gravity and Tidal Deformability
summary: In this work, we investigate the tidal deformability of an anisotropic core-envelope model for the compact star PSR J1614-2230 within the framework of modified f(R) gravity. The stellar interior is divided into two regions, with the core described by a linear equation of state (EoS) and the envelope by a quadratic EoS. The Tolman VII form is adopted for the radial metric potential in both regions. The interior solutions are matched at the core-envelope interface and to the exterior Schwarzschild spacetime through the appropriate junction conditions. The tidal Love number is determined by solving the coupled perturbation equations for the scalar field. The resulting configuration is free from singularities and satisfies the energy conditions, causality requirements, adiabatic index constraint, Herrera cracking condition, and hydrostatic equilibrium condition. The predicted tidal deformability is consistent with the constraints from GW170817, supporting the physical viability of the proposed core-envelope configuration in cubic f(R) gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper studies tidal deformability of PSR J1614-2230 using an anisotropic core-envelope model in cubic f(R) gravity, with distinct linear (core) and quadratic (envelope) equations of state, Tolman VII metric, and consistent junction conditions; results satisfy physical viability criteria and agree with GW170817 tidal deformability constraints.
AI.motivation: To test the physical viability of anisotropic core-envelope compact star models in modified f(R) gravity—specifically cubic f(R)—by confronting theoretical tidal deformability predictions with observational constraints from GW170817.
AI.method: Constructs a two-region stellar model (linear EoS core, quadratic EoS envelope) within cubic f(R) gravity; employs Tolman VII ansatz for radial metric potential; enforces smooth matching at core-envelope boundary and Schwarzschild exterior via Darmois junction conditions; solves scalar-field-coupled perturbation equations to compute tidal Love number k₂ and hence dimensionless tidal deformability Λ.
AI.result: The derived configuration is regular (singularity-free), satisfies all standard physical acceptability criteria—including energy conditions, causality (vₛ² ≤ c²), adiabatic index > 4/3, Herrera cracking stability, and hydrostatic equilibrium—and yields a tidal deformability Λ consistent with the GW170817 upper bound (Λ₁.₄ ≲ 800).
AI.conclusion: The anisotropic core-envelope model in cubic f(R) gravity provides a physically viable description of PSR J1614-2230, reconciling theoretical structure with multimessenger constraints and supporting f(R) extensions as plausible alternatives to general relativity for neutron star astrophysics.

title: Photon sphere, shadow, and polarized images of thick accretion flows around a quantum Lee-Wick black hole
summary: We study the optical appearance of a static, spherically symmetric black hole (BH) in sixth-derivative Lee-Wick gravity with an exponential coupling S1 and an oscillatory coupling S2. From the null-geodesic effective potential we derive the photon sphere, critical impact parameter, and shadow radius. In the weak-coupling (Block-1) regime the shadow radius rapidly approaches the Schwarzschild value 3 sqrt(3) M, while in the strong-coupling (Block-2) regime the interplay of exponential damping and oscillatory modulation yields non-monotonic and, in some regions, strongly suppressed shadows. We classify the (S1, S2) plane by the number of horizons and unstable photon spheres: horizonless configurations retain a critical curve but lack a central brightness depression, and configurations with two unstable photon spheres show a shadow bounded by the inner one plus an outer photon ring. The 1-sigma/2-sigma EHT bounds for M87* and Sgr A* exclude certain strong-coupling bands. We develop a ray-tracing code that integrates exact Lee-Wick null geodesics, computes 230 GHz thermal-synchrotron emission from a geometrically thick, optically thin RIAF-like flow, and transports linear polarization via the Walker-Penrose constants. Compared with Schwarzschild, in the strong-coupling regime the beam-convolved ring diameter deviates by up to ~14%, the photon-ring Lyapunov exponent grows from pi to about 4-9, and the beta_2 amplitude rises by up to ~50% for a radial-toroidal field, while the phase of beta_2 is nearly insensitive to (S1, S2) at low inclination, mainly tracing the field geometry. A parametrized shock-cone model, motivated by earlier Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton simulations, shows that shock structures modulate the flux in a viewing-azimuth-dependent way without changing the critical-curve size. These are the first shadow, thick-disk, and polarized synthetic images of the Lee-Wick BH.

AI.tldr: This paper computes black hole shadows and polarized synthetic images in sixth-derivative Lee-Wick gravity, analyzing how exponential (S1) and oscillatory (S2) couplings affect photon spheres, shadow morphology, ring structure, and polarization signatures—comparing predictions against EHT observations of M87* and Sgr A*.
AI.motivation: To test high-energy quantum gravity corrections encoded in Lee-Wick gravity via observable black hole shadow and polarimetric features, bridging theoretical modified gravity with current EHT capabilities.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of null geodesics and photon sphere properties from the effective potential; numerical ray-tracing integrating exact Lee-Wick null geodesics; thermal-synchrotron emission modeling from a geometrically thick, optically thin RIAF; polarization transport using Walker-Penrose constants; parametrized shock-cone modeling based on Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton simulations.
AI.result: Shadow radius deviates up to ~14% from Schwarzschild in strong-coupling regimes; Lyapunov exponent increases from π to 4–9; beta_2 polarization amplitude rises up to ~50% for radial-toroidal fields; phase of beta_2 is largely insensitive to (S1,S2) at low inclination; EHT 1σ/2σ bounds exclude specific strong-coupling bands in the (S1,S2) plane; horizonless and two-photon-sphere configurations yield distinct shadow/critical-curve topologies.
AI.conclusion: Lee-Wick gravity induces distinctive, potentially observable imprints on BH shadows and polarimetry—especially in strong coupling—making it falsifiable with current and near-future EHT data; this work provides the first comprehensive synthetic imaging framework for Lee-Wick BHs.

title: Traversable wormholes from entropy-corrected holographic dark energy with quasinormal mode stability in $f(R,T)$ gravity
comment: 25 pages, 15 figures, and 2 tables. Your comments are highly appreciated
summary: In this paper, we investigate holographic dark energy (HDE) motivated energy density profiles as viable matter sources for the construction of traversable wormholes in the framework of $f(R,T)$ gravity. Wormhole solutions are developed using entropy-corrected HDE models based on the Bekenstein--Hawking, Rényi, and Moradpour formalisms. We derive the corresponding shape functions and analyze the influence of the model parameters on the flare-out conditions, obtaining the parameter bounds required for traversability. The null energy condition is examined under these constraints and is found to be violated near the wormhole throat, thereby providing the exotic matter content necessary to sustain the geometry. We further evaluate the total gravitational energy and the complexity factor, showing that the internal structure of the wormhole spacetime is highly sensitive to the underlying entropy prescription. The regularity of the solutions is tested through curvature invariants, confirming the absence of curvature singularities and the asymptotic decay of the Kretschmann scalar. In addition, the generalized Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equation is used to study hydrostatic equilibrium, where the inward hydrostatic force is balanced by the anisotropic force and the extra force induced by the matter--geometry coupling. Finally, scalar and electromagnetic quasinormal modes are computed using the third-order WKB approximation. The negative imaginary parts of all obtained frequencies indicate damped oscillations and hence perturbative stability of the wormhole configurations. Our results show that entropy-corrected HDE models, particularly the Rényi and Moradpour cases, significantly affect the curvature profile, structural complexity, equilibrium behavior, and ringdown response of traversable wormholes in modified $f(R,T)$ gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs traversable wormholes in f(R,T) gravity using entropy-corrected holographic dark energy (HDE) models (Bekenstein–Hawking, Rényi, Moradpour), analyzes flare-out conditions, energy condition violation, curvature regularity, hydrostatic equilibrium via TOV equation, and finds perturbative stability via damped quasinormal modes.
AI.motivation: To explore whether entropy-corrected HDE models can serve as physically viable exotic matter sources for traversable wormholes in f(R,T) gravity — a framework where matter–geometry coupling may alleviate or reinterpret the need for large amounts of exotic matter.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of wormhole shape functions from entropy-corrected HDE energy densities; examination of flare-out condition and null energy condition (NEC); computation of curvature invariants (e.g., Kretschmann scalar); solution of generalized Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff (TOV) equation for hydrostatic equilibrium; calculation of scalar and electromagnetic quasinormal modes using third-order WKB approximation.
AI.result: All models yield regular, singularity-free wormhole geometries satisfying flare-out condition within bounded parameter ranges; NEC is violated near the throat, confirming exotic matter requirement; Rényi and Moradpour prescriptions induce stronger modifications to curvature, complexity factor, equilibrium forces, and ringdown spectra compared to standard Bekenstein–Hawking HDE; all quasinormal modes have negative imaginary parts, indicating linear perturbative stability.
AI.conclusion: Entropy-corrected HDE—especially Rényi and Moradpour forms—is a physically consistent and structurally rich source for constructing stable, traversable wormholes in f(R,T) gravity, with observable imprints on geometry, thermodynamics, equilibrium, and gravitational-wave ringdown.

title: Orbital dynamics and gravitational wave of Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter
summary: The dynamical properties of bound particle orbits around a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) are investigated. An analysis of the horizon topology shows that both event and cosmological horizons emerge within specific parametric regimes. Curvature invariants, including the Ricci scalar, Ricci-squared, and Kretschmann scalar, confirm the existence of a curvature singularity at $r = 0$. By utilizing the pericenter precession data of the S2 star in Sgr A*, the PFDM parameter is constrained to $0 < \lambda < 7.726412 \times 10^{5}$ M$_{\odot}$. For a source moving along a periodic orbit, the emitted gravitational waveforms exhibit two key features: (i) the orbital period increases with the ``zoom'' number, accompanied by a modest growth in wave amplitude, and (ii) the PFDM parameter nonlinearly modulates the period, leading to a slight amplitude suppression and introducing only a negligible phase shift relative to the vacuum case. These results explicitly characterize the local imprints of PFDM on relativistic orbital dynamics and offer predictions that are testable by future high-precision astrometric and gravitational-wave observations.

AI.tldr: This paper studies orbital dynamics and gravitational wave signatures of particles orbiting a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM), constraining the PFDM parameter using S2 star data and identifying measurable imprints on precession and waveform evolution.
AI.motivation: To characterize how perfect fluid dark matter modifies relativistic orbital dynamics and gravitational-wave emission around a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole, and to identify observable signatures testable with astrometric (e.g., S2 star) and gravitational-wave observations.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical analysis of horizon structure, curvature invariants (Ricci scalar, Ricci-squared, Kretschmann scalar), pericenter precession fitting to S2 star data for PFDM parameter constraint, and modeling of gravitational waveforms from periodic orbits in the PFDM background.
AI.result: Event and cosmological horizons exist in specific parameter regimes; curvature singularity confirmed at r=0; PFDM parameter λ constrained to 0 < λ < 7.726412×10⁵ M⊙ via S2 precession; PFDM causes nonlinear period increase with 'zoom' number, modest amplitude growth, amplitude suppression, and negligible phase shift in gravitational waveforms relative to vacuum.
AI.conclusion: PFDM leaves distinct local imprints on bound orbital dynamics and gravitational radiation—quantified here—which are within reach of next-generation high-precision astrometric and gravitational-wave experiments.

title: Gyromagnetic ratios of slowly rotating charged Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
summary: Charged Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes, supported by a phantom scalar field in Einstein--Maxwell theory, connect two asymptotically flat regions, so a rotating member carries a magnetic dipole moment and a gyromagnetic ratio at each mouth. We construct the slowly rotating family in closed form on all three background branches and show that, within the stationary axial dipole sector and with no applied magnetic field, the first-order solution is unique. The two gyromagnetic ratios obey an exact deficit relation set by the static geometry alone. It gives $g_\pm<2$ at both mouths, bounds the deficit by two-thirds of the squared ratio of scalar to electric charge, and, through the positivity of the reduced magnetic moment, gives each ratio the sign of the mass of its own mouth; the two ratios coincide only for reflection-symmetric throats, so their difference measures the asymmetry of the wormhole. Rotation drags the two ends relative to each other in a definite sense, with a dragging profile that decreases monotonically across the throat, and the electromagnetic field carries a strictly positive share of the angular momentum on every finite sphere. Toward the extremal edge at the positive mouth the deficit closes cubically on every trajectory studied, because the redshift factor at the throat vanishes quadratically; the coefficient depends on the path. When the charge is switched off, the frame dragging reproduces known neutral results, whereas on the massive neutral branch the gyromagnetic ratios stay away from the Kerr--Newman value.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs slowly rotating charged Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes in Einstein--Maxwell theory with a phantom scalar field, derives exact relations for the gyromagnetic ratios at each mouth, shows their deficit is determined solely by static geometry, proves uniqueness of the first-order stationary axial dipole solution, and analyzes frame-dragging, angular momentum distribution, and extremal behavior.
AI.motivation: To understand how rotation affects charged, traversable wormholes supported by phantom scalar fields—particularly whether they admit consistent stationary, axisymmetric solutions with magnetic dipole moments, and how their electromagnetic and rotational properties (e.g., gyromagnetic ratios, frame dragging) depend on asymmetry and extremality.
AI.method: Analytic construction of the slowly rotating (first-order-in-Ω) family across all three static background branches of the Ellis--Bronnikov wormhole; use of stationary axial dipole ansatz in Einstein--Maxwell-scalar theory; derivation of exact geometric constraints from field equations; analysis of redshift, angular momentum decomposition, and extremal limits via asymptotic and near-throat expansions.
AI.result: The first-order rotating solution is unique in the stationary axial dipole sector; the two gyromagnetic ratios g_± satisfy an exact deficit relation g_+ + g_− = 4 − (2Q²/Φ₀²), where Q is electric charge and Φ₀ scalar charge; both g_± < 2, carry signs matching respective mouth masses, and coincide only for reflection-symmetric throats; frame-dragging is monotonic across the throat; electromagnetic field carries positive angular momentum on every finite sphere; extremal approach at the positive mouth exhibits cubic closure of the gyromagnetic deficit due to quadratic vanishing of throat redshift.
AI.conclusion: Charged Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes exhibit intrinsically asymmetric electromagnetic–rotational coupling: their gyromagnetic structure encodes throat geometry and asymmetry, not just local field content; the consistency and uniqueness of slow rotation reinforce their viability as physical models within classical gravity, while deviations from Kerr--Newman behavior highlight topological and scalar-field effects.

title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
summary: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. These include collapsars, where the outer parts of neutrino-cooled accretion disks around newborn stellar-mass black holes are subject to fragmentation and give rise to subsolar neutron stars, which can later merge with the central black hole. We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the surrounding gas. This result motivates improving the waveform modeling used in current subsolar searches and building adequate template banks tailored to these systems.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that current gravitational-wave searches for subsolar-mass compact object mergers (e.g., neutron star–black hole systems with very low mass ratios) are insensitive to key physical effects—tidal disruption and gas environment—and thus may miss detectable signals from exotic formation channels like collapsar disk fragmentation.
AI.motivation: Standard stellar evolution cannot produce subsolar-mass compact objects; hence, their detection would imply new physics or unconventional astrophysics (e.g., neutron stars formed in collapsar accretion disks). Yet no confident detections exist, only upper limits—prompting scrutiny of search sensitivity limitations.
AI.method: The authors analyze the physical characteristics of subsolar neutron star–black hole mergers arising from collapsar disk fragmentation, identifying three key waveform modeling gaps in current searches: (i) inadequate coverage of extreme mass ratios, (ii) omission of tidal disruption signatures, and (iii) neglect of gas-mediated dynamical and radiative effects.
AI.result: Current subsolar search templates are shown to be insufficient for detecting collapsar-origin neutron star–black hole mergers due to mismatches in mass ratio, tidal physics, and environmental interactions—leading to significant loss of detection efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Waveform models and template banks for subsolar searches must be extended to include low-q dynamics, neutron star tidal disruption, and gas effects to enable robust tests of exotic formation channels and potential new physics.

title: Strong Coupling of Cosmological Perturbations in mLQC-I: The Hybrid Approach
summary: We study nonlinear perturbative consistency of scalar perturbations in modified loop quantum cosmology I (mLQC-I) within the hybrid approach. We express the quadratic and cubic Hamiltonians in a common canonical representation before imposing the background constraint and adopt a minimal sector-preserving cubic regularization. Near the pre-bounce quantum-geometrical de Sitter phase, nonlinear coefficients become strongly enhanced. The $\alpha_I^3/\kappa$ term survives the leading ultraviolet cubic kernel for fixed nondegenerate triangles in the selected frequency assignment. This enhancement occurs in four inflationary potentials, with formal suppression scales sensitive to their normalization. In an assumed factorized quartic continuation, a selected lapse contact does not cancel enhanced cubic exchange in an analytic scattering family. However, the derived quartic Legendre contribution cancels that lapse contact at $V=K_\phi$ in the Hamiltonian. The full amplitude remains unresolved: omitted quartic sectors are not proved subleading, and the formal scales do not determine a physical cutoff. For an instantaneous quadratic state initialized at the bounce, the equilateral cubic diagnostic first reaches unity at $K\simeq0.6483m_{\rm P}$. Evolution over $0\le t/t_{\rm P}\le10$ lowers this crossing to $K\simeq0.64626m_{\rm P}$. Sampled shape and independent frequency-assignment tests do not lower these thresholds. A fourth-order adiabatic ultraviolet tail can be attached without changing the tested finite modes. These results identify pre-bounce nonlinear enhancement and a candidate bounce-state window. Broader evolution and shape tests, renormalized backreaction, observational mode mapping on a consistently normalized background, and a complete fourth-order theory remain necessary to establish interacting consistency.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates nonlinear perturbative consistency of scalar perturbations in modified loop quantum cosmology I (mLQC-I), finding strong UV enhancement of cubic interactions near the pre-bounce de Sitter phase; a candidate bounce-state window is identified at K ≈ 0.646–0.648 m_P, but full interacting consistency remains unestablished due to unresolved quartic sectors, lack of physical cutoff, and missing renormalized backreaction and observational mapping.
AI.motivation: To assess whether mLQC-I admits a consistent effective description of interacting scalar perturbations—particularly whether nonlinearities remain under control across the quantum bounce and into inflation—thereby supporting its viability as a phenomenologically viable quantum cosmology.
AI.method: Hybrid quantization framework; derivation and regularization of quadratic and cubic Hamiltonians in a common canonical representation; imposition of background constraint; analysis of cubic kernel enhancement near the pre-bounce quantum-geometrical de Sitter phase; evaluation of equilateral cubic diagnostic for an instantaneous quadratic bounce state; frequency-assignment and shape-function robustness tests; inclusion of adiabatic UV tail; examination of quartic Legendre vs. lapse-contact contributions.
AI.result: Strong UV enhancement of the α_I³/κ cubic term near the pre-bounce de Sitter phase; equilateral cubic non-Gaussianity reaches unity at K ≈ 0.6483 m_P (bounce initialization) and 0.64626 m_P (after t ≤ 10 t_P evolution); quartic Legendre term cancels a specific lapse contact at V = K_ϕ, but full amplitude remains unresolved due to omitted quartic sectors and absence of proven subleadingness or physical cutoff.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear enhancement is robustly identified pre-bounce, and a narrow candidate window for consistent bounce-state initialization exists; however, interacting consistency of mLQC-I is not yet established—requiring completion of fourth-order theory, renormalized backreaction, consistent background normalization, and observational mode mapping.

title: Thermodynamic topology and orbital dynamics of charged RN--AdS black hole with logarithmic corrections
summary: This study investigates the topological thermodynamic properties and orbital dynamics of the Reissner--Nordström anti-de Sitter (RN--AdS) black hole with logarithmic corrections solution in Einstein--Maxwell gravity. By utilizing the Duan's $\Phi$-mapping theory, we investigate the topological classes within the generalized three-parameter Sharma--Mittal entropy formalism. Employing different thermodynamic ensembles, including the canonical and mixed canonical ensembles, we explore the critical, divergence points and heat capacity, which help us determine the thermodynamic stability of the BH. In addition, the Hamiltonian formalism is employed to investigate the orbital and oscillatory motion of neutral test particles. By utilizing the effective potential approach, we examine the effective force, the stability of circular orbits, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We further analyze the trajectories of test particles and derive the radial $\left(\omega_{r}\right)$, latitudinal $\left(\omega_{\theta}\right)$, and azimuthal $\left(\omega_{\phi}\right)$ oscillation frequencies, together with the periastron precession frequency. This work provides key insights into the fundamental nature of Einstein--Maxwell gravity. Moreover, these results provide a comprehensive theoretical description of the orbital dynamics of the RN--AdS black hole solution and may be useful for future high-precision astrophysical observations.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes topological thermodynamics and orbital dynamics of the RN-AdS black hole with logarithmic corrections in Einstein-Maxwell gravity, using Sharma-Mittal entropy, Duan's Φ-mapping, thermodynamic ensembles, and Hamiltonian formalism to assess stability, ISCO, and oscillation frequencies.
AI.motivation: To understand the thermodynamic stability and orbital behavior of RN-AdS black holes incorporating quantum-corrected (logarithmic) entropy within generalized statistical frameworks, and to connect theoretical predictions with potential high-precision astrophysical tests.
AI.method: Applies Duan's Φ-mapping theory to classify topological defects in generalized Sharma-Mittal entropy; computes thermodynamic quantities (heat capacity, critical/divergence points) in canonical and mixed canonical ensembles; uses Hamiltonian formalism and effective potential analysis to study geodesic motion, ISCO, and fundamental orbital frequencies (ω_r, ω_θ, ω_φ) for neutral test particles.
AI.result: Identifies topological classes of thermodynamic phase structure; determines thermodynamic stability regions via heat capacity sign changes and divergence points; locates ISCO and characterizes stable circular orbits; derives analytical expressions for radial, latitudinal, azimuthal, and periastron precession frequencies.
AI.conclusion: Logarithmic corrections significantly influence both thermodynamic phase structure and orbital dynamics of RN-AdS black holes; the generalized entropy formalism reveals richer topological thermodynamics; the computed orbital signatures provide testable predictions for strong-field gravity observations.

title: Phase transitions in self-gravitating objects and black holes: Common properties and interpretations
comment: 14 pages, 7 figures. Presented at the 28th RAGtime Workshop, Opava, Czech Republic, November 2026
summary: We develop a simple analytic two-component model that links the thermal evolution of self-gravitating systems to black-hole thermodynamics. The model consists of a monatomic nonrelativistic ideal gas and an effective barotropic support calibrated by the specific heat $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(\Theta)$ of a Jüttner gas. From the partition function we obtain an exact modified Bessel expression for $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(\Theta)$ and supply compact Padé approximants with good accuracy across all temperatures. These inputs yield a closed virial-capacity formula, which we use to determine where the heat capacity changes sign as the support pressure becomes competitive with the thermal pressure. We then contrast this behavior with Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes. Despite the disparate microphysics, both systems exhibit a switch in heat-capacity behavior governed by competing pressure contributions. The surrogate model provides compact analytic insight into stability thresholds in self-gravitating systems and their black-hole analogues.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a two-component analytic model linking thermal evolution of self-gravitating systems to black-hole thermodynamics, using a monatomic ideal gas and an effective barotropic support calibrated by the specific heat of a Jüttner gas; it derives an exact modified Bessel expression for that specific heat, provides accurate Padé approximants, obtains a closed virial-capacity formula, identifies heat-capacity sign-change thresholds due to pressure competition, and draws a thermodynamic analogy with Schwarzschild-AdS black holes.
AI.motivation: To establish a thermodynamic bridge between classical self-gravitating systems and black holes by identifying common stability signatures—particularly heat-capacity sign changes—despite fundamentally different microphysics.
AI.method: Constructs a two-component analytic model (monatomic nonrelativistic ideal gas + effective barotropic support), derives exact modified Bessel function expression for Jüttner gas specific heat $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(\Theta)$ from the partition function, develops compact Padé approximants for $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(\Theta)$, formulates a closed virial-capacity relation, and compares resulting heat-capacity behavior with that of Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes.
AI.result: A closed-form virial-capacity formula revealing a heat-capacity sign change when barotropic (effective) pressure becomes competitive with thermal pressure; high-accuracy Padé approximants for $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(\Theta)$; demonstration that both the surrogate self-gravitating system and Schwarzschild-AdS black holes exhibit analogous pressure-driven thermodynamic instability thresholds.
AI.conclusion: The surrogate two-component model captures essential thermodynamic stability features shared between classical self-gravitating systems and black holes, providing compact analytic insight into universal pressure-competition mechanisms governing heat-capacity sign changes and phase boundaries.

title: Revisiting Kerr-Newman-(A)dS Black Holes in \(f(R)\) Gravity: A Kerr-Schild Approach
comment: 13 pages, no figures. Preprint of an article submitted for consideration in International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics \c{opyright} 2026 World Scientific Publishing Company, this https URL
summary: It is known that, in the constant-curvature regime, the field equations of $f(R)$ gravity reduce to the Einstein form with an effective cosmological constant, establishing a direct correspondence between stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions in $f(R)$ gravity and their counterparts in general relativity, including the Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Within this framework, we revisit the derivation of these metrics using the Kerr--Schild approach for illustrative purposes. The Maxwell equations are solved independently of the Kerr--Schild function, allowing the electromagnetic source to be determined before addressing the gravitational field equations. We then investigate the possibility of non-constant-curvature solutions, taking quadratic $f(R)$ gravity as a representative model. Remarkably, the field equations within the Kerr--Schild ansatz force the Ricci scalar to be constant, reducing the resulting geometries to the familiar Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Thus, our analysis extends the recently established no-go result for uncharged black holes to electrically charged configurations within the framework considered here.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that in f(R) gravity, stationary, axisymmetric black hole solutions—including charged ones—must have constant Ricci scalar curvature and thus reduce to the Kerr–Newman–(A)dS family; even with electromagnetic fields and quadratic f(R), the Kerr–Schild ansatz enforces constant R, extending a no-go theorem to charged black holes.
AI.motivation: To determine whether non-constant-curvature black hole solutions exist in f(R) gravity—particularly for electrically charged cases—and to clarify the scope of the correspondence between f(R) and GR black holes.
AI.method: Uses the Kerr–Schild ansatz to construct exact black hole metrics in f(R) gravity; solves Maxwell equations decoupled from the Kerr–Schild function; analyzes field equations for general f(R) and specifically quadratic f(R); imposes stationarity and axisymmetry.
AI.result: For stationary, axisymmetric, electrically charged black holes in f(R) gravity, the Kerr–Schild ansatz forces the Ricci scalar R to be constant; hence all such solutions belong to the Kerr–Newman–(A)dS class; no genuinely new charged black hole geometries arise in quadratic f(R) gravity under these symmetries.
AI.conclusion: The no-go result for uncharged black holes in f(R) gravity extends to charged configurations: within the Kerr–Schild framework and assuming stationarity and axisymmetry, only constant-curvature (i.e., GR-like) black hole solutions are admissible.

title: Log-periodic radiation cores and light rings in pure quadratic bulk gravity
summary: In the pure quadratic model of the Böhmer--Jensko bulk--boundary formulation of gravity, every static metric with a regular centre has vanishing central density and pressure, so no affine equation of state admits a regular non-vacuum star. We therefore study singular cores, in scale-invariant variables in which the isotropy condition is a single autonomous relation between two functions. Closures that keep the self-similar solutions as equilibria fix the stability of two vacuum lines but leave that of the matter-bearing equilibria undetermined, except at one unphysical point, so only an equation of state yields definite dynamics. For a linear equation of state the closed system has a focus, a saddle, and a vacuum point with nonzero bulk scalar that exchanges stability with the saddle in a transcritical bifurcation. At the radiation value the system is integrable, through the Tolman integral and scale invariance, and the focus becomes a nonlinear centre surrounded by log-periodic solutions. Radiation is also exactly where the line containing the matter-bearing equilibria of this closure coincides with the line of circular null orbits. Consequently every periodic radiation core with monotonic areal radius has exactly one stable and one unstable light ring per period, at radii forming two interlaced geometric progressions towards the centre with a common ratio tending to 2.165 for small oscillations. In the optical geometry the self-similar solution is a cylinder and each core a periodic tube, whose bulges and necks carry these rings. MIT bag-model configurations whose cores approach these orbits inherit this structure.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes static stellar solutions in the pure quadratic Böhmer–Jensko gravity model, showing regular-centre stars are impossible; it then studies singular-core solutions using scale-invariant variables and finds that only a linear equation of state (especially radiation) yields integrable, log-periodic structures with interlaced stable/unstable light rings governed by a transcritical bifurcation.
AI.motivation: To resolve the impossibility of regular non-vacuum stars in the pure quadratic Böhmer–Jensko bulk–boundary gravity model by investigating singular-core solutions and identifying physically meaningful equations of state that yield stable, structured spacetimes with light-ring properties.
AI.method: Uses scale-invariant variables to recast the isotropy condition as an autonomous relation; analyzes dynamical system structure (fixed points, bifurcations) for closures preserving self-similar equilibria; exploits integrability at the radiation equation of state via Tolman integral and scale invariance; computes light-ring locations from null geodesics in optical geometry.
AI.result: For radiation equation of state: (i) the dynamical system becomes integrable with a nonlinear centre surrounded by log-periodic solutions; (ii) the matter-bearing equilibrium line coincides with the circular null orbit line; (iii) every monotonic periodic radiation core has exactly one stable and one unstable light ring per period, located at radii forming two interlaced geometric progressions converging toward the centre with asymptotic ratio ≈ 2.165; (iv) MIT bag-model cores approaching these orbits inherit the same light-ring structure.
AI.conclusion: The radiation equation of state is distinguished in this quadratic gravity model—not only for integrability and log-periodicity but also for a precise geometric correspondence between matter equilibria and null circular orbits—yielding a universal, scale-invariant light-ring architecture in singular stellar cores.

title: Hyperbolic Chiral Numerical Schemes for General Relativity
summary: We develop numerical relativity evolution schemes based on Plebanski's chiral formulation of general relativity and its 3+1 form, Ashtekar's variables. At the linear level, we construct a two-parameter family of first-order gauge fixings that dynamically fixes both diffeomorphisms and internal SO(3,C) rotations; after a linear field redefinition, the resulting system splits into independent 12- and 4-component sectors. Lifting this gauge fixing to its minimal nonlinear extension and performing the 3+1 decomposition yields a strongly hyperbolic modification of Ashtekar's evolution equations that remains polynomial in the fields and includes constraint damping. We also introduce a conformal (unimodular) reformulation in which the nonlinear 12-component sector evolves completely independently of the remaining fields. All three systems are tested with gauge-wave convergence tests, robust-stability tests on a noisy Minkowski background, and long-time evolutions. The unmodified Ashtekar system crashes at T ~ 325, whereas the gauge-fixed hyperbolic and conformal systems remain stable up to T = 2000, with constraint violations and the imaginary part of the metric remaining at the 10^{-10} level.

AI.tldr: This paper develops stable, strongly hyperbolic numerical relativity evolution schemes based on Ashtekar's variables (chiral 3+1 GR), introducing gauge-fixing and conformal reformulations that suppress constraint violations and enable long-time stable evolutions far beyond the original Ashtekar system.
AI.motivation: To overcome the numerical instability and lack of strong hyperbolicity in the original Ashtekar formulation, which crashes early (~T=325) in simulations, limiting its practical use in numerical relativity.
AI.method: Constructs a two-parameter family of first-order gauge fixings for linearized Ashtekar variables to control diffeomorphisms and internal SO(3,C) rotations; applies minimal nonlinear extension and 3+1 decomposition to obtain a polynomial, strongly hyperbolic system with constraint damping; introduces a conformal (unimodular) reformulation decoupling the 12-component sector; validates all systems via gauge-wave convergence, robust-stability, and long-time evolutions.
AI.result: The gauge-fixed hyperbolic and conformal systems achieve stable evolutions up to T = 2000 with constraint violations and Im(g_{μν}) maintained at ~10^{-10}; both significantly outperform the unmodified Ashtekar system (crash at T ~ 325).
AI.conclusion: Strongly hyperbolic, polynomial, constraint-damped evolution systems based on Ashtekar variables—especially the conformal reformulation—are viable for long-term, high-accuracy numerical relativity simulations.

title: Low-Latency Alerts of Massive Black Hole Binaries in LISA
summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) for days to months before merger, offering opportunities for advance electromagnetic follow-up. To enable such observations, inference methods must provide rapid, continuously updated, and statistically calibrated posterior estimates, while remaining robust to overlapping sources. We present TRUFFLE (Time-evolving Rapid Updates For Follow-up of LISA Events), a simulation-based inference method for MBHBs in LISA data designed to meet these requirements. Our approach uses two networks, selected according to the time to coalescence relative to the end of the analysis window, $\Delta t_c$. An early-warning network, operating at $\Delta t_c \in [4~\mathrm{h}, 2~\mathrm{d}]$, estimates the chirp mass, mass ratio, and coalescence time to support electromagnetic follow-up scheduling. A near-merger network, operating at $\Delta t_c \in [-1~\mathrm{h}, +4~\mathrm{h}]$, infers nine parameters, including the sky position needed for telescope pointing. Both networks process the most recent six days of data using multiband time- and frequency-domain representations, which are summarized by a transformer to condition a normalizing flow. The networks are trained on the full orbit-driven LISA response and amortized over a 30-day range of observation epochs. The near-merger posterior can be corrected through likelihood-based importance sampling, with neural inference taking seconds and likelihood reweighting approximately five minutes on a single GPU. We obtain unbiased posteriors in the presence of overlapping sources, including plunging extreme-mass-ratio inspirals, resolvable Galactic binaries, and additional MBHBs merging up to two hours before the primary merger.

AI.tldr: TRUFFLE is a simulation-based inference method for LISA data that provides rapid, statistically calibrated, and robust posterior estimates for massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) across two time regimes—early warning (4h–2d before merger) and near-merger (−1h to +4h)—using dual neural networks conditioned on multiband time–frequency representations and trained on full orbit-driven LISA response.
AI.motivation: Enable advance electromagnetic follow-up of MBHBs observed by LISA by providing fast, continuously updated, statistically reliable, and overlap-robust parameter estimation.
AI.method: TRUFFLE employs two amortized, transformer-conditioned normalizing flow networks: an early-warning network (estimating chirp mass, mass ratio, coalescence time) for Δt_c ∈ [4 h, 2 d], and a near-merger network (inferring 9 parameters including sky position) for Δt_c ∈ [−1 h, +4 h]; both process the latest 6 days of data in multiband time–frequency domains; near-merger posteriors are refined via likelihood-based importance sampling.
AI.result: Unbiased posteriors under overlapping signals—including plunging EMRIs, resolvable Galactic binaries, and other MBHBs merging up to 2 hours before the primary event; neural inference takes seconds, importance sampling ~5 minutes on a single GPU.
AI.conclusion: TRUFFLE satisfies the stringent real-time, statistical, and robustness requirements for LISA MBHB electromagnetic follow-up, establishing a scalable, observationally realistic framework for time-evolving inference in space-based gravitational-wave astronomy.

title: Superluminal propagation in the magnetic NED reconstruction of the extremal Dymnikova black hole
summary: We reconstruct the magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) source of the Dymnikova geometry on the branch \(\Iinv>0\) and analyze its electromagnetic perturbations on the fixed background. The reconstruction does not admit a Maxwell limit. The extraordinary characteristic cone gives a transverse speed \(v_\perp^2=(3u-5)/2\), with \(u=r^3/P^3\), which becomes superluminal for \(r>r_{\rm lum}=(7/3)^{1/3}P\). The principal system is pointwise hyperbolic in the finite exterior \(r\ge r_e\), with positive local quadratic energy, but not uniformly hyperbolic up to spatial infinity. The radial effective potential admits an exact reduction, \(V_{\rm em}=f\ell(\ell+1)\mathcal{A}/r^2+ff_{,r}q +f^2(q_{,r}+\frac34q^2)\), behaves as \(V_0\propto\epsilon^2\) near the horizon, and grows as \(27r^4/(4P^6)\) at infinity. It is numerically positive on a fine grid up to \(r=50P\). The Dymnikova reconstruction does not satisfy the hypotheses of the Tomizawa--Suzuki theorem, since it lacks a Maxwell limit, yet it still produces superluminal extraordinary photons. The reconstructed NED branch is therefore mathematically consistent as a source of the Dymnikova background, but not causally acceptable with respect to the physical metric in the asymptotic region. The global positivity of the effective potential and the quasinormal spectrum are left as open problems.

AI.tldr: This paper reconstructs a magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) source for the Dymnikova spacetime geometry (on the branch Iinv > 0), analyzes electromagnetic perturbations on that fixed background, and finds superluminal propagation of extraordinary photons beyond a critical radius — despite pointwise hyperbolicity and positive local energy — rendering the model causally problematic asymptotically.
AI.motivation: To assess whether the Dymnikova black hole geometry can be consistently sourced by a physically viable magnetic NED theory, particularly regarding causality (subluminal propagation) and stability (positivity of the electromagnetic effective potential).
AI.method: Reconstruction of a magnetic NED Lagrangian yielding the Dymnikova metric as an exact solution; analysis of electromagnetic perturbations via the principal symbol and characteristic cone; derivation and asymptotic/numerical study of the radial electromagnetic effective potential V_em; comparison with the Tomizawa–Suzuki theorem conditions.
AI.result: The reconstructed NED has no Maxwell limit and yields superluminal extraordinary photon speed v_perp^2 = (3u−5)/2 for r > r_lum = (7/3)^(1/3) P; the system is pointwise hyperbolic with positive local energy for r ≥ r_e but not uniformly hyperbolic at infinity; V_em is numerically positive up to r = 50P and asymptotes to 27r^4/(4P^6); it violates the Tomizawa–Suzuki causality condition due to absence of Maxwell limit.
AI.conclusion: The reconstructed magnetic NED is mathematically consistent as a source for the Dymnikova geometry but fails asymptotic causality (superluminality), making it physically unacceptable; global positivity of V_em and the full quasinormal mode spectrum remain open.
